## 2026-07-17 (round 233, build 260618.06) — CL-0037: CS/Audiovisual videos → Vimeo scaffold = **MEASURED DECLINE** + SGP capture (Chris — the CL0037 kickoff, ticket 8 of the CL0029-CL0052 triage; ZERO-blast output-inert round, the r229-CL-0030/r230/r231 class — no regen, ship ledger NOT incremented, 4 headroom unchanged)

**Plain English.** The design team's rule CL-0037 says: when a video is produced in-house
(a Te Kura / Audiovisual item), the page should ship the standard Vimeo player box with
the video ID left blank, plus a red "Designer/Developer To Do" note telling the developer
to drop the ID in when the video is ready. Before building it, this round measured the
one thing the ticket flagged: can the converter actually TELL, from the Writers Template
and Media List alone, that an item is an in-house **video** (rather than an in-house
audio recording, animation, or interactive)? The answer is no — and the honest outcome,
which the ticket itself pre-authorised, is a recorded decline. The writers' `[Audiovisual
item N]` markers are real and plentiful (160 of them across 13 modules), but they mean
"CS-produced media of ANY kind", and in today's library they are mostly AUDIO —
pronunciation sounds, mp3 voice-overs, a boy's voice reading a passage. Nothing in any
Writers Template or Media List says which kind an item is, not one of those 13 modules'
human builds contains a Vimeo player, and the 201 human pages that DO contain Vimeo have
no marker at all. Shipping a Vimeo VIDEO box at these markers would put wrong players on
audio sites. So no code ships; instead the rule is captured in the Subject Global
Parameters (the CL-0030 pattern) so future audits never chase the human's Vimeo pages,
with the mechanism pre-named for the day the writers' templates start marking a CS video
explicitly. Nothing in the converter's output changed — proven byte-for-byte.

**THE RULE (CL-0037, 16 Jul — captured, not live).** A CS-produced (Te Kura in-house /
Audiovisual) VIDEO embeds the designer-supplied Vimeo `videoSection` scaffold with the ID
pending (`src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/"`), preceded by a red+bold
`Designer/Developer To Do: add vimeo embed for [audiovisual item x]` note; the trailing
`<!-- &amp;start=0 --> <!-- &amp;end=0 -->` placeholders are a permitted comment
exception. The ticket's own proviso: "the discriminator may be non-derivable from V2's
inputs; if so, record a measured decline."

**MEASURED (STEP 1, live parser — never the stale txts).**
- **The marker family** (`outputs/_detect_avitem.cjs`, ALL 431 WTs through the live
  extractor+TagNormaliser, 8-sharded; both channels — the first cut scanned RED spans
  only and used a case-sensitive black regex, each of which silently missed modules:
  BLL255/256's black forms, BLL257's capital-A `[Audiovisual item N]`, BLL254's
  `[Audiovisual request item 1]` variant): **160 occurrences / 13 modules** — BLL254,
  BLL255, BLL256, BLL257, BLL270–276, ENGJ403, SSOG105. Red-span forms resolve TODAY as
  `data marker` SUBTAGs (the `[Item N]` embedded alias — `outputs/_probe_r233_parse.cjs`);
  black/table-cell forms carry no tag at all; one LINK-nested form resolves
  `external link`.
- **The kind is NOT derivable.** The marker denotes CS media of ANY kind: context
  keywords classify AUDIO 8 / VIDEO 2 / UNKNOWN ~150, the keyword classifier itself
  misfires (a pronunciation drill "a (incorrectly spoken)" scored VIDEO), and gold's own
  choices at the UNKNOWN mass are audio-dominant. NO WT or Media List channel marks an
  item's kind. The Media List leads dissolved: "cs Video | Scratch Garden" rows are
  ordinary EXTERNAL YouTube rows (source column "you tube"); the 23 "Te Kura"-source ML
  rows corpus-wide are images/templates/links — **zero cs-video rows exist**.
- **Gold pairing is per-KIND, and never Vimeo.** ZERO of the 13 marker modules' golds
  ship `player.vimeo.com` (0 pages). BLL270's gold at its markers: red `Designer note:
  Animation to come` + an **EMPTY `videoSection icon ratio ratio-16x9`** (the pre-ledger

## 2026-07-17 (round 232, build 260618.05) — CL-0038: `[MTKquiz]` → THE "Go to quiz" BUTTON + Designer/Developer To Do note (Chris — the CL0038 kickoff, ticket 7 of the CL0029-CL0052 triage; the FIRST output-changing round since r229; SCOPED ship #4, 4 headroom left)

**Plain English.** Writers mark a D2L quiz with an "MTK quiz" note in a dozen different
spellings — `[MTKQuiz]`, `[MTK Quiz, supports engagement, audio, video, file sharing]`,
`[Insert MTK Quiz – trigger engagement]`, even a bare red line with no brackets. Until
now the converter treated each spelling differently and mostly wrongly: most became an
un-buildable quiz-widget placeholder that swallowed the writer's quiz questions into an
orange dump box, some became plain red notes, and two spellings mis-fired into a text
box or a drop-down. The design team's rule (Change Ledger CL-0038) says: every such
marker ends in the standard **"Go to quiz" button** — with an intentionally EMPTY link,
because the developer wires the real D2L quicklink at publish time — plus a visible
**"Designer/Developer To Do:"** note telling the developer to create the quiz in MTK.
That is what ships now, on every one of the 54 markers across 21 modules: one button +
one note per quiz, the writer's own quiz questions kept visible on the page (the
developer needs them to build the quiz), and where the writer had ALSO typed their own
"Go to quiz" button next to the marker, the two collapse into ONE button (the human's
form — never two buttons for one quiz). The off-switch restores the old output
byte-for-byte, and every quality gate held or improved.

**THE RULE (CL-0038, 16 Jul).** Any `[MTKquiz]` (any modifiers) ends in
`<a href="#" target="_blank"><div class="button">Go to quiz</div></a>` (blank href; dev
wires the D2L quicklink) + a visible `Designer/Developer To Do:` note to create the quiz
in MTK. Writer-supplied quiz content STAYS rendered (constraint 1); the `dropbox`
wrapper modifier does NOT attach. `[MTKquiz]` added to the tag taxonomy (`mtk_quiz`).

**MEASURED FIRST (STEP 1, live parser — never the stale txts).**
- **Population** (`outputs/_detect_mtkquiz.cjs`, ALL ~430 WTs incl. the parsed-txt-less
  bilingual dirs, 8-sharded for the 45s wall): **54 marker occurrences (33 distinct span
  forms) / 21 modules** + exactly ONE closer (`[End of MTK Quiz content]`, ARFUN01).
  19 modules tracked (have Claude dirs); **HPRE301 + SSCI104 untracked** — their fix is
  a FORWARD GUARANTEE (the r231 class).
- **Live resolutions were all over the map** (`outputs/_probe_r232_parse.cjs`, the
  r189/r191 probe-Parse-first lesson): most forms → `mcq` INTERACTIVE via the embedded
  "quiz" alias (un-built bundles that swallowed the writer's quiz content into cv2
  dumps); `[MTKQuiz]`/`[Auto-marked MTKquiz]`/`[MTKQuiz] 2F`/the ENG1004/ENG1005
  bracket-less red lines → bare instructions (Writers Notes); `[MTK quiz, Free text
  box…]` → a **text box ELEMENT** mis-route (TEFUN02 ×5); `[MTK Quiz – … teacher
  dropbox]` → a **dropdown** mis-route (EXBP901).
- **Gold pairing:** gold ships the exact button shape on 122 pages (populated D2L
  quickLink hrefs = the publish-time wiring itself, the CL-0044 class → the blank-href
  divergence is INTENTIONAL). At every measured site gold's button sits where the
  WRITER's own button marker sits — `[button] Go to quiz`/`Quiz` (ARFUN02/04,
  TEFUN02/06/07/08), a standalone `[Go to quiz]` span (HPRE301), or the MTK marker
  itself — so AT-TAG emission + writer-button absorption reproduces gold's placement.
  **FIVE modules have NO gold button** (SCFUN01, MXFUN02, SSOG103, SSOG301, EXPFUN07 —
  gold predates the rule): shipped anyway per CL-0038 = **named CHANGE-LEDGER OVERRIDE
  deltas**, captured, never chased.
- **Scope fence:** standalone `[go to quiz]`-family spans exist in **~40 modules**
  corpus-wide — far beyond the MTK family. They participate ONLY as button markers
  inside an MTK item's window; the corpus-wide standalone class is a RECORDED follow-up
  (CL-0004-adjacent), keeping this round's blast exactly the detector set.

**FIX (DATA OVER CODE; env `MTKQUIZ_OFF` reverts everything).**
- **Taxonomy + retag** (`Tag_Lexicon.json`): canonical **`mtk quiz`** entry (ELEMENT,
  deliberately ZERO aliases — natural alias matching is not env-gateable; the entry is
  the taxonomy record + directive lookup) + **`_meta.mtk_quiz_retag`** — a span-level
  Parse step (the r170 tag_promote class, but able to fire on tag-less instruction
  spans too): folded span carries the MTK-quiz head (`mtk[\s-]*quiz`) and is not the
  closer (`^\[?end\b` excluded) → the quiz-junk co-tags in `drop_tags`
  (mcq/engagement/question/text box/option/dropdown/video/audio — so `dropbox` never
  attaches) are removed and ONE `mtk quiz` ELEMENT injected; a bracket-less span must
  be ≤12 words (`bracketless_max_words` — a long prose note mentioning an MTK quiz can
  never retag). **Primary recompute = SURVIVORS-FIRST + CONTAINER-FIRST**: a surviving
  `[Activity]`/`[drag and drop]` co-tag keeps governing; the CONTAINER-FIRST preference
  was a live catch — `[Activity 2B] [MTK quiz, autograded…][H3]` (ARFUN02) recomputed
  to the h3 (ELEMENT 6 > CONTAINER_OPEN 5) and the activity box silently vanished
  before the preference was added. ELEMENT ⇒ the scanner never opens a capturing
  bundle ⇒ the writer's quiz content flows to the normal body render (constraint 1).
- **Emit** (`Emit_Templates.interactive_builders.mtk_quiz`; ContentConverter):
  `#mtkQuizEmit` ships the canonical button + ONE todo note (kind "todo" → the r219
  `red_flag.todo_form`, red+bold, class `cv2-note` = gate-excluded by construction)
  whose `{spec}` is the span's raw text — the modifier prose ("supports engagement,
  audio, video, file sharing", "should go to teacher dropbox") is never silently
  stripped (round-43 principle). **Four emit sites** cover every measured shape:
  the ELEMENT route (#element), the activity-opener co-tag (HPRE301's `[Activity 3C]
  [MTKQuiz]` — button+note inside the box it opens), the **bundle tail** (markers
  CAPTURED into a neighbouring widget's bundle — TEFUN03/06/07/08's `[Quiz]`-opener
  merge — and the bundle's own opener item, the ARFUN04-1H catch: the opening span
  lives in neither openerItems nor memberItems), and the element co-tag guard (makes
  the mechanism total). Once-per-item via `_mtkQuizEmitted`.
- **THE DEDUP (adjacent writer-button absorb)** — `#mtkQuizPrepass`: for each
  mtk-carrying item, a small window walk (2 back / 5 forward non-blank items; STOPS at
  another mtk item, an `[Activity]` opener, or any section/page/closer boundary — never
  leaks across activities; bundle-consumed items are INVISIBLE to the count — the
  ARFUN04 window-exhaustion catch) finds the writer's own quiz button: a
  `[button]`-family item labelled per `button_label_pattern` ("Go to quiz."/"Quiz") or
  a `[Go to quiz]` span per `marker_span_pattern`. Found → THAT site renders the ONE
  canonical anchored button (`_mtkQuizAnchor` upgrade at the button emit; a claimed
  thin `[Go to quiz]` BUNDLE has its empty placeholder box suppressed —
  `#mtkQuizBundleThin`) and the marker ships note-only (`_mtkButtonAbsorbed`). A
  bundle-consumed `[button]` is never claimed (it would lose the button — the TEFUN03
  live catch; the marker keeps its own). 
- **The closer:** `[End of MTK Quiz content]` stays `end mcq` CONTAINER_CLOSE both
  toggle states; with no open container the existing machinery ignores it gracefully
  ("[end mcq] had no open container — ignored", probe-observed).

**RESULTS.** The 19 tracked modules ship **54 anchored buttons + 54 todo notes — 1:1
per marker, zero doubles, zero losses** (per-module census in-round). Gold-shaped
site checks: TEFUN02 (box > h4 > p > button+note = gold EXACTLY), ARFUN02-2B (box 2B >
h3 > button > note > the kept quiz questions), ARFUN04 4/4, TEFUN03 3/3 with the
questions staying rendered in the sibling `[T/F]` dump. **Recorded residue:**
ARFUN04-4D's writer button glues an artifact link onto the same black run (multiline
label fails the exact-match claim BY DESIGN) → the canonical button ships plus the
writer's plain button below it, content preserved — 1 site.

**PROOF (scoped ship #4 — `scoped_ship.sh --affected outputs/_affected_mtkquiz.txt
--toggle MTKQUIZ_OFF --no-regen --commit`; ledger 4 scoped since the r228 full, 4
headroom).**
- **Toggle-OFF byte-identity:** 6-module OFF regen (TEFUN02/ARFUN02/SSOG301/ENG1004/

- **Containment PERFECT:** content-hash 0-stale (19 affected fresh, 371 unaffected

- **Completeness:** FRESH 12-module spot-check sample (the r229 re-plan-per-round

- **Forward guarantee** (`outputs/_probe_mtkquiz_fwd.cjs`, the r231 probe pattern —

**PROTECTED GATES — ALL HELD-or-IMPROVED at the r229 baselines (exact,

## 2026-07-17 (round 231, build 260618.04) — CL-0033: LANGUAGES-COHORT MODULES SHIP `template="combo"` — LIVE output-inert guarantee + capture (Chris — the CL0033 kickoff, ticket 6 of the CL0029-CL0052 triage; ZERO-blast round, the r224/r230 class, no ship-ledger increment)

**Plain English.** The design team's Change Ledger says every module in the Languages
cohort (Chinese, French, Gagana Samoa, German, Japanese, Spanish — their FUN and non-FUN
course codes) must load the "combo" page template on every page. There are no Languages
modules in the library yet, so nothing on disk changes today — but without this rule the
FIRST Languages module converted would have shipped with an EMPTY template attribute
(an unstyled page), because nothing in the converter's normal inheritance chain would
ever choose "combo" for a brand-new code with no siblings. A small data-driven rule now
guarantees the right template the day those modules arrive. Proven three ways: real
modules re-convert byte-identical with the rule on; a synthetic Languages code gets
"combo" on every page; the off-switch faithfully reverts it. Every gate holds by
construction.

**THE RULE (CL-0033, 14 Jul).** Every page of a Languages-cohort module ships
`template="combo"` on `<html>` (the sub-type still comes from the `<body>` class). The
cohort = doc-14 §14.1's `cohort_prefixes` (`data/Subject_Global_Parameters.json`, family
"14.1 Languages P1-4"): **CHIFUN, FREFUN, SAMFUN, GERFUN, JAPFUN, SPAFUN, CHI, FRE, SAM,
GER, JAP, SPA** — six languages × FUN + non-FUN forms.

**MEASURED FIRST (STEP 1 census, live, both corpora).** **431 distinct dir codes — ZERO
match any of the 12 prefixes; ZERO short-prefix collisions** (no non-Languages code
starts CHI/FRE/SAM/GER/JAP/SPA — the r218 "BLLR is NOT BLL" startswith trap checked and
clear); compare_set (200) holds none. And the gap is real: nothing today would ever
RESOLVE combo for a fresh Languages code — no registry row, no sibling → the TEDC-style
EMPTY attribute (the r221 pre-fix class; the probe's toggle leg doubles as this
measurement — with the fix OFF a synthetic JAPFUN01 ships the host chain's value, never
combo). Population 0 → an INERT forward-looking guarantee (the r218/r224/r230 class).

**FIX (DATA OVER CODE).** NEW `Emit_Templates.skeleton.template_phase_presets.
cohort_overrides` = `{enabled, value:"combo", prefixes:[the 12 verbatim]}` —
self-contained with a `_doc` cross-reference to doc-14 §14.1 (the engine never reads
Subject_Global_Parameters at runtime; SGP stays shipped-inert, `master_enabled:false`).
`SkeletonBuilder.BuildPage` applies it AFTER the r224 `prefix_overrides` loop (no key
overlap): code startsWith any listed prefix → `phaseForAttr = "combo"`, UNCONDITIONAL
(outranks sibling inheritance AND the digit preset; `preserve_values` does not apply —
the r224 absolute-override semantics), one `run.AddNote` info line. Kept a SEPARATE
block from `prefix_overrides` so each fix reverses independently (§2): **`LANGCOMBO_OFF`**
reverts Languages alone; `TPLPREFIX_OFF` keeps reverting BLL2 alone. `template_attr_map`
already carries `"combo":"combo"`. Captured
`_universal_conventions.cl0033_languages_combo` (the r229/r230 entry shape;
overrides_gold moot with no Languages gold on disk, but the marking stands — when
Languages modules arrive, an audit divergence matching the rule is INTENTIONAL, never
chased).

**PROOF (zero-blast round — `outputs/_probe_langcombo.cjs`, the r230 `_probe_ossch1`
pattern; ALL LEGS PASS).**
- LEG 1 INERT: **ENFUN01** (a real combo-attr module via its own chain — combo intact) +
  **BLL210** (the `prefix_overrides` fence — its "1-3" still wins) + **OSSC301** (r230
  canary, NCEA) full live conversions fix-ON = **6/6 pages byte-identical to disk**
  (page counts match disk exactly: 1/1/4).
- LEG 2 DETECTION: the r230 BuildPage monkey-patch sets `run.moduleCode = "JAPFUN01"`
  (the FUN 2-digit form) then `"JAP101"` (the digit-preset-shaped 3-digit form — matches
  `code_pattern` but JAP is not in `subjects`, covering both prefix classes) over
  OSSC301's conversion → **template attrs ["combo","combo","combo","combo"]** both times
  (template attr asserted ONLY — the patched code also changes chip etc., irrelevant).
- LEG 3 TOGGLE: same synthetic + `LANGCOMBO_OFF=1` → **["NCEA","NCEA","NCEA","NCEA"]**
  (the host chain's value, NOT combo — the faithful revert AND the STEP-1.2 gap proof).
- LEG 4 FENCE: covered by LEG 1's byte-identity (census: no real module carries a
  Languages prefix).
- `subject_parameters.py --selftest` PASS · `vet_issue.py --selftest` PASS (incl. the
  cascade selftest) · `node _check_index_sync.cjs` OK (32 browser / 27 node engine
  files, disk in sync — no new engine file this round).

**GATES.** Zero output bytes changed (byte-identity proven live; no regen — the corpus
and content manifest remain the r229 shipped state) → **every protected gate HOLDS BY
CONSTRUCTION at the r229 baselines**: skeleton **49.549% / ≥50 918 / ≥75 179 / ≥90 12 /
RAW 34.791% @ 1836 skipped 0** · cs **9442/172/455** · body **266** · clean **97.7%** /
leak **290/46** · tags **9557/9557** · flipCard **33 / div 0** · speechBubble **0** ·
entry-parity PASS. Ship ledger NOT incremented (the r190/r193/r224/r230 byte-identical
class) — scoped-ship headroom stays 6 before the full backstop is due.

**Data:** `skeleton.template_phase_presets.cohort_overrides` + the

## 2026-07-17 (round 230, build 260618.03) — THE OSSC PAIR: CL-0042 lesson-h1 GUARANTEE (live, output-inert) + CL-0043 lead-in VERIFIED ALREADY IN EFFECT — both captured (Chris — the CL0042_CL0043 OSSC-pair kickoff, tickets 4+5 of the CL0029-CL0052 triage; ZERO-blast round, no ship-ledger increment)

**Plain English.** The design team's Change Ledger added two rules from the OSSC401
difference report. (CL-0042) An OSSC lesson page's big heading must be that lesson's OWN
title — one heading only, never the module title doubled up with the Te Reo title pair.
(CL-0043) When the writer opens a lesson's overview with a describing sentence ("Ākonga
will…"), that sentence appears as a normal paragraph above the "We are learning:" labels.
We measured both first, and the converter ALREADY does both correctly: OSSC301's three
lesson pages ship exactly the rule's heading form today, and the lead-in sentence already
renders as a paragraph everywhere writers actually supply one (checked across the whole
Online Safety family — the converter matches the hand-built pages pair for pair). What
shipped is the missing GUARANTEE: the machinery that adds a second Te Reo heading to
lesson pages is real and configured to fire on OSSC — OSSC301 escapes it only by a lucky
accident (its title line never splits because of a ✅ emoji). A one-line data-driven gate
now makes the correct behaviour permanent for OSSC at every level, changing ZERO pages
today, plus both rules are recorded so no future audit ever "fixes" the converter back
toward the older hand-built form (which repeats "Ngā Tāware" on every lesson — those pages
pre-date the rule). Every gate holds by construction.

**Context.** OSSC401 (both rules' evidence module) is NOT on disk; `OSSC301` is the ONLY
OSSC dir (gold `Standard/OSSC301`, 4 pages; Claude dir present; the one dir NOT in
`compare_set.txt`). Both rules are (b)-scoped: OSSC-wide, designer-confirmed.

**CL-0042 (constraint 69) — OSSC lesson `<h1>` = the lesson's own title: LIVE
output-inert guarantee (the r224 TPLPREFIX pattern) + capture.** MEASURED FIRST
(`outputs/_measure_ossc_lesson_h1.py`, NEW): **Part A** — Claude ALREADY ships the rule's
exact form on all 3 OSSC301 lessons: chip (`1.0`) + ONE `<h1><span>` holding the
prefix-stripped lesson title (`[H2] *Lesson 1: What are online scams?*` → "What are online
scams?" — the r143 pre-activity harvest), NO te-reo second h1, NO body-h3 repeat (either
side). The GOLD is the diverging side: it repeats the module Te Reo title **"Ngā Tāware"
as a third h1 on every lesson** — the gold pre-dates the rule; that divergence is the
recorded INTENTIONAL override (never chase it back in). **Part B** — the dual-title lesson
machinery is REAL and fires today on **XMES 18 / CEDT 13 / SSFUN 4 pages — 0 OSSC** (1,619
Claude lesson pages scanned). The hazard is live: the registry's mined **OSSC3 lesson

## 2026-07-17 (round 229, build 260618.02) — THE ACTIVITY PAIR: CL-0030 measured-DECLINED + captured, CL-0048 live for the gold-solid ENFUN slice + captured (Chris — the CL0030_CL0048 activity-pair kickoff, tickets 2+3 of the CL0029-CL0052 triage; SCOPED ship #1 since the r228 full)

**Plain English.** The design team's Change Ledger added two rules about activity boxes:
(CL-0030) an activity box should hold at most ONE interactive — a writer stacking two gets
them split into lettered sibling activities; and (CL-0048) inside an activity, the text
should sit in its own row and the interactive in a separate row below it. We measured the
whole hand-built library first, and it says the library was built BEFORE these rules: the
human puts 2+ interactives in one box **510 times across 226 modules**, and the dominant
inside-the-box layout (75%) is text and widget together in ONE column — which is exactly
what the converter already produces. Splitting or restructuring everything would break
thousands of pages that match the human today. So: both rules are now RECORDED as marked
forward-looking rules (future modules and stocktakes honour them; nobody will ever "fix"
the converter back toward the old gold form), and the ONE place where the human library
already follows the new layout — the ENFUN Fundamentals family, 80% of its activities —
now gets the exact human form: text row first, widget in its own full-width row. Eight
ENFUN pages changed; every gate held or improved.

lesson / home) used to be pre-filled with links to the neighbouring generated files. The

"the one conflict to settle with Chris" — contingent on whether the gold populates footer

protection needed is for the 68 quickLink pages (rule `cl0044_footer_hrefs_empty` appended
to `Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions`: publish-time wiring is never
converter output — never chase those 68 toward "populated").

attributes (`home-nav` was always empty), and the round-226 choice-page TILE hrefs (a
different element, Chris's explicit decision — tiles keep linking the generated lesson
files). The emptied footer now byte-matches the gold's footer form.

## 2026-07-15 (round 227, build 260618.00) — THE DROPPED SOFT LINE BREAK: w:br → "\n" at the extractor (Chris — the XDLS900 triage's corpus-wide lever; the round-225 recorded follow-up; FULL ship)

**Plain English.** When a writer presses Shift+Enter (a soft line break inside one paragraph),
the document reader silently deleted it — the text on either side got GLUED together with no
space at all ("…two kinds of data.Measurements and numbers…", "…a place to stand."It is…").
That is corrupted text, corpus-wide: **5,999 soft breaks across 357 of the 429 Writers
Templates** (measured round 225, which patched the symptom inside whakataukī boxes only). This
round fixes the disease at the source: the extractor now keeps the writer's line break as a real
newline, and everything downstream renders it the way the hand-built pages do.

**MEASURED FIRST (`outputs/_measure_softbreak.py`, NEW — the top-8 carriers, 1,900 breaks,
classified against their own golds).** Gold's rendering of a soft-broken BLACK paragraph:
**split into consecutive `<p>`s 84** / same-element space-joined 172 (**164 of them EXPFUN03's
single house style** — its rubric tables, where our `\n` inside a `<td>` renders as plain HTML
whitespace = visually identical) / a literal `<br>` 31 / glued **0**. A THIRD of all breaks sit
in RED (tag/instruction) context. So: genuinely mixed at the margins, split-`<p>` the majority
form, and NOTHING in gold is ever glued — the kickoff's provision applies (the glue is a text
corruption, not an editorial choice; ship on net-positive gates).

**The fix (DATA OVER CODE; data `Input_Doc_Rules.paragraph.soft_break_newline`; env
`SOFTBR_OFF` reverts to the glued extraction byte-for-byte — proven on 10 modules).**
`DocxExtractor.#parseParagraph`'s run walk now reads `w:t` and `w:br` tokens IN ORDER; a
`<w:br/>` without `type="page|column"` contributes `"\n"` at its own position (the page-break
counter is untouched). Multi-line text is an existing, handled shape: `renderBlackText` emits
one `<p>`/`<li>` per line (the majority gold form), table cells show the newline as ordinary
whitespace (gold's space-join), `Utils.Fold` collapses `\s+` so tag CLASSIFICATION is
byte-identical, and the round-225 `#proverbSplit` goes dormant (proverb lines arrive
pre-split — XDLS905/906 and the other r225 modules regenerate BYTE-IDENTICAL, proving the two
mechanisms agree; OSSM301 additionally RECOVERS its "Meaning:" line as its own `<p>`).

**TWO CONTAINMENTS, both caught live by the disciplined loop (each part of the one toggle):**
- **Red-span granularity (caught on SSOG103's lesson menu).** A soft break often lives in a
  COLOURLESS run of its own between two red runs (`[Overview]` ⏎ `[H3] Knowledge` — one
  paragraph, tags on separate lines). Pre-fix that run carried NO text, was invisible to the
  red-group merge, and the two red runs fused into ONE marker span; a naive "\n" piece SPLIT
  the span in two and flipped tag granularity (SSOG103's two-col lesson menu vanished). A
  pure-newline colourless piece between two red pieces now merges INTO the red span — Fold
  collapses the newline, so the merged span parses byte-identically to the pre-fix glued form
  (probe-proven: primary/tags/RenderText identical). ONLY a `/^\n+$/` piece bridges this way;
  any other separator was already visible pre-fix and keeps its two-span behaviour.
- **Hover-sentinel atomicity (caught on MXDI202-09, defect class E).** A woven
  U+E000…U+E001 definition pair whose text spans a soft break was CUT by the per-line split,
  leaking an unpaired sentinel character into each half. `renderBlackText` now collapses any
  newline INSIDE a sentinel pair to a space before splitting — the pair stays atomic; corpus
  sentinel characters **1 → 0**. (The guard is provably inert elsewhere: it needs a `\n`
  inside a pair; the class-E scan over ALL 2,009 pages finds exactly the one page, and a
  69-page regen of the hover-heaviest modules through the guard is byte-identical — the
  post-guard regen is content-proven fresh even though its mtime postdates the bulk regen.)

**FULL ship (the due backstop — ledger reset to 0).** All 393 gated dirs regenerated, 0 stale
by mtime; blast = **305 pages / 143 modules changed, 0 added / 0 removed** (pagination stable

## 2026-07-15 (round 225, build 260617.98) — WHAKATAUKĪ PROVERB NORMALISE: the glued reo/English split + the plain-<p> strips (Chris — the XDLS905/906 screenshots)

**Plain English.** Chris's screenshots showed the whakataukī boxes shipping wrong: the Māori
proverb and its English translation jammed into ONE bold line with the writer's curly quotes
kept (`"Kei roto i te pōuri…"Through perseverance…`), where the human developer always ships two
separate plain paragraphs (the site CSS supplies the bold/italic styling). This round makes every
whakataukī box match the human house form.

**Root cause (triangulated).** The writer authors the proverb as a bold reo line, a SOFT line
break (`w:br` inside one docx paragraph), then the English. `DocxExtractor` DROPS soft breaks, so
the two lines arrive GLUED with no separator at all — the text itself is corrupted
(`…ana”Through…`). The lost break is still VISIBLE as a boundary in the raw text, so the fix
re-derives the writer's own line structure at the proverb render instead of guessing.
(A corpus-wide `w:br → \n` extractor fix was measured and DEFERRED: **5,999 soft breaks across
357/429 WTs** — a full-ship round of its own; recorded lever.)

**Measured convention (tool `outputs/_measure_whakatauki.py`, NEW — the standing verifier).**
GOLD: 215 `.whakatauki` boxes / 178 modules — **two+ separate PLAIN `<p>` 213/215**, `<b>` kept
only 2/215, `<i>` 5/215, edge quotes (curly or straight) 9/215. CLAUDE before: 85 boxes /
74 modules — 27 glued single-`<p>`, 14 with `<b>`, 10 with curly quotes.

**Fix (DATA OVER CODE; data `callouts.by_tag.whakatauki.proverb_normalise`; env `PROVERBNORM_OFF`
reverts split AND strips).** Two halves in ContentConverter:
- **`#proverbSplit`** (raw text, before renderBlackText — the markers ARE the signal; one split
  per line, first rule wins, URL lines untouched): a leading `**bold**`/`*italic*` marker group
  (EXACT pair alternation — a `\*{1,2}` quantifier let backtracking DONATE an asterisk to the
  tail and split off a junk `*` line, caught on the round's own A/B: XDLS904/XTAS101; inner ≥10
  chars so XLP03's mangled `***“***` can never split mid-proverb; the tail must carry a real
  letter/digit) · a leading `“quoted”` phrase + prose (CEDO301) · a space-BEFORE pipe with no
  space after (`riri |*Well done…*`, OSBY301 — the strict spaced-pipe rule needs both sides) ·
  a full-tail `(english translation)` with the parens dropped (ENGR102, gold drops them too).
- **`#proverbStripSeg`** (rendered segments, applied to lead + content): `MenuBuilder.
  stripTextBold/Italic` (handles the mangled triple-marker runs cleanly) + edge-anchored
  curly/straight-quote strip + stray-asterisk cleanup + an ORPHAN EDGE PIPE strip (the writer
  typed the separator INSIDE the bold group — `**…rangatahi |**`, OSSM301; the r177
  boundary-separator class; measured exactly 1 site corpus-wide).

**After (same tool):** single-`<p>` **27 → 9** — the 9 are the MEASURED DECLINES: single-language
payloads whose English is in NO WT (XDLS904, XLP03, CEDT104, EXBP901×2, HES1005×2 — gold's
English is editorial, recorded C) + the no-marker language-boundary glue (CEDT501-12 "kōrero. The
food…", CEDO105 — no derivable split point, recorded C). `<b>` **14 → 0**, `<i>` **→ 0**,
edge-quotes **10 → 0**. XDLS905/906 whakataukī now match gold byte-for-byte.

**SCOPED SHIP #5 (§10a; 3 of headroom before the full backstop).** Affected superset = the 74
modules whose output carries a `.whakatauki` box (+ TEFUN02, see drift) — `outputs/
_affected_whakatauki.txt`. Proofs: toggle-OFF byte-identical to the r224 manifest (55/56 sample

## 2026-07-14 (round 224, build 260617.97) — THE BLL200 PHASE EXCEPTION: template="1-3" for every BLL2xx module (Chris — design-team note, permanent rule)

**Plain English.** The design team has ruled that the BLL200 modules (every module whose code
starts "BLL2") are actually PHASE 1 — so the `template=""` attribute at the top of each HTML page
must be **"1-3"**, never the "4-6" that their series digit or a mis-built sibling would suggest.
BLLR200 modules, in contrast, ARE phase 2 and keep "4-6". This round makes that a PERMANENT,
data-configured converter rule, and also corrects the human gold library where it carried the
wrong value.

**The rule (engine + data).** A new GENERAL mechanism, the r221 preset's sibling:
`skeleton.template_phase_presets.prefix_overrides` — an explicit code-PREFIX → template map for
families whose code digit is NOT a curriculum level (exactly the families the r221 digit preset
had to exclude). LONGEST matching prefix wins; a `null` value means "explicitly no override"
(a guard entry); the override is UNCONDITIONAL — it outranks sibling inheritance AND the r221
`by_level_digit` preset, and `preserve_values` ("combo") does not apply (an explicit exception
list is absolute). Entries this round: `"BLL2": "1-3"` + `"BLLR": null` (belt-and-braces — a
"BLLR…" code can never `startsWith("BLL2")` since the 4th char is R not 2, but doc-14's r218
"BLLR is NOT BLL" startswith trap earns the explicit fence; when BLLR modules join the corpus
they fall through to the normal chain and ship "4-6"). Applied in `SkeletonBuilder.BuildPage`
directly after the r221 digit-preset block; emits the same one-per-module info run-note when it
actually changes a value. Adding a future prefix exception = one data entry, no code.

**MEASURED (before coding).** Corpus census (`outputs/_detect_tplprefix.cjs`, ALL 431 dirs —
Claude ∪ gold, live `ModuleResolver.Resolve` per module, the r175/r221 complete-detector
pattern): 50 BLL2 gold modules / 32 tracked Claude dirs; **every one already resolves
template_phase "1-3"** via the style-anchor registry's BLL2 group, so the rule changes **ZERO
attributes on the current corpus** — it was only ACCIDENTALLY right (the registry is mined from
a gold library that was itself 90% correct; a wrong-sibling chain or a registry rebuild over the
5 bad golds could have flipped it). The rule converts that accident into a guarantee. Over-fire
ZERO by construction (the map matches only BLL2*; BLL1xx census 154 pages "1-3" untouched).

**PROOF (output-inert + detection, the r218 pattern).**
- `outputs/_probe_tplprefix.cjs` — 5-leg LIVE full-conversion proof on BLL225, ALL PASS:
  (1) CLEAN: fix ON → template="1-3" AND byte-identical to the shipped corpus;
  (2) DETECTION: `rules.template_phase` doctored to "4-6" after PrepareRun (a simulated wrong
  sibling chain) → pages STILL ship "1-3" + the info note appears — the override provably fires;
  (3) TOGGLE: same doctored run under `TPLPREFIX_OFF=1` → ships "4-6" (faithful reversal);
  (4) BLLR FENCE: doctored run as "BLLR225" → stays "4-6"; (5) BLL1 FENCE: as "BLL125" → "4-6".
- `outputs/_probe_tplprefix_inert.cjs` — full live conversions byte-identical to the shipped
  corpus on 8 modules: BLL210/BLL240 (Inquiry parents), BLL211/BLL232/BLL254 (Standard),
  BLL110 (BLL1 canary), OSAH501 + ENGC102 (non-BLL canaries).
- `node _check_index_sync.cjs` OK (32/27 — no new engine file).

**GOLD LIBRARY CORRECTION (Chris's explicit instruction).** 5 of the 50 BLL2 gold modules
carried the wrong `template="4-6"` — **BLL250, BLL261, BLL264, BLL265, BLL275** (13 files) —
all corrected to `template="1-3"`, including BLL265_1_0.html's page-local
`html[template="4-6"]` CSS selectors (3 occurrences — replaced WITH the attribute so the

## 2026-07-12 (round 218, build 260617.91) — DOC-14 v2026-07-09 REFRESH + THE GOLD-OVERRIDE MARKING (Chris)

**Plain English.** Chris supplied the newest Subject Global Parameters (doc 14, last updated 9 July
2026) with a standing instruction: these are the design team's up-to-date rules, and **future Claude
conversions must follow them even where the existing human-built HTML does not** — the gold library
was built before these rules existed. He also asked that the new principles be **marked** so nothing
ever mistakes a doc-14-mandated difference for a converter regression during a WT→human-HTML
stocktake. This round does exactly those two things. It changes NO converter output (the doc-14
mechanism stays inert, as shipped in round 178) — it locks the rules into the converter's data as
the single source of truth, and teaches every stocktake/vetting tool to recognise and protect them.

**WHAT CHANGED.**
1. **`data/Subject_Global_Parameters.json` recaptured to doc-14 v2026-07-09** (was the round-178
   8-family snapshot): now **10 families** — adds **14.9 BLLR** (bookworm avatars by code range,
   secret-shelf/Whispering-Archives red-notes, the parameters-partial rule) and **14.10 MiW/WJ**
   (NZ-map intro pages + the iStock-1454804075 ack line, the FUN trailing-digit naming test, the Kea
   character) — plus the expanded LS (Venn button, move-forward alert copy, standard LS overview,

   and `_meta` carries a dated **`gold_override_policy`** (Chris, 2026-07-12): within its scope a
   doc-14 rule **outranks the module's own human gold** — the ONE recorded exception to LEVEL 0
   (`reference/Human_Gold_Is_The_Per_Module_Target.md`, new carve-out section; mirrored in

## 2026-07-12 (round 217, build 260617.90) — THE ACTIVITY/INTERACTIVE BOUNDARY AUDIT → the STANDALONE TASK-WIDGET ACTIVITY BOX + the bare-[Interactive] invocation (Chris)

**Plain English.** Chris reported that activity and interactive boundaries are often wrong — boxes
closing too early (content spills below) or too late (later content absorbed) — and asked for a full
audit of how the human developer bounds these, then immediate action. The audit measured every
misplaced text block corpus-wide and found the single biggest boundary error is not a close-too-early
or close-too-late at all: **the human INVENTS an activity box the writer never tagged**. The gold
library ships **6,863 activity boxes against only 5,663 writer `[Activity*]` tags** — whenever a
TASK-type interactive (drag-and-drop, quiz, self-check…) stands alone, the human wraps it in
`<div class="activity interactive" number="1B">` with the next lesson letter, and whole families
(MXDI, HIS, MXFU…) author with ZERO `[Activity]` tags. Claude only ever boxed writer-tagged
activities, so on those pages every box was missing and every later letter drifted (the audit's
A_WRONG class). This round ships that convention, plus the bare `[Interactive]` invocation that
previously dissolved into an instruction note and leaked its data table.

**THE AUDIT (the measurement record — all in `outputs/`).** `_measure_boundary_audit.py` — every
text block located on BOTH sides (inside widget? inside which activity box?), matched Claude→gold by
folded text against a whole-module map (pagination-immune), classified: **W_OVER 3,944** (widget ate
it, gold keeps free) / **W_UNDER 5,367** (gold puts it in a widget Claude never captured/built) /
**A_OVER 2,047** (box too greedy) / **A_SPILL 5,854** (gold's box holds it, Claude's doesn't) /
**A_WRONG 3,560** (different-numbered box). `_measure_boundary_triggers.py` — the FIRST spilled /
absorbed item per box names each boundary's trigger tag; **A_SPILL decomposed: 1,149 of 1,478 spilled
boxes were never created at all** (the invented-box class) vs 329 genuine early-closes.
`_measure_widget_boxing.py` — the gold census: task types are boxed ~1.00 (dragAndDrop 731/731,
multiChoiceQuiz 0.99, typing/dropQuiz/radioQuiz/reorder/wordDrag/memoryGame/bingo/selfCheck ≈1.00);
display types are boxed only via a writer [Activity] (accordion 0.29, carousel 0.46, flipCards 0.33,
tabs 0.36, clickDrop 0.39, shapeHover 0.10, imageLabel 0.05). `_measure_standalone_boxing.py` — the
DISCRIMINATOR measured on Claude's own bundles (for each STANDALONE bundle, does gold box that same
content?): **dragAndDrop 0.97 (73 decided) / unclassified 0.88 (163) / multiChoiceQuiz 0.89 (38) /
radioQuiz 0.88 (8) / selfCheck 0.83 (6) → BOX; display types 0.08–0.16 → stay bare; AMBIGUOUS band
dropDown 0.57 / selectionBox 0.78 / typing 0.60 / slider 0.43 / reorder 0.50 → recorded, NOT shipped**
(needs a group-level discriminator — do not add without re-measuring).

**FIX 1 — STANDALONE TASK-WIDGET ACTIVITY BOX (env `ACTWRAP_OFF`; data
`activity_wrapper.standalone_widget_box`).** At the bundle emit, a standalone bundle (no
activityOwner, no activityId, not embedded/reo) whose `bundle.type` is in the measured list wraps in
the standard box via a SYNTHETIC owner (the reo_bundle_activity pattern — no lead text; the gold's
box TITLE heading is human-authored, in no WT → recorded C, never invented) with `.interactive`
FORCED (the box exists because of the widget) and the **NEXT POSITIONAL lesson letter**
(`ActivitiesBuilder.activityOpen` gains `positionalId` — advances the same per-lesson counter the
tagged activities use, exactly how the human counts its invented boxes in sequence; AGH1001-01 ships
1A/1B matching gold). **Scope: numbered-lesson pages only** (`#pageLessonNumber != null`) — on
single-file fundamentals/overview pages the human numbers by PHASE (HPFUN201 gold 1A/1B/2A/2B…),
which is not yet derivable; a numberless box is a shape gold never ships and MIS-PAIRS against
gold's numbered boxes (measured −15..−17pp on HPFUN overviews before the scope was added). Phase
numbering = recorded follow-up. reoMode excluded (bilingual has reo_bundle_activity + its own
placeholder surface).

**FIX 2 — THE BARE `[Interactive]` INVOCATION (env `INTALIAS_OFF`; data Tag_Lexicon
`_meta.qualifier_alias_demote.standalone_becomes` + boundary-bank `interactives.interactive` +
`member_rule.bare_invocation_dissolve_empty`).** "interactive" is an ALIAS of the activity tag,
demoted by qualifier_alias_demote — correct for "[Interactive Stop Watch] …" qualifiers, but the
BARE standalone "[Interactive]" span (the span's ONLY tag, matched EXACTLY) is the writer's generic
widget invocation: AGH1001-01 authors "[Interactive] ↵ Drag and drop the products… ↵ TABLE" and gold
builds widget + box; Claude rendered an instruction note and LEAKED the data table as a kept
`<table>`. The bare form now RE-TAGS as a generic INTERACTIVE opener (canonical `interactive`,
GetWidgetTypes [] → the scanner names the bundle after the tag) so the instruction + table are
captured, and FIX 1 boxes it. THREE containments, each measured in: (a) embedded qualifier forms +
multi-tag spans still demote-drop exactly as before; (b) a NEW boundary-bank entry for the type
(heading_is_terminator + **uses_data_table** — without it the post-table `[Body]` was absorbed,
tripping body_compare OVER-CAPTURE on AGH1001-01); (c) **bare_invocation_dissolve_empty** — a bundle
that captured NO table and under 40 RENDERED chars of member text (bold markers stripped —
ANZH203-06's 38-char title read 42 raw) DISSOLVES at scan finalization (items left unconsumed → the
pre-217 note/image forms; without this the alias pushed body_compare EMPTY +7). The affected-set
detector `outputs/_detect_intalias.cjs` runs the SHIPPED Parse over every WT's red spans (the r175
completeness rule — a line-anchored grep found 13 spans/8 modules; the real class is **37 modules**,
mid-line spans included; ground-truth banner sweep confirmed +XWHA02 whose span arrives via the r174
bracket repair).

**BLAST + PROOFS.** FULL corpus regen (34-batch plan + the follow-up passes), `_stalecheck` 0 stale
at each stage; final byte-diff vs the r216 manifest = **400 pages / 155 modules**. Toggle-OFF
invariant: `ACTWRAP_OFF=1 INTALIAS_OFF=1` regen of AGH1001/HIS1003/MXDI202/HPFUN201/BLL240/TEDC402 is
**byte-identical to the r216 manifest** (all six vanish from the manifest diff). Spot-checks after
each engine edit: BLL210/ENGJ402/OSAI501/HIS1004/TEDC402 re-regen byte-identical (edits are no-ops
outside the fired sets). Two ghost FLAT dirs created by passing out-of-corpus codes (TRR110, CEDR203
— NOT in compare_set, no nested dir) were deleted; the r128 pre-create rule stands.

**PROTECTED GATES (all vs the r216 baselines).** PRIMARY skeleton (5-chunk fresh full score, merged
`outputs/_r217_sk_final.json`, **skipped 0 @ 1825**): SCAFFOLD mean **49.295 → 49.436% (+0.141
IMPROVED)** / RAW **34.661 → 34.680 (IMPROVED)** / ≥90% **12 EXACT** / ≥50% **913 (−1)** / ≥75% **176
(−2)** — the dip is DOCUMENTED NET-POSITIVE (the r164 class): 351 pages moved, **154 up / 197 down,
net +258pp**; the named crossers (AGH1009-06, ANZH304-03, BLL111-02, AGH1007-01, MXDI102-03,
HIS1005-07, ENGR301-03, MXFL203-11, SSOG301-03 ↓50; BLL166-01, PHE1005-01 ↓75 — against ANZH104-06,
AGH1001-02, AGH1009-07, MXFL204-04, MXFU201-03, PES1004-07, PHE1008-02/-04 ↑50) sit in the two

## 2026-07-11 (round 214, build 260617.87) — BASIC INTERACTIVES: accordion NUMBERED-SERIES CONTAINMENT + working CAROUSELS + the ROW-per-tab TABS build (Chris, the OSOH501-01 screenshot set)

**Plain English.** Chris's screenshots showed OSOH501 lesson 1 falling apart: the writer authored ONE
accordion with four numbered panels ([Accordion 1]…[Accordion 4]), but the converter split it into
fragments — panel 1's clickable images broke out as a separate box, panel 3's READYSAFE letter-tabs

hauora carousel (4 slides of image + title + text) and the READYSAFE tabs never built at all. Chris's
rule, applied generally: everything between [Accordion N] and [Accordion N+1] belongs to panel N —
including other interactives typed inside a panel — and these basic widget forms should BUILD. Now:
OSOH501-01 ships ONE real accordion with all four panels (the modals and values table nested inside
their panels, the READYSAFE tabs BUILT and nested inside panel 3 exactly like the human's page), both
carousels BUILD, and the same fixes fire wherever the same authoring appears in the corpus (63 modules
changed). Every fix is corpus-general, data-flagged, and reversible.

**MEASURED (before coding).** (a) ACCORDION SPLIT (`outputs/_measure_accnest.py`): 66 modules author
>=2 numbered [Accordion N]; **28 have interactive invocations interposed between panels** (modal 48,
carousel 61, tab/tabs 50, clickDrop 95, speechBubble 93 …); gold groups the panels into FEWER
accordion divs in nearly all. (`outputs/_measure_accnest_gold.py`): **83 modules' golds nest widget
markup INSIDE accContent** (videoSection 74m, carousel 13m, speechBubble 12m, flipCard 6m, clickDrop
6m, dropDown, hintSlider, tabs, shapeHover). (b) TABS ROW-FORM (`outputs/_measure_tabrows.py`): the
row-per-tab table ([tab N] label cell | content cell) is authored by **EXACTLY 3 modules** (OSOH501
×9 rows, OSOH201, CEDT501) and the gold builds a tabs nav on ALL THREE. (c) CAROUSEL CAPTION FORM
(`outputs/_measure_carousel_caption.py`): the slide-title form is group-split — OSAI-style
<h4>-above-img (A) vs OSOH-style bold first caption <p> (B, OSOH 29:0); B-dominant subject prefixes
mined into a data list, A stays the default (byte-identical for every carousel already building).

**THE FIVE FIXES (each data-flagged + env-toggled).**
1. **`ACCNEST_OFF`** — NUMBERED-SERIES CONTAINMENT (`member_rule.numbered_series_absorb`;
   `InteractiveScanner`): while an accordion host is a numbered series, a different-type interactive
   invocation absorbs as a NESTED sub-bundle (the r95 mechanism, factored into the shared
   `#absorbNestedSubBundle`) — always when a later numbered same-type tag lies ahead (the
   between-panels forward guarantee), after the LAST panel only when the series is real
   (>= min_panels 2); an invocation-carrying member TABLE (panel 4's [Click drop] values table)
   absorbs the same way; a lone heading that CONTINUES a same-level run inside the current panel
   ([H5] Manaaki/Tika/Whanaungatanga) no longer truncates the last panel. Nested sub-bundles render
   in place — BUILT when their own builder succeeds (the READYSAFE tabs), else an honest nested
   placeholder.
2. **`ACCRICH2_OFF`** — rich-accordion member extensions (`accordion.rich_panels.*`): a panel's own
   [H2]-[H6] sub-heading renders faithfully; a writer CS/Dev note inside a panel is SKIPPED by the
   build (it still surfaces as the standard red cv2-note after the widget via bundle.instructions —
   never silently stripped); a docx numbered-list artifact line ("1.") renders nothing; a nested
   BUILT widget wraps in the human's in-panel <div class=row>.
3. **`CARTRAIL_OFF`** — carousel TRAILING-SECTION-HEADING break (`member_rule.
   slideshow_heading_lone_break`): the r96 blanket "every heading is internal" exemption let the
   section heading AFTER the whole carousel be swallowed as a bogus empty 5th slide, killing the
   build. Now PRECISE: a heading preceded by a [Slide N] marker is a slide title (the r96 OSAI501-04
   protection); otherwise the r77 lone+follow test runs (follow=image keeps a heading-opened slide's
   title inside; a trailing heading followed by body text terminates). TWO measured guards: REO
   modules keep the blanket exemption (TRR301's text-form carousel re-leaked 1 literal tag without
   it — the r145 exclusion class) and only IMAGE-carrying carousels run the test (a text-form
   heading+body carousel would lose its LAST slide — measured MXDB302-06 scaffold 54.8→25.0 without
   this guard; both guards A/B-caught during this round's gate runs and fixed before shipping).
4. **`CARCAP_OFF`** — the bold-<p> caption title form (`carousel.caption_title_bold` +
   `item_image_caption`): B-dominant subjects ship the slide title as the caption's first
   <p><b>title</b></p> (the OSOH gold shape); a slide whose heading the writer forgot (OSOH501-02
   slide 4 — gold's recovered title is in NO WT, recorded C) ships body-only instead of an empty h4.
5. **`TABROWS_OFF`** — ROW-per-tab table tabs (`tabs.rich_panes.row_panes`; `#tabsTableRows`): label =
   the [tab N] cell's remaining text (** stripped, nav chrome PLAIN); pane = the content cell's
   [image]/[H4]/[body] segments in order (img + h4 + p — the gold OSOH501-01 pane shape). Gated to
   the measured subjects (OSOH/CEDT). OSOH501: **9/9 panes verifier-EXACT**. OSOH201/CEDT501 decline
   on richer cells (recorded residue). NEVER half-builds.

## 2026-07-11 (round 213, build 260617.86) — DOMAIN LINK-TEXT DISPLAY: deep speldsa.org.au links show the site root as their visible text (Chris, the BLL241 supervisor-note screenshot) + THE FULL ship.sh BACKSTOP (cadence reset)

**Plain English.** In the human-built BLL modules, a supervisor note's link to the SPELD SA website
shows just "https://speldsa.org.au" on screen, while the link itself still points at the full deep
address (…/pages/speld-sa-phonic-books). The converter was showing the whole long URL as the visible
text. Chris asked for the human's form on every such link, in any module. The converter now does
exactly that: for the domains listed in the data (currently speldsa.org.au — add a domain by adding
one line), a link whose visible text is itself a URL renders that text as the site root, and the full
deep address stays in the link underneath. A link whose text is a normal descriptive phrase is never
touched, so no meaningful wording can ever be lost.

**MEASURED (before coding).** Human golds, corpus-wide: BODY-side speldsa links show the bare domain
**67/68** (66 modules — nearly all BLL supervisor notes); their ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS keep the FULL URL
text (97+ sites). So the rule is BODY-scoped: the post-pass stops at the acks block. Claude before:
113 body anchors all showing the deep URL (99 pages / 73 BLL modules).

**FIX (data `elements.link_text_display`; env `LINKTEXT_OFF`).** `ListsAndRuns.LinkTextDisplay` — a
full-page post-pass (the OmitPlaceholderResidue/TidyDeveloperNotes pattern, wired in PageAssembler)
so every emitter present and future is covered uniformly. Three containments, each measured: (1)
stops at the acknowledgements block (the human keeps full URLs there); (2) skips `cv2-interactive`
placeholder subtrees (an un-built widget's dump is the developer's raw hand-off material — the r201
containment class; without this, 8 pages' short link-only dumps tripped the body gate's EMPTY-widget
heuristic, A/B-proven 272→280→272); (3) rewrites ONLY an anchor whose text is itself a URL on the
same domain — a phrase link never matches. RESULT: **92 visible body links canonicalised across 71
modules**; 21 dump-internal links stay raw; href always untouched.

**THE FULL SHIP (the due cadence backstop — scoped #8 had been reached).** Full 392-dir regen
(34-batch plan + resume splits), `_stalecheck` **0 stale**; content-manifest diff = **exactly the
71 link-text modules** (the whole rest of the corpus reproduced byte-identical through the current
engine — bounding any accumulated under-scoping from rounds 206–212 at zero); fast-loop baselines
refreshed (cs/bc/defect direct; skeleton written from the decomposition-proven r211→r212 state chain —
the full skeleton run exceeds the sandbox 45s wall; the r213 change is text-only and skeleton-invisible,
spot-verified EXACT on BLL241/BLL225/BLL211); ledger **record-full round 213, scoped counter reset 0**.

bilingual module (title "Ngā tau: 1 / Numbers: 1", a three-tab Tirohanga Whānui | Ngā Whāinga Matua |
Mōhiohio menu, and the module introduction with its video). The cause: the PNR family is written on a
NEW bilingual Writers Template ("Te Aka Taumatua") whose opening markers the converter had never seen.
The whole overview lives between a `[Content for DROP DOWN MENU]` marker (one English|Māori two-column
table holding the entire module menu) and a `[MODULE CONTENT: PAGE 1]` introduction — and because none
of those markers was a recognised "content start", the front-matter trimmer threw ALL of it away as
boilerplate before conversion even began. The first thing it recognised was `[LESSON 1 CONTENT]`, so
only the lesson pages survived. This round teaches the converter the new template's shape end to end;
the overview now converts with the title, the full bilingual tabs menu, and the introduction — closely
matching the human build on all three PNR modules — and two TRR siblings gain their missing module
titles from the same metadata source.

**WT → human → Claude (the triangulated evidence, PNR101-0.0).** Raw WT: front matter (checklist/LOT)
→ `[Content for DROP DOWN MENU]` → ONE English|Māori table (a `[TITLE BAR]` row left empty;
`[H2][TAB1] Overview`, `[TAB2] Key objectives`, `[TAB3] Information` label rows; `[H2]`/`[H1]`
headings; `[Body]` prose/bullets/checkbox lists) → `[END OF DROP-DOWN MENU]` (PNR102 types it WITHOUT
the hyphen) → `[MODULE CONTENT: PAGE 1]` → the proverb + module-introduction table → `[END PAGE]` →
`[LESSON 1 CONTENT]` → …. The module title lives in the front-matter metadata TABLE row "Module Name |
Ngā tau: 1 | Numbers: 1" (there is NO [TITLE BAR] payload anywhere). Human 0.0: two title `<h1>`s (reo
first), nav `<li><a><span reo>…</span><span eng>…</span></a></li>` ×3, pane 1 `col-md-8`, panes 2/3
`col-md-6 offset-md-0 paddingR` (the Information pane SPLIT at the Connections heading into
paddingR|paddingL), `<h4><span>` section heads / `<h5>` lead-ins / paired `<p reo>/<p eng>` +
`<ul reo>/<ul eng>`, and the introduction in the body. Claude before: empty page. Claude after: all of
it (the three PNR overviews now scaffold-match the human at 82–89%).

**MEASURED (the class, corpus-wide).** The exact bracketed `[Content for DROP DOWN MENU]` marker
exists in the WTs of EXACTLY PNR101/102/104 (grep over every parsed WT) — plus, live-scanned through
the shipped guard over the 14 Bilingual dirs that have NO parsed txt (the r175 detector lesson),
TRR203 and TRR301 carry the marker in a PARAGRAPH-form dialect (their menu content is loose paragraphs
inside one giant para, with a visible [TITLE BAR] the standard chain already finds) and TRR301/TRR304
carry a "Module Name" metadata table row. Detector: `outputs/_detect_reodropdown.cjs`. The
paragraph-form TRR dialect is deliberately NOT built this round (a recorded follow-up); every scoping
choice below exists to keep TRR203's bytes identical.

**FIX (six coupled pieces, ONE toggle `REODROPMENU_OFF`; data `elements.dual_language.dropdown_menu` +
`Input_Doc_Rules.content_start.content_start_fragments_dropdown` +
`front_matter_metadata.table_row_fields`).**
1. **Content-start rescue** (`DocxExtractor.TrimFrontMatter`): when the standard chain's first content
   start is a LESSON-CONTENT block (not a title-bar one) and a `[Content for DROP DOWN MENU]`
   paragraph exists earlier, the document opens there instead. TRR203/TRR301 (title-bar starts) are
   untouched by construction.
2. **Page split** (`PageSplitter`): a `page`-PAGE_BOUNDARY item whose folded text matches
   `^\[module content\b` stays on the OVERVIEW (the human's 0.0 = menu + module content), gated on the
   stream having carried the STANDALONE opener (`_ddSeenOpener`); the marker's own table is flagged
   `_reoModuleContent`. TRR203/301 glue this marker onto the closer inside one span (the anchored
   pattern never matches) and TRR304 has no opener — all three keep their pagination.
3. **Scanner suppression** (`InteractiveScanner.#dropdownMenuMarker`): the opener parses as a
   "dropdown" INTERACTIVE invocation — on a reo module whose opener is DIRECTLY followed by a table
   it never opens a widget bundle (it is a menu marker, not a widget; the r194 suppression class).
4. **Menu routing** (`ContentConverter.#partitionItems`): on a reo overview, opener→closer routes to
   the MENU side (the table flagged `_reoDropdown`, the markers consumed) — only when the opener is
   directly followed by the table (the PNR shape).
5. **The bilingual tabs menu compose** (`MenuBuilder.#reoDropdownTabs` + the NEW `menu.shells.reo_tabs`
   shell + `SkeletonBuilder`): one pane per `[TABn]` row (its text = the nav label only, reo+eng
   spans); `[TITLE BAR]`/English|Māori divider rows skipped; the pane's FIRST heading and every [H2] →
   `<h4><span>`, later [H1]/[H3] → `<h5>` (the human's exact levels on all three golds); a
   Connections-family heading (`pane_split_labels`) starts the pane's second paddingR|paddingL column;
   body rows render through the shared `BilingualBuilder.bilingualSplit` interleaved reo-first, with
   "☐" checklist lines becoming ordinary bullets. Declines (no [TABn] rows) fall through to the
   generic walk.
6. **The title** (`PageAssembler` + `DocxExtractor.#extractMetadata`): the front-matter metadata table
   is now read for the fields in `table_row_fields` (ONLY `moduleName` — deliberately not
   course/moduleCode so the Course-backup path can never newly fire); when NO title was derived at
   all, "Module Name" pipe-splits into the two header `<h1>`s in payload order (reo first — the
   CEDW501 positional-slot precedent). Also fixes TRR301 ("Reretūpono") and TRR304 ("Te Kaimahi
   Whakaputa") whose golds carry exactly those titles and whose Claude pages had NONE.
   And `BilingualBuilder.bilingualTable` accepts the `_reoModuleContent`-flagged table without an
   English|Māori header row (PNR102/104 open theirs with "Module Introduction | Kōwae Ako Whakataki").

**SCOPED SHIP (§10a, #8 since the last full ship).** Affected list = PNR101/102/104 + TRR203/301/304
(`outputs/_affected_reodropdown.txt`); toggle-exists OK; content-hash 0-stale OK; **containment: 5
changed ⊆ 6 affected** (TRR203 byte-identical, as designed); **completeness spot-check 12/12

## 2026-07-10 (round 211, build 260617.84) — INFORMATION-PANE NATIVE TWO-COLUMN: the overview menu's Information tab lays out in the human's two columns (Chris, the AGH1002 screenshot)

**Plain English.** On AGH1002's human-built overview, the Information tab shows its content in TWO
side-by-side columns — Learning Intentions and Success Criteria on the left, "Planning your time" and
"What do I need to get started?" on the right — while the converter dumped everything into one long
column. This round measured every human-built tabs overview in the library to find WHEN the human
uses two columns there, and shipped the rule. The answer: it is a per-subject-family house style, and
within a family the tell is whether the pane holds the Learning-Intentions/Success-Criteria block —
AGH's humans go two-column on every overview whose Information tab carries the LI/SC (3 of 3) and
one-column on every overview whose tab only has planning/get-started (6 of 6). Crucially the rule is
NOT "LI/SC present ⇒ two columns" globally: the maths (MXEO) family's human "Learning" tabs carry the
LI/SC and stay ONE column (0 of 3 split) — so the rule ships as a per-group registry, exactly like the
extra-tabs and Learning-tab rounds before it. AGH1002's Information tab now matches the human's
arrangement: LI + SC left, planning + get-started right, in the human's exact
`col-md-6 paddingR | paddingL` column pair.

**The measurement (`outputs/_measure_tab2_cols.py`, NEW — all 186 gold tabs-overviews + the Claude
side; scans `--scan H/C`, census `--report`, registry `--gen`).** Human info panes: 44 two-col / 138
one-col / 4 none. Chris's candidate discriminators, tested: (1) PANE LABEL — no signal (Information
splits 41/146, Learning 1/5). (2) SECTION COUNT — no clean threshold (2-section panes split 14/75;
8-section panes 0/19). (3) GROUPING LADDER — subject|phase is where it solidifies (8 solid-2col
groups, 7 mixed, the rest solidly 1-col). (4) THE WITHIN-GROUP DISCRIMINATOR (the real find): LI/SC
presence in the pane. AGH|NCEA li-carrying 3/3 vs li-less 0/6; HIS|NCEA li-carrying 5/6 (HIS1001 the
one outlier) vs li-less 0/2; MXEO|1-3 li-carrying 0/3 (the r209 canary — stays 1-col, registry-gated).
THE SPLIT POINT itself is partly editorial — AGH's three two-col golds cut 4|1, 3|2 and 1|3 — so two
KINDS were mined per group from the dominant gold pattern: **li_sc** (LI-family groups LEFT,
everything else RIGHT — the MX* families, whose golds ship `[li] | [sc]`) and **balance** (first
ceil(G/2) section groups LEFT — AGH/ANZH/HIS/CEDO/ENGR/MXFU; matches ANZH303/304/404 + CEDO105 +
HIS1005/6/8 + MXFU301/302 gold arrangements EXACTLY). Adjacent li/li runs (an LI heading + its "We
are learning to:" lead) merge into ONE section group before counting.

**The fix (DATA OVER CODE; env `INFOCOLS_OFF`).** `data/Emit_Templates.json menu.tab2_cols` — an
18-row GENERATED registry (subject|phase → `{cols: [left, right], kind}`; `--gen` emits it, never
hand-typed). `MenuBuilder`: native tab-2 content is now recorded as kind-tagged RUNS (the t1Runs
pattern; vocabulary shared with `tabs_pane1_two_col`), `#tabsPane1Partition` additionally returns the
moved LI/SC as STRUCTURED runs (`t2movedRuns`), and a composer (runs LAST of the tab-2 shapers, only
when nothing already set `tab2Cols` — the r172 moved-LI/SC and r209 learning-tab paths win first)
family-groups the runs, applies the row's kind, and fills the existing `{tab2Body}` shell slot.
FIRES only when the pane holds ≥1 li/sc-family group + ≥2 groups total and both columns end
non-empty — AGH1003/1005-9's planning-only panes correctly stay one column.

**DECLINED with measurement (recorded C / residuals):** PHE|NCEA (2/7 li-less split — editorial);
XDLS|combo (3/9, its two-col golds are li-less and byte-indistinguishable on the engine side from its
1-col siblings' panes — no derivable discriminator); BLL's 3-col overview/Knowledge/Practices form
(the r208-declined K/P family, out of the 2-col scope); SSFUN05/08 (phase-labelled panes, Claude side
empty — the funLi capture class). RESIDUALS: HIS|NCEA's row is DORMANT (Claude's HIS panes never
captured the LI/SC — a pre-existing menu-capture gap; the row fires correctly when that class ships);
gold AGH1002's "Want to know where to start?"/year-planner section is not in Claude's pane
(pre-existing capture gap); the MX*/ENGR301 golds DELETED the writer's planning/connections sections
(no WT discriminator — retained below per the r209 principle, they home on the RIGHT column);
ANZH301's swapped arrangement + AGH1001/1004's other split points = the family-form collateral
(r164 class); ENGR302's degenerate gold menu (one truncated pane) ships the family form.

**SCOPED SHIP (§10a, #6 since the last full ship — 2 of 8 headroom).** Candidate superset = all 40
gated tabs-overview modules of the 18 rowed groups (`outputs/_affected_infocols.txt`); **blast =
EXACTLY 17 modules / 17 `-00` pages** (AGH1001/1002/1004, ANZH301/303/304/404, CEDO105,

self-contradictory. The assessment tab (the part that matters most on these pages) already ships from

evidence at every solidify rung (r182): XMES|1-3 = XMES101/102/103 + XMES201's standard revision ship
the standard form (the six-tab slice is a 2-of-5 minority → defers up); XMES|4-6 = XMES202 alone

## 2026-07-10 (round 208, no build bump — measurement-only verdict) — BLL Knowledge/Practices TABS: DECLINED with measurement (Chris, r206 follow-up ticket 2)

**Plain English.** Some human-built BLL overviews show "Knowledge" and "Practices" as their own menu
tabs, and round 206 left open whether the converter should create those tabs for BLL. This round
measured every BLL module and the answer is NO — for three reasons that stack. First, half of the
human pages that show those tabs built them from content that is NOT in the Writers Template at all
(the writer never wrote a Knowledge/Practices section — the human developer authored it), and the
converter's standing rule is that it can only create what the writer's document carries. Second, among
the modules where the writer DID supply the sections, the human's own choice is a perfect 50/50 split
(5 modules promote them to tabs, 5 keep them inside the Information pane) — there is no solid
convention to ship. Third, and decisive: NOT ONE of the modules whose human page shows the tabs is in
the converted corpus — every converted BLL module's human page uses the non-tabs two-column menu with
Knowledge/Practices as in-pane headings, which the converter ALREADY matches. Adding the rule would
change zero pages today while betting on two-or-three-module evidence for the future.

**The census (`outputs/_measure_bll_kp.py`, NEW — the permanent record).** All 44 BLL2xx gold modules:
15 are tabs-overviews, 10 promote K/P (the r206 aggregate 0.64 confirmed). WT-derivability cross-tab:
KP-tab WITH a WT `[H2/H3] Knowledge/Practices` source = **BLL243, BLL247, BLL265, BLL271, BLL274** (5);
KP-tab with NO WT source = **BLL250, BLL261, BLL272, BLL273, BLL276** (5 — the r147 human-authored C
class; BLL250's combined "Knowledge and Practices" label is additionally a 1-module form); plain tabs
WITH a WT source = **BLL255, BLL257, BLL264, BLL266, BLL275** (5). Derivable-population promote share =
**5/10 = 0.50, a perfect tie** — the r182 solidify rule defers up, nothing asserts. Series level:
BLL24x 2/2 and BLL27x 2/3 promote but at n=2/n=3, below the reliability floors (MIN_MODULES 5); BLL25x
0/2 and BLL26x 1/3 keep. Gated-corpus fire population: **NONE** — the gated BLL modules (BLL241/242/
244/245/246/252/254…) all gold-ship the non-tabs two-col menu with K/P in-pane, Claude matching.

**Verdict: DECLINE — no code, no data row, no toggle, zero output change.** Revisit ONLY if the
BLL24x/27x gold-only modules join the tracked corpus (the r197 TEDC precedent, Chris's decision) —
then re-run `outputs/_measure_bll_kp.py` and judge at series level. PRIOR round below.

to 121, and every one of the remaining is a group the human genuinely keeps bilingual.

every piped heading Claude ships in a menu region (Claude is WT-faithful there — 519 headings, reo
modules excluded), each PAIRED against the human gold module's menu: the human ships the same piped

## 2026-07-09 (round 205, build 260617.80) — HTML GENERATOR V2: six browser-only UI-polish changes + the RAW-VERBATIM {CODE}_interactives.txt hand-off + a shortened plain-text interactive REFERENCE CODE (Chris, pre-commit polish)

**Plain English.** Eight changes Chris wanted before committing the converter to GitHub. Six are polish
on the browser converter's own web page; one changes what the developer-only hand-off text file captures;
one shortens the interactive REFERENCE CODE to a plain hyphenated form. NONE of them changes the DEFAULT
converted HTML pages — they are all either browser-only UI, the hand-off `.txt`, or (for the reference code)
a marker that is only emitted when someone converts with the extract switch ON, which the corpus never does.
Proven: after the work, a full regeneration of all 392 gated module folders leaves the HTML pages
**byte-identical to round 204 (0 pages differ)**, every one of the eight protected gates reproduces its
round-204 number exactly, and the extract-mode contract verifier confirms the page marker and the `.txt`
header still carry the SAME (new) reference code. The only files that change on disk are each module's
`{CODE}_interactives.txt`. **The converted modules are provably unchanged.**

**The eight changes.**
1. **Title rename** — the UI's own title now reads **"HTML Generator V2"** (the mode Chris opens it under),
   not "Converter V2": the header `<h1>`, the `<title>`, the file:// guard heading, the startup console line,
   and the `.txt` header line. Display-only — the internal class/engine names ("ConverterV2", data flags) are
   untouched.
2. **Auto-scroll to the very bottom (the "Download all" button)** — after a successful conversion the page scrolls
   to the bottom so the **"Download all as .zip"** button is guaranteed visible: when a module produces many HTML
   files their filenames can push that button off-screen, so we land on the button itself (`#download-all`,
   `scrollIntoView block:"end"`; a full-height `window.scrollTo` when the button is absent) rather than the top of
   the Output files section. Success only (never the refusal/error paths).
3. **Hide the Convert button on success** — once a module is converted the Convert button is hidden (not
   destroyed); the reset button (change 5) brings it back. It still starts disabled-until-a-file-is-added on a
   fresh page.
4. **Collapsible Conversion summary** — the summary panel is now a native `<details>`, **collapsed by default**,
   with the four headline figures shown on the always-visible header as a compact, still-labelled stat bar
   (`N pages · N interactives · N red flags · N ack-todos`). Expanding shows the full large-card summary exactly
   as before. Keyboard-accessible; no JS state.
5. **"Clear everything & convert another module" reset button** — a prominent button between the Output-files
   section and the summary panel. It resets the converter to its fresh state **in place, without reloading the
   page** (a reload would drop the user out of the embedded converter back to the site's landing view): it clears
   the uploads + file list + all outputs + the summary, hides + resets the progress bar and log, brings the
   Convert button back, resets the image-mode radios to Mode P and the extract checkbox to off, hides itself
   again, and scrolls back to the top. Shown only after a conversion completes.
6. *(folded into change 5's reset behaviour — no separate item.)*
7. **RAW-VERBATIM `{CODE}_interactives.txt`** — for the UN-BUILT interactives, the hand-off file now carries the
   raw parsed content VERBATIM instead of the round-176 processed form. Each un-built entry keeps only its minimal
   header (INTERACTIVE N of M, the extract REFERENCE CODE + hint when in extract mode, File, Placeholder marker,
   Activity, Type) and then a single `Content:` block that walks the member SOURCE BLOCKS in reading order
   (deduped by block identity) and prints each block's raw text EXACTLY — the `🔴[RED TEXT]…[/RED TEXT]🔴`
   sentinels, the `[tags]`, and the `**` markers all preserved — with a captured TABLE rendered INLINE at its
   position as the `┌─── TABLE ───/│ cell ║ cell/└─── END TABLE ───` ASCII box (which is literally the table
   block's own raw serialised text — DocxExtractor already serialises every table into that form). The
   Modifier / Tier / Data Pattern / Position / Activity Heading / Writer Instructions / Associated Media /
   Red Flags sections are DROPPED from the raw un-built entry (Chris: type + anchor + raw content only). BUILT
   entries are already omitted from the worklist, so this only affects the un-built hand-off. MEASURED FIRST
   (`outputs/_measure_manifestraw.cjs`, ENFUN05 + ENGC101): the desired ASCII table box IS the table block's raw
   `block.text`, and the writer's `[IMAGE: …]`/red words survive because they are already in the raw block text —
   no embedded-image-filename extraction is needed (that marker is writer-typed, not extracted from the docx
   binary). The multiple red spans a writer authors in ONE paragraph become several member items pointing at the
   SAME source block, so blocks are deduped by identity exactly like the round-176 faithful path.
8. **Shortened, plain interactive REFERENCE CODE** — the un-built interactive's reference code (used in extract
   mode) was long and used unusual glyphs, e.g. `⟦INT · MXDI202-01-01 · unclassified⟧`. It is now plain and
   hyphenated with `INT` moved in after the module code, and uses ONLY the first widget type (no `+ accordion +
   accordion` repeats): `MXDI202-INT-01-01-unclassified` (and `⟦INT · MXDI202-02-01 · accordion + accordion +
   accordion⟧` → `MXDI202-INT-02-01-accordion`). This is the SEARCH-BY-CODE contract, so the SAME string is
   written into the page's `cv2-int-ref` marker AND the `.txt` `REFERENCE CODE:` header (verified end-to-end);
   the bare `data-cv2-ref` id attribute stays the plain `{code}-{NN}-{seq}`. Data-driven in
   `Emit_Templates.interactive_placeholder.extract` (`ref_format: "{code}-INT-{NN}-{seq}-{type}"`,
   `label_format: "{ref}"`; the old glyph form is reverted by editing these two strings back); `ContentConverter`
   builds `type` from `bundle.type` alone. The manifest banner's example code was updated to the plain form, and
   `_verify_intextract.cjs` now expects (and passes on) the new shape. This code only appears when someone converts
   with the extract switch ON — the default inline corpus never emits it, so the standard HTML stays byte-identical.

**Data flag + env toggle (change 7).** `Emit_Templates.interactive_placeholder.manifest_raw_verbatim.enabled`
(default true) + env **`MANIFESTRAW_OFF`** revert the `.txt` to the round-176 faithful/processed form
byte-for-byte. `manifest_faithful_content` stays intact underneath as the fallback. Changes 1–6 are pure UI /
display and have no output byte to reverse; change 8 (the reference-code shape) is inherently reversible by
editing `ref_format`/`label_format` back to the glyph form, and only shows in extract mode.

**A/B toggle proof (change 7) + extract contract (change 8).** ENFUN05 regenerated with `MANIFESTRAW_OFF=1`
reverts to the processed form and is byte-identical to the round-204 `.txt` EXCEPT the single
"Generated by HTML Generator V2" header line (the intended change-1 rename) — i.e. the raw-content behaviour is
fully reversible; only the display rename persists. For change 8, `_verify_intextract.cjs` (the only gate that
exercises extract mode) PASSES with the new expected format on ENFUN05 — 21 codes in the HTML == 21 codes in the
`.txt`, all matching (e.g. `ENFUN05-INT-00-01-accordion`), deterministic, and its `--selftest` is GREEN; the
plain inline gates (below) run in inline mode and never see the marker.

**PROTECTED gates — full 392-dir regen, 0 stale, content manifest IDENTICAL (0 pages differ), ALL HELD EXACT at

1823 paired** (8-shard state-chain merge, every shard skipped 0); compare_structure exact **9250** / EXTRA **169**
/ missing **437**; body_compare ANY **272**; structural-clean **1963/2009 = 97.7%** / leak **292 occ / 46 pages**;
tags **9557/9557** / REAL FAILURES 0; flipCard **TOTAL 33 / divergence 0**; speechBubble **defect 0**; entry-parity
**PASS**; index-sync **32/27** (no engine file added — the data flags live in the already-loaded Emit_Templates.json);
extract-mode `_verify_intextract.cjs` **PASS** (new code format, `--selftest` GREEN).
