## 2026-07-09 (round 204, build 260617.79 — NO AppVersion bump) — CONSOLIDATION + COMMENTS UPGRADE VERIFIED: full-corpus regen through the one engine copy is byte-identical, all eight protected gates hold exactly

**Plain English.** Over the previous two sessions the engine was tidied and re-homed without touching any
executable code: (a) all 33 engine files had their comments rewritten (round-number references removed,
plain-English WHAT/HOW/WHY banners added, and `Config.js` cut from ~2,523 to 145 lines by deleting an
embedded duplicate of this changelog); (b) the engine was consolidated to **one copy on disk inside the
git repo** (`pageforge-site/converter-v2/`), with the dev harness `CONVERTER_V2/` reaching it through
symlinks. Neither of those can change what the converter outputs — comments and symlinks don't run. This
round PROVES it: a full regeneration of the whole corpus produces the exact same HTML, and every gate
reproduces its round-203 numbers. **No output changed, so there is no `AppVersion` bump.** The comments
upgrade — which had never been gate-tested, because the sandbox shell was down when it was made — is now
verified.

**What was proven, and how.**
- **Byte-identity (the real criterion).** A full regen of all **392 gated dirs** (compare_set's 199 +
  OSSC301 + the rest, through `batch_convert.cjs --force`, batched under the 45 s wall) followed by
  `_content_manifest.py diff` = **IDENTICAL — 0 pages differ** across all **2009** pages vs the round-203
  content manifest. 0 outputs older than the newest source (0-stale by mtime as well). Because the corpus
  is byte-for-byte the same, the eight gates reproduce by construction — they were run anyway as the
  formality:
- **PROTECTED gates — ALL HELD EXACTLY at the round-203 baseline:**
  - Index/manifest sync **32 browser / 27 node — OK**.
  - Entry-parity selftest **PASS** (static contract + BLL225 liveness + option-divergence detection).
  - Skeleton selftest **PASS**; **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD 49.3% / ≥50 913 / ≥75 173 / ≥90 12 / skipped 0**
    @ **1823** paired (scored in 4 shards of ~98 modules via `_skeleton_compare.py <codes> --json` then
    merged — the state-chain wall workaround; every shard skipped 0).
  - compare_structure exact **9250** / EXTRA **169** / missing **437** — EXACT.
  - body_compare ANY **272** (over-capture 70 / runaway 6 / empty 199) @ 2009 pages — EXACT.
  - structurally-clean **1963 / 2009 = 97.7%** / literal-`[tag]` leak **292 occ / 46 pages** — EXACT.
  - tags **9557 / 9557** HANDLED / **0** real failures — EXACT.
  - flipCard **TOTAL 33 / divergence 0** (exact 13, copy-edit 10, defect 10 — baseline held) — EXACT.
  - speechBubble **defect 0** — EXACT.

**The consolidation, recorded.** The engine now has exactly one copy on disk, in
`pageforge-site/converter-v2/`. The old locations (`CONVERTER_V2/app`, `CONVERTER_V2/data`, the root and
`CONVERTER_V2/` copies of `CLAUDE.md` + `BUILD_CHANGELOG.md`) are **symlinks** to that copy. Symlinks were
chosen over moving `CONVERTER_V2` into the repo precisely so **no code path changed** — the gates,
`_engine_load.cjs`, `batch_convert.cjs` and `_check_index_sync.cjs` all resolve the engine and corpus at
the same relative paths they always did. `publish-converter-to-site.sh` is **RETIRED** (moved to
`_Backups/pre_consolidation_2026-07-09/`) because it did `rm -rf $DEST/app`, which would now delete the
real engine; publishing is henceforth a git commit. The `.gitignore` was rewritten to track the 19 runtime
data JSONs the engine loads and ignore the 6 dev-only data files (the ~5.5 MB granular registry etc.).

**Gotcha logged (§16).** The connected folder is a FUSE mount that blocks deletes until permission is
granted. `batch_convert.cjs` deletes each output dir before rewriting, so the first regen attempt failed
silently with `EPERM: unlink` on every module (the wrapper reported them all "stale"). Granting delete
permission up front is now required for any regen.

**No new data flag, no env toggle, no `AppVersion` bump — nothing functional changed.** CLAUDE.md §4
(repository map) and §16 (working discipline) updated to describe the symlink layout and the retired
publish script.

## 2026-07-09 (round 203, build 260617.79) — HTMLGen HPFUN902 CONVERSION FIXES 1 / 3 / 4 / 5 — subject-family title, the leftover template prompt, the stray "[Dev]" note, and the menu→body comment tidy-up (Chris, published-test of the HTML Generator on HPFUN902)

**Plain English.** Chris published-tested the converter (now the "HTML Generator" mode in the PageForge 1.5 website) on module **HPFUN902** and found five conversion bugs. This round ships the **four gate-neutral ones** (the header title, a leftover writer prompt, a stray empty note, and tidying developer comments); the fifth — two missing phase panels/tiles caused by the writer gluing the panel-break markers into a big instruction block — is genuinely deep and skeleton-visible, so per Chris's decision it lands as **its own next round (204)**.

## 2026-07-08 (round 202, build 260617.78) — MODE-OPENER FORWARD MERGE — the empty `[Activity individual]`/`[embedded]` box merged into the numbered activity (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 21 — classO ACTIVITY OVER-GENERATION, backlog item 5)

**Plain English.** A lesson writer often types a "mode" label before a real activity — `[Activity individual]`
("do this on your own") or `[Activity embedded]` ("an interactive lives here") — then the box's title, then
the numbered activity itself: `[Activity individual]` → `[H3] Which rights were taken?` → `[Activity 1A]`.
The human developer builds ONE grey activity box (numbered 1A) with the heading as its title inside. Our
converter was splitting it into TWO boxes: the mode label opened an empty-ish box (just the title), which
the numbered opener then auto-closed, before opening a second box for the content. This round merges the
pair into one, matching the human — the empty mode box disappears.

**THE MEASUREMENT (first product — `outputs/_measure_activityboxes.py`; reports
`_activityboxes_report.md` + `_activityboxes_rows.jsonl`):** counted `<div class="activity">` boxes gold
vs Claude for ALL 392 paired modules, joined to a WT classification of `[Activity …]` openers (numbered /
mode-word / bare).
- **Over-generation is NOT corpus-wide.** Corpus-wide Claude ships **FEWER** activity boxes than gold
  (5,349 vs 6,863 = **0.78×**). Over-boxing is **concentrated in ~25 modules** and splits into several
  DISTINCT mechanisms — there is no single "over-box" rule:
  - **MODE-WORD** (the biggest, ~15 modules): an un-numbered `[Activity individual]`/`[embedded]`/`[body]`
    opener makes an empty box. HIS1004 alone had **38 empty-ish boxes** (title-only, no content); the human
    ships none.
  - **BARE-`[Activity]`+black-number GROUPING** (XDLS903-906/908/909/901): the writer numbers with black
    text after the bracket (`[Activity]` then `1A`) and the human GROUPS a Learn/Explain/Do triad into ONE
    `dropbox` — a separate, intricate convention.
  - **Fundamentals gold=0** (MXFUN02/03, BLL155): the content belongs in panels, not activity boxes.
  - **XGF9004** modal-quiz grouping; **MXFL203** numbered-heavy.
- The MODE-WORD triad `[Activity individual]` → `[H3] title` → `[Activity NX]` is the clean, provably
  derivable slice: gold ships ONE box numbered from the `[Activity NX]`, the `[H3]` its title inside
  (triangulated on HIS1004-01 gold `<div class="activity … number="1A">` → `<h3>Which rights…</h3>` inside).

**THE FIX (DATA OVER CODE; env `ACTMODEMERGE_OFF`; data `activity_wrapper.mode_opener_merge`).** The
round-84 consecutive-opener merge only skips BLANK lines between the two openers; this extends it to skip the
box's own TITLE HEADING(s) (`max_intervening_headings` 1 — the HIS1004 shape is exactly one `[H3]`). In the
activity `CONTAINER_OPEN` branch, when this opener is un-numbered (`!myId`) with no content of its own
(`!myContent`), peek forward past blank lines + title headings for the next un-consumed NUMBERED activity
opener; if found, adopt its id (`it._activityIdOverride`) and mark it `consumedBy = "activity-mode-merge"`,
then open ONE box HERE (so the heading lands inside). The consumed numbered opener renders only its own lead
into the open box, opens no second box, and does not auto-close (a dedicated handler beside the round-160
`activity-super-content` skip). **GENERAL** — keys on "un-numbered activity opener with empty content", not
a per-module word list; XDLS's `[Activity]`+black-number is EXCLUDED BY CONSTRUCTION (`number_from_tail`
leaves the number in `blackAfter` → `myContent` true). A standalone mode opener with no numbered follower is
left as its own box (a separate, measured follow-up).

**FULL SHIP (resets the cadence; the scoped-5-of-8 backstop was due).** 392 dirs regenerated, `_stalecheck.sh`
**0 stale**. `_content_manifest.py diff` = **14 modules / 50 pages changed**; A/B decomposition (regen the 5
box-count-unchanged modules with `ACTMODEMERGE_OFF`): **10 are the fix** (ANZH301/304/404/203, HIS1003/1004,
SSFUN02/05/06/08) and **4 are pre-existing shared-corpus drift** (AGH1003/AGH1009/BLL122/ENGR302 — `OFF==ON`,
the round-76/201 drift class). Box counts moved toward gold: HIS1004 95→69, HIS1003 66→50, SSFUN02 41→27,
ANZH301 50→39, **ANZH304 42→25 (gold 21)**, **ANZH404 21→12 (gold 10)**, SSFUN06 42→31, SSFUN08 22→17,
SSFUN05 22→14; ANZH203 a clean 10→9 (the `[Activity individual]`→`[H3] Cultural exchanges`→`[Activity 3C]`
trio). Toggle-OFF byte-identical to the r201 baseline on the changed modules (proven on HIS1004/ANZH301/
HIS1003/SSFUN02 + 5 controls, incl. `_run.json`/`_interactives.txt`).

**PROTECTED gates — ALL HELD-or-IMPROVED** (skeleton via the state-chain merge `outputs/_r202_sk_merge.py`,
the r191–r201 recipe; the r201 sanity reproduces 49.236%/912/173/12 EXACTLY):
- **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD 49.236% → 49.279% (+0.043pp)** / RAW 34.345→34.376% / **≥50 912 → 913 (+1)** /
  ≥75 173 / ≥90 12 / **skipped 0** @ 1823 paired. A/B on the 84 changed-module pages: **39 up / 8 down / 37
  flat, net +79.3pp**. The 8 dips (worst HIS1004-04 −8.38pp) are the r176/r186 NET-POSITIVE class — an EMPTY
  activity-box wrapper node that coincidentally matched gold's skeleton is removed; **visible text is
  char-identical** OFF↔ON (HIS1004-04 4685 == 4685 chars, only 2 empty wrapper divs gone).
- **compare_structure exact 9249 → 9250 (+1)** / EXTRA container **169** / MISSING container **437** —
  IMPROVED/HELD, **no new MISSING** (removing spurious wrappers did not delete a box the human keeps).

## 2026-07-08 (round 201, build 260617.77) — infoTrigger SPLIT-BRACKET re-stitch — recovering the hover-definition markers that leaked as literal text (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 20 — backlog item 4, the §15 lever)

**Plain English.** When a lesson writer marks a word for a hover pop-up definition (a "rollover") —
e.g. `herbivorous [definition: Plant eating.]` — and the marker is split across coloured spans, our
converter used to leak the raw `[definition: …]` bracket straight onto the page instead of making the
hover-word. The human developer weaves it into `<span class="infoTrigger" info="Plant eating.">herbivorous</span>`.
This round recovers those on the pages where the marker sits in ordinary body text or a plain table.

**THE MEASUREMENT (first product — `outputs/_measure_infosplit.py` + `_measure_infosplit_verdict.py`
+ the item-stream probe `_probe_infosplit_leak.cjs`; report `outputs/_r201_measurement.md`):**
- The hover/rollover/definition family has **428 raw literal `[…]` leaks across 111 modules** — but
  **389 of them (91%) are TRAPPED inside un-built-widget cv2 placeholder dumps** (the human built the
  widget as live content with hovers; the converter left the whole widget as an orange placeholder, so
  its raw markers dump into the box). A free-body re-stitch cannot reach those — that is the
  widget-building backlog. The brief's "~761 gap / ~108 modules" was counting these 428. The headline
  example **ENGJ302 ("41 leaks") is 41 dump / 0 visible**.
- The honest, fixable **VISIBLE free-body footprint = 39 leaks / 19 modules**; the scanner's existing
  round-75/82/86 weave already handles the reachable red-tag bulk (174 openers in those 19 modules, 39
  leak). The item-stream trace showed the leaks arrive as BLACK items (`[Rollover definition for TERM:
  DEF]`, HIS1002), a `definition`-head data-marker tag (ENGJ301), or a free-body table cell (CEDO501) —
  NOT clean red tags an existing tweak reaches; the round-146 note had deferred the "for TERM" named
  anchor to "this round (queue 5)".

**§0A APPROVAL GATE:** presented the plain-English summary + the affected-module list + the reconciliation
(the mechanism is a black-text/table render weave, not a red-tag extension), and Chris chose **"attempt
full class"** (recover the ~26 stitchable across the 3 mechanisms). Only then did any code change.

**THE FIX (DATA OVER CODE; env `INFOSPLIT_OFF`; data `elements.hover_definition_inline.render_stitch`).**
A render-level `ListsAndRuns.hoverStitch(text)` weaves any hover/rollover/definition marker that reached
the FINAL free-body text as a literal, inserting the same U+E000…U+E001 sentinel `#inlineMarkup` already
turns into `<span class="infoTrigger" info="DEF">anchor</span>`. Run at the top of `renderBlackText`
(FULL multi-line text — so a cross-line `[… for manslaughter: DEF]` finds "manslaughter" in the prior
sentence) and `inlineMarkup` (table cells + headings). Anchor = the LAST whole-word occurrence of the
`for/on TERM`, else the word immediately before the marker. Separators `: = – —`; heads
hover/rollover/roll-over/mouseover/**definition**. Reuses the round-146 hygiene (instruction-def + URL
decline) and the round-82 "trigger" exclusion; a marker with no clean anchor/def is LEFT as the
pre-existing literal — never a wrong weave, never a NEW leak.

**CONTAINMENT — the key correctness catch.** `contentTable` routes even cv2-dump cells through
`inlineMarkup`, and the un-built placeholder dumps text via `renderBlackText` (L3864) — so a naive
universal placement over-fired into the 389 trapped leaks (~111 modules, corrupting the developer
hand-off). Fix: a `stitch` flag (default true = free-body) that is set FALSE for cv2-placeholder /
built-widget content — `contentTable` passes `!insidePlaceholder` to the cell `inlineMarkup`; the dump's
`renderBlackText` (L3864) + the InteractiveBuilder render callbacks pass `false`. So the 389 trapped
markers are untouched BY CONSTRUCTION (proven: ENGJ302/MXDI301/HIS1001/CEDT501/CEDW501/TEFUN02 all
regenerate byte-identical to r200).

**THE SET: 12 modules changed** (ARFUN05, CEDK501, CEDO501, CEDR501, ENGJ301, HIS1002, HIS1005, PHE1007,
SSFUN01, SSFUN06, SSFUN07, TWHA903). Declines/residue LEFT as-is (footprint's other 7): bare `[definition]`
(XDLS905/904, TEFUN07), writer instructions (CEDO501-07 copyright, HIS1002-13 "please have three tabs",
ANZH104), a URL "click this link" def (AGH1007), a heading-anchor ARFUN03, a standalone long-quote def
(HIS1004). SSFUN06 + BLL155 also carry PRE-EXISTING shared-corpus drift (round-76 class; SSFUN06's fix
contribution is exactly its 2 hover lines, BLL155 has no hover content).

**PROOFS (scoped ship §10a, #5-of-8):**
- **Toggle-OFF byte-identity:** the 12 regenerated `INFOSPLIT_OFF=1` revert byte-identical to the r200
  manifest (only the pre-existing SSFUN06/BLL155 drift remains).
- **Containment:** `_content_manifest.py changed` = the 12 (+ BLL155 drift); cv2-heavy hover modules
  byte-identical; the current-corpus footprint shows only declines remain (no un-woven weavable
  free-body leak) → the affected set is complete. No stray U+E000/E001 sentinels corpus-wide.
- **Gates ALL HELD-or-IMPROVED** (skeleton via the state-chain merge `outputs/_r201_sk_merge.py` →
  `_r201_affected_on.json`; the chain reproduces the r200 baseline EXACTLY as sanity): **`A_literal_tag_leak`
  305 → 292 occ / 49 → 46 pages (the required drop); structurally-clean 1960 → 1963 / 2009 = 97.7%**
  (HIS1005 52→50, its 2 free-body leaks woven, the 50 cv2-dump untouched); PRIMARY skeleton **49.232 →
  49.236% / ≥50 912 / ≥75 173 / ≥90 12 / RAW 34.342 → 34.345% @ 1823 skipped 0** (A/B +6.83pp on the 85
  changed pages, 4 up / 6 down / 75 flat — CEDK501-08 +4.23, HIS1002-16 +2.61; the small downs are the
  r164/r176 net-positive class); compare_structure exact **9249 / EXTRA 169 / missing 437** EXACT (inline
  spans never touch the wrapper chain); body_compare **273** EXACT; tags **9557/9557**; flipCard **33 /
  div 0**; speechBubble **defect 0**; index-sync **32/27**; entry-parity **PASS**. **AFTER-PROOF: Claude
  infoTrigger spans 550 → 573** (+23); visible free-body footprint **39 → 16** (all 16 remaining are the
  declines/residue above).
- **Follow-ups (recorded):** the 389 cv2-dump-trapped hover markers = the widget-building backlog (a
  built widget with hovers, not this round); ARFUN03's cross-structure heading anchor; HIS1004's
  standalone long-quote def; the SSFUN06/BLL155 pre-existing drift. Backlog advances to **item 5: classO
  ACTIVITY OVER-GENERATION (24 modules)**.

Data `elements.hover_definition_inline.render_stitch`; env `INFOSPLIT_OFF`. Files: `ListsAndRuns.js`
(hoverStitch + `#lastWordIndex` + the `stitch` param), `TablesAndGrids.js` (cell `!insidePlaceholder`),
`ContentConverter.js` (dump/built-widget `stitch=false`), `Emit_Templates.json`, `Config.js`. PRIOR round below.

## 2026-07-08 (round 200, build 260617.76) — VIDEO ICON: the videoSection `icon` play-button styling — a per-SUBJECT/SERIES house style shipped where it SOLIDIFIES (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 19 — backlog item 3)

**Plain English.** When the human developer embeds a video, they wrap it in a `videoSection` box and,
on many pages, add a small `icon` styling (a play-button / thumbnail look). Our converter always
shipped the plain box, so it never matched that look. This round MEASURED whether there is a reliable
rule for WHEN the human adds the icon, then applied it only where the data solidly supports it. The
answer: it is a per-SUBJECT/SERIES HOUSE STYLE (some subjects are consistently icon, some consistently
plain), NOT a per-video choice — so we add the icon on videos in the subjects/series that solidly use
it, and leave the genuinely mixed subjects plain.

**THE MEASUREMENT (first product — `outputs/_measure_videoicon.cjs`, a pure gold-HTML read of every
`videoSection` in all 392 paired modules, cv2 lane decomposed out, joined to each module's derivable
context; full tables `outputs/_videoicon_report.md`; per-video rows `_videoicon_rows.jsonl`):**
- **Gold ships 2536 icon / 1992 plain (56% icon) across 4528 videos.** The make-or-break stat:
  **82% of video-carrying modules are internally PURE** (182 all-icon / 126 all-plain) vs 65 MIXED —
  the choice is per-module, not per-video.
- **No per-video rule exists.** On the 65 mixed modules, every candidate rule (first-video-on-page,
  first-in-module, in-carousel, in-activity-box, media-kind) predicts 56–59% — the always-majority
  baseline is 58%. Carousel/position/media-kind are all dead (confirming the session-5 finding).
- **The r182 solidify verdict per grouping level.** The signal is a per-SUBJECT/SERIES house style,
  SOLID in some groups and a genuine near-tie in others. STRONG icon: Arts/English/Social-Science
  Fundamentals (97–100%), the BLL phonics series BLL11–17 (92–98%), History (97%), PE (98%), several
  Maths/English series, ANZH (85%), EXPlore Inquiry (82%). STRONG plain: Online Safety (17%), Te
  Marautanga Bilingual (7%), Leaving-to-Learn (21%). NEAR-TIE (do NOT solidify → stay PLAIN): Blended
  Literacy|Standard 51%, English|Standard 53%, ConnectED|Inquiry 61%, HPE|Fundamentals 62% — shipping
  icon here would blanket-iconify many pure-plain modules (the r199 near-tie decline pattern).

**THE DECISION (Chris-approved via the §0A pre-change approval gate, 2026-07-08): the CONSERVATIVE
ship — icon ONLY where a group is strongly solid** (a SERIES with n≥3 modules at pooled share ≥0.85,
else a SUBJECT|TEMPLATE with n≥5 at ≥0.80). Chris was presented the affected-module list + the
alternatives (full decline; the aggressive r182-0.60 version, which he/we rejected as the near-tie
hazard) and chose the conservative ship.

**THE FIX (DATA OVER CODE; env `VIDEOICON_OFF`; data `video.icon_rule`).** A mined group-level registry
(the Menu_Scaffold / rich_panes.registry precedent — a corpus-consensus data list, never per-module
code, never reading gold at conversion time): `icon_series` (15 series: ANZH10, ART10, BLL11–17,
ENGI10, ENGI20, HIS10, HPFUN10, MXFL20, PES10) + `icon_subject_template` (5: Arts/English/SocSci
Fundamentals, ANZH|Standard, EXPlore|Inquiry). `MediaBuilder.media` POST-REPLACES the class token
`videoSection ` → `videoSection icon ` (mirroring the existing videoHost `.replace` at MediaBuilder
L111 — so the shared video templates + the InteractiveBuilder/carousel builders that reuse them stay
byte-identical) when the run's module (series/subject|template from `Module_Structure_Index.module_meta`)
is in a list. A group not in a list keeps the default plain form.

**THE SET: 115 icon-group modules; 79 actually emit a `videoSection` and changed** (the other 36 emit
zero — un-built widgets — so the fix is a harmless no-op there, incl. HIS1001 + 4 of the 5 collateral).
Collateral (accepted, documented net-positive per §6 / the r164 class): 5 pure-plain modules ship a
gold-absent icon — ANZH404, BLL171, BLL172, BLL174, EXPFUN06 (only ANZH404 emits any videoSection);
plus the plain videos inside the mixed ANZH|Standard modules (ANZH301). **MAGNITUDE CORRECTION (honest
record): the +1163 projection was over GOLD videoSections; Claude UNDER-emits (many gold videos are
un-built placeholders), so the real change is 519 icons added, at a BETTER Claude-side correctness
(~526 right / ~24 wrong ≈ 96%).** The module set + collateral are unchanged, so the approval stands.

**PROOFS (scoped ship §10a, #4-of-8; the change is contained-by-construction to the icon groups):**
- **Containment:** `_content_manifest.py changed` = exactly 79 modules, ALL ⊆ the 115 icon set (nothing
  leaked outside — the rule fires only in its groups).
- **Toggle-OFF byte-identity:** 6 changed modules regenerated `VIDEOICON_OFF=1` reverted to the r199
  manifest byte-for-byte (the toggle is faithful; the last-shipped corpus IS the toggle-OFF state).
- **Outside-group no-op:** OSAI501/ENGC102 (non-icon groups) regenerated fix-ON = byte-identical to r199.
- **Census after-proof:** classV Claude videoSection icon **0 → 519** (Standard 360 / Fundamentals 138 /
  Inquiry 21 / Bilingual 0), 79 modules.

## 2026-07-08 (round 198, build 260617.74) — HEADER TITLES stage 1: the classT h1-COUNT slice — the missing second-language (Te Reo Māori) title heading (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 17 — backlog item 2 OPENS)

**Plain English.** The page header's most visible element is the title block: the module code chip plus one `<h1>` per language. On 66 paired modules the human's gold page carries a DIFFERENT NUMBER of title lines than ours — almost always a Te Reo Māori title we never ship. This round measured, module by module, whether that missing title actually EXISTS anywhere in the Writers Template — and shipped it wherever it does, without ever inventing one where it does not (the round-80 "only ship what's real" rule).

**THE MEASUREMENT (first product — the D2 chrome census REBUILT FRESH post-r197, then `outputs/_measure_titleh1.cjs` over ALL 430 module dirs through the live pipeline, gold/Claude h1 sets joined from the census):**
- **The 66 h1-count modules decompose:** **57 = recorded C** — the Te Reo title is in NO part of the WT (body, tables and front matter all searched; the ENGC102 human-added class). **4 = gold outliers, declined** — gold itself ships boilerplate or junk as an h1 ("MODULE TITLE TE REO" OSOH501, "Te Reo Māori Translation" ENGS202, a duplicated "Working together as one" PHE1004, ANZH101's "2 Genealogy Title Lorem Ipsum Dolor") — we keep correctly not shipping those. **1 = a gold text edit** (HIS1004 subtitle truncation → the text-diff pile). **The derivable slice = the 7 shipped modules below.**
- **The adjacency truth (live-probed item streams):** the second-language title hides in FOUR WT shapes — (a) a Māori-language BLACK line directly after the `[TITLE BAR]` payload (AGH1006 `**Te whakatō tipu kākāriki**: Te whakahaere hātepe ahumāra` — gold splits the colon pair into TWO h1s; AGH1005 same shape); (b) the embedded RED title + a black payload that is a bare pipe-HALF (`[TITLE BAR] Whakaaro Auaha` + `| Thinking creatively`, TEFUN03 — the r76 black-preferred rule shipped the half and LOST the embedded language); (c) a no-primary RED SPAN directly after the title bar holding the other half — pipe-leading (`| Tangata Whenua Pūrākau`, ANZH101) or a bare red `|` separator span whose OWN blackAfter carries the Te Reo (MXFL104, a mid-paragraph red span) or the mirror form where the PAYLOAD dangles the trailing pipe and the span is the half (`*ONLINE @HOME |*` + red `Ngā whakahaeretanga ā-ipurangi i te kāinga`, OSOH301); (d) PES1002's payload carries the literal boilerplate "Te reo Māori translation needed", which we SHIPPED as an h1 (the one claude>gold module — gold drops it).
- **Every arm's fire surface measured to exactly the named modules** (the Māori-adjacent-line population = AGH1005+AGH1006 with over-fire ZERO corpus-wide; pipe_lead_black = TEFUN03 + ANZH401 whose pipe-half is placeholder boilerplate → dropped downstream, byte-identical; pipe-sibling = ANZH101 + MXFL104; dangling-pipe = OSOH301 alone; the placeholder string = PES1002 alone). The measurement lens ALSO caught its own composition gap: MXFL104's Te Reo lives in the '|' span's blackAfter, invisible to the single-item lens — live re-probing of the whole 24-module unresolved-span pool closed the census.

**THE FIX (data `header.title_split.te_reo_line` + `header.title_split.split_payload_join` + one placeholder-list string; env `TEREOLINE_OFF` + `TITLESPANJOIN_OFF`; the string rides the r76 `placeholder_title_rule`/`TITLEPH_OFF`):**
- **te_reo_line** (`ContentConverter.#partitionItems`): when the payload yielded a single (English) title, the FIRST non-empty item after the title bar being a BLACK line that passes the round-80 Māori-alphabet letters test (never mtkFlag) and is title-sized (`max_words` 20) becomes the Te Reo title source; the line is CONSUMED (it stops rendering as body/menu text — the r148/r187 capture precedent). A single-colon line splits into the gold PAIR (`titleBar.teReoLines`, rendered as consecutive h1s by `SkeletonBuilder.#buildHeader` — the r86 two-h1 shape extended to a list).
- **split_payload_join** (same branch): `pipe_lead_black` re-joins the embedded red title with a pipe-leading black half; `pipe_sibling` absorbs the adjacent no-primary red span (text AND blackAfter) when the span leads with `|` OR the payload dangles a trailing `|` — an awaiting-translation note span is never absorbed (boiler guard). The joined payload then splits on the pipe like any normal bilingual title; a JOINED 2-part payload with exactly ONE Māori-lettered half assigns ENGLISH FIRST (gold ships EN-first on TEFUN03/ANZH101/OSOH301; ALSO keeps `#pageEnglishTitle` English so the r80 overview heading de-dup still fires; scoped to joined payloads only — the dash/char split paths keep payload order, CEDW501 gold ships Te Reo first there).

ANZH101's lesson pages 01-03 also drop the leaked `CS: | Tangata Whenua Pūrākau` note (gate-excluded class; gold ships none).

**The fix (data `body_region.fundamentals_panels.phase_text.accordion_delimiter`; env `FUNPANACC_OFF`; `FUNDPHASE_OFF` still reverts the whole phase-text machinery).** FOUR coupled pieces, all gated by fundamentals body_class + single-file + the registry row (`XFUN|combo`, the r166/r187/r188 lookup): **(1) scanner SUPPRESSION (the novel seam)** — `InteractiveScanner.#accordionPhaseForm` at the ScanPage invocation gate: an accordion-primary INTERACTIVE invocation on a gated page never opens a bundle (numbered/bare left unconsumed for the pre-pass; counts toward `phaseLineCount`, 9 ≥ 2); the bare `[accordion]` opener + the closers (bracketed `end accordion` CONTAINER_CLOSE + the bracket-less instruction form, `noop_patterns`) → consumed no-ops; blackAfter preserved everywhere (measured 0 carriers — belt-and-braces). **(3) the THIRD nav/tile dialect** — `PanelsBuilder.#phaseTextDialect` on the ptsent branch, driven by the registry row: nav labels = each panel's FIRST heading (the r111/r188 extractor, faithful text; fallback "Phase {n}"), tiles = ALL phases (incl. 1) in ONE `row phaseContainer noPhase` row of `col-md-4 col-6` tiles with `alt="Phase N"`, tile img = panel-first-img with intro fallback; a NO-row module (TEFUN/SCFUN/ARFUN/ENFUN…) takes the r106/r113 path byte-identical. **(4) leftover handling** — `link_dissolve_pattern` (`^\[?link to\b`): an unconsumed cross-reference marker dissolves to its blackAfter prose (gold keeps the prose, drops/edits the links — the 3 pre-round orphan RED FLAGs go, none added); ## 2026-07-08 (round 190, build 260617.66) — THE PRIMARY SKELETON GATE REPAIR — the 238-pair raw-crash blind spot CLOSED + the skeleton baselines RE-STATED over the TRUE population (Chris's session-8 pick, STOCKTAKE session 9; a TOOLING round — ZERO converter-output change, manifest-proven; the r189 "NEW FINDING" charter).

**Plain English.** The PRIMARY gate (`reference/tests/_skeleton_compare.py`) has been silently ignoring **238 of the 1,806 comparable page pairs (~13%)** — whole modules' pages never counted toward the skeleton score. Cause: the human gold's hand-built HTML writes `<div class="accordion" layout>` — a `layout` attribute with NO value. Python's html.parser stores a bare attribute's value as **None**; the skeleton labeller's guard (`a[k] != ""`, `_structural_skeleton.py` L81) passed None into `.strip()` (L82) which threw AttributeError, and the gate's `except Exception: continue` (L65) dropped the pair with NO trace — a raw-pass crash removed it from BOTH the raw AND scaffold stats. The fix: a bare attribute now contributes nothing to the label (the measured-right form), the gate COUNTS and PRINTS skipped pairs so a silent drop can never recur, a `--selftest` proves both, and the skeleton baselines are re-stated over the true 1,806-pair population (the r104/r186 fresh-baseline pattern).

**MEASURED FIRST (`outputs/_measure_skelcrash.py` over all 1,806 gate pairs, acks/glossary excluded):** bare KEEP_ATTR attributes corpus-wide = **379 occurrences, ALL gold-side, ALL `layout`** — 374 on `div.accordion` + 3 accordion variants (`accordion.margB0`, `accKeepOpen.accordion`, `accordion.wordHighlighter`) + **1** `<div class="row convoStarter" layout>` (gold SSFUN05_0.0.html L1251 — the ONLY bare attr outside a WIDGET_MARKERS subtree, i.e. the only scaffold-visible site); CLAUDE-side bare attrs **0**; predicted crash set == the real `match(scaffold=False)` AttributeError set **238/238 EXACT** (`outputs/_skelcrash_pairs.txt`, 125 modules — MXFL301 ×9, HIS1004/MXDB302 ×8, XGF9006 ×7 …); scaffold-mode sample crash-free (widget subtrees collapse to the WIDGET marker BEFORE `label()` runs — why the r189 A/B could score the ENFUN pages scaffold-only). **Patch form chosen by measurement:** **(b) skip-bare** (`if k in a and a[k]`), NOT (a) render-`[layout=]` — Claude's built accordion opens `<div class="accordion">` with no `layout` attribute at all (`Emit_Templates.interactive_builders.accordion.open`), so under (b) the paired nodes AGREE (a bare attr means "default layout", zero structural information) while (a) would manufacture a `[layout=]` token on 374+ gold nodes that Claude can never match; gold's VALUED `layout=standard/speech/column/paragraph` renders exactly as before; `""` was already skipped pre-190, so None is the ONLY behavioural change.

**THE FIX (`_structural_skeleton.py` `label()` + `_skeleton_compare.py`):** **(1)** the one-line guard `a[k] != ""` → `a[k]`. **(2)** the pair loop factored into `_score_pairs()`, which COUNTS skips — every gate run now prints **`pairs skipped (parse error): N`** (+ the first 10 with exception text; `skipped_parse_errors` added to the `--json`) — **N must be 0**; any future parse crash shows up loudly in every run (the r149 vacuous-gate discipline; never remove the line). **(3)** **`--selftest`**: LIVENESS — a synthetic bare-attr fragment must SCORE ratio 1.0 vs its attr-less twin, `label(Node("div",{"layout":None})) == "div"`, and a valued attr must still render `[layout=speech]`; DETECTION — a raising pair must land in the skipped count, never hidden — **PASS**. **Importer audit:** `anchor_compare.py` mentions the tool in a comment only; `_fastloop_diff.py`/`_fastloop_snapshot.py`/`_gatecheck.py`/`run_all_gates.sh` consume the gate as a subprocess + `--json` (existing keys unchanged, one added — safe); NO other gate imports `label()`/`render()`; `_structural_defect_audit.py` re-verified clean (does not call them); `outputs/_audit_fix_queue.py` + `_measure_stocktake_skeleton.py` are DIAGNOSTICS that import `skeleton()` (they now see more pages — diagnostics may move, protected gates may not).

**ZERO output change PROVEN:** no `app/js`/`data` edits (Config.js AppVersion comment only); `_content_manifest.py diff` = **IDENTICAL, 0/1990 pages**. The html-reading gates re-run EXACT at the r189 baselines: structural-clean **1941/1990 = 97.5%** / leak **305 occ / 49 pages**; compare_structure exact **9173** / EXTRA **157** / missing **436**; body_compare ANY **265**. tags/flipCard/speechBubble/entry-parity/index-sync untouched by construction (no converter change, no verifier change).

**THE RE-BASELINE (OLD 1568-pop vs NEW true-pop, side by side — the protected numbers move by POPULATION HONESTY, not by any page's score changing):**
- OLD (238 pairs invisible): SCAFFOLD mean **50.4%** / ≥50% **817** / ≥75% **164** / ≥90% **11** / RAW **35.7%** @ 1568 paired.
- **NEW (TRUE population — the protected baseline from this round): SCAFFOLD mean 49.2% / ≥50% 905 / ≥75% 168 / ≥90% 11 / RAW 34.4% @ 1806 paired, skipped 0.**
- Sanity: the previously-scored 1,568 pages recompute to EXACTLY the r189 baseline (50.39% / 817 / 164 / 11 / RAW 35.71) — the patch is a no-op for every previously-scoring page (a page carrying a bare attr ALWAYS crashed, so the two sets are disjoint by construction). The re-admitted 238 score SCAFFOLD mean **41.4%** (≥50%: 88, ≥75%: 4) — widget-heavy AGH/ENFUN/MXFL/HIS-class pages, honestly below the corpus mean, which is exactly why hiding them flattered the old number. Ran as 6 module-chunks merged (`outputs/_r190_sk*.json` + `_r190_sk_summary.json`; the per-page union == a single full run by construction — the gate scores pairs independently).

**Files:** `reference/tests/_structural_skeleton.py` (label guard), `reference/tests/_skeleton_compare.py` (`_score_pairs` + loud counter + `--selftest` + json key), `app/js/Config.js` (AppVersion). **Tools:** `outputs/_measure_skelcrash.py` (the class probe: bare/valued attr survey, side/tag incidence, prediction==reproduction), `outputs/_skelcrash_pairs.txt` (the 238), `outputs/_r190_sk_summary.json` (the new baseline record). **Env:** none — a diagnostic-tool patch with no output shape (the `*_OFF` convention covers OUTPUT shapes; the pre-190 behaviour is recoverable from this entry). **Follow-ups:** the fastloop baseline `baselines/skeleton.json` stays deferred-stale (since r176) — the next `_fastloop_snapshot.py` bakes the true population; the D2 census is html-side and unaffected; the queue resumes at the class-P sibling dialects (ARFUN first, untangling ARFUN04's class-O over-generation).

## 2026-07-08 (round 185, build 260617.61) — D0: HARNESS↔APP ENTRY PARITY — the two conversion entries unified at ONE choke point (Chris, HPFUN903; the MASTER-STOCKTAKE campaign's top-priority workstream, session 1). Byte-identical corpus by full-regen proof; a NEW protected gate guards the contract.

**Plain English.** On 2026-07-07 Chris ran HPFUN903 through BOTH conversion paths and got different results: the local-server app produced ONE file (the human gold's single-file shape); the node batch harness — what every protected gate, baseline and dev round has measured since the beginning — produced TWO. The engine, the data files and the input `.docx` were identical (Chris confirmed corpus copies, fresh serve + hard refresh, default settings). The divergence was the two ENTRY SEQUENCES: `App.js` and `batch_convert.cjs` each ran their own copy of the prep steps, and they had drifted. **(1) `run.mtkFlag`** — batch sets it from the document's "MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE" house header (round 129); **App.js never set it at all.** That flag is one arm of the `_reoMode` disjunction in `PageSplitter` (L137), `ContentConverter` (L138) and `InteractiveScanner` (L86/L597) — and since 374/390 WTs carry the house header (the round-167 finding: it is the house template name, NOT a bilingual marker), the harness has been converting ~357 non-bilingual modules in reoMode while the app converted them standard. ## 2026-07-06 (round 184, build 260617.60) — OVERVIEW-MENU ONE-LINE "TITLE + CONTENT" SPLIT — the dropped "Understand" recovered (Chris, ENGR202-00). A menu (`#header`-scoped) fix, shipped SCOPED (§10a) behind a data flag + two env toggles.

**Plain English.** ENGR202's overview menu (a **tabs** menu) has three curriculum headings — Understand / Know / Do — and the writer put **Understand's content on the SAME LINE as its bold title**: `[H2] **Understand:** Literature, language, and texts embody power relationships.` Know/Do put their content on the following lines. The result: Claude **dropped the whole "Understand" column**. Root cause: the whole line rendered as ONE heading (`<h4>Understand: Literature…</h4>`) with its content glued *inside* the heading, so the very next line was another heading (Know) and `#dropEmptyHeadings` nuked Understand as "a content-less scaffolding heading." This is EXACTLY the round-109 failure mode — but round 109 fixed it only for the `two_col_li` menu path; the **tabs** path had no curriculum split at all. The fix splits the bold **title** from the non-bold **content** (title → the heading, content → a following `<p>`) so the heading can never be dropped, using a method proven most reliable across the whole corpus.

**Triangulated (Chris's mandate).** raw WT `[H2] **Understand:** Literature, language, and texts embody power relationships.` → human `ENGR202_0.0.html`: `<h4><span>Understand</span></h4><p>…</p>` in the LEFT `col-md-6` (the human editorially rewrote the prose — non-derivable; we reproduce the STRUCTURE) → Claude `ENGR202-00.html` (round 183): the LEFT col STARTED at `<h4>Know</h4>` — Understand gone (0 occurrences). CEDW101 (all three one-line) was a SECONDARY spot-check but is a DIFFERENT mechanism (its overview menu is entirely SUPPRESSED — no `#module-menu-content` at all — not a same-line drop); recorded as a separate follow-up, NOT fixed this round.

**THE METHOD — measured corpus-wide BEFORE coding (`outputs/_measure_menu_title_split.py`).** (a) A corpus **heading LEXICON**: every human overview `#module-menu-content` h3/h4/h5, folded → count — **222 overview menus / 1,787 occ / 105 distinct; 61 headings ≥3× cover 96.8%** (learning intentions 190, understand 153, do 153, know 152, how will I know 96, success criteria 73, planning your time 67, i can 44, assessment for learning 41, kia tika/kia mārama 36, technical precision 36, …). (b) The **target class** (an overview `[H#]` = **bold title + non-bold content**, non-bilingual): **253 occ / 147 modules**, dominated by understand/know/do (249). (c) The **most-reliable signal**: the **bold→non-bold boundary is the PRIMARY split point**; the trailing colon confirms **97%**, the lexicon recognises **98%**, `two_col_li.left_match` (understand/know/do) **98%**; the mid-title-colon trap Chris flagged is **0 occurrences** (preferring the bold boundary over the colon handles it for free). (d) The **bilingual GUARD** (a top-level `|` or an all-bold trailing half = a Te-Reo|English title, LEFT to the round-142/145 reduce): a large population (1,305) → must guard.

**The fix — data-driven, two independently-reversible toggles (DATA OVER CODE).** (A) A corpus **frequency lexicon** `data/Overview_Menu_Heading_Lexicon.json` (the "database" — a GENERAL vocabulary of heading STRINGS, never keyed by module code, never reads a module's own gold; the LEVEL-0 guardrail), built by the new `reference/tests/build_menu_heading_lexicon.py` (dynamic paths + `--selftest`; keys folded per `Utils.Fold` + trailing-colon strip so the engine lookup matches). Loaded via `Config.DataFiles` + `_modules.json` `data_map` (32 browser / 27 node, index-sync OK). Env **`MENUHEADINGLEX_OFF`** ignores it (falls back to colon + `left_match`). (B) `MenuBuilder.#splitTitleContent` + the tabs branch: on an OVERVIEW tabs heading, split `**Title:** content` when there is a bold→non-bold boundary with REAL non-bold content, it is NOT bilingual, AND the title is confident (colon-terminated **OR** lexicon ≥ `min_count` **OR** `left_match`); routing then reads the **TITLE** (`hFold`), not the content prose, so a body mention of "connections"/"assessment" can't mis-route the heading to tab 2. An ambiguous / no-boundary / bilingual line is **KEPT WHOLE (never dropped)**. Data flag `menu.tabs_pane1_curric_split`; env **`TABCURRICSPLIT_OFF`** reverts to the round-183 content-glued heading. The `two_col_li` path (round 109) is untouched — BLL/ENGC eng_family overviews proven byte-identical.

**Scope — measured, bulletproof.** Affected superset = **151 modules** = the strict `[H#]`-tagged one-line scan (147) ∪ the bracket-lenient generous scan (MXFU402, XWHA02) ∪ the malformed-bracket overviews round-174 repairs live (ANZH404, ENGC101, ENGR201). Regenerated the whole 151 WITH THE FIX ON; the manifest byte-diff shows the fix **actually changed EXACTLY 33 modules, ALL on the `-00` overview page** (0 lesson pages) — a genuinely narrow class (most candidates are `two_col_li` = round-109-handled, or have their content on a separate line = never glued). The 33: AGH1007/1008, ART1003, ENG1005, ENGJ201/202/301, ENGR202/301, HES1005, HIS1002, MXDB102/302, MXDI102/103, MXEO102/202, MXEX301, MXFL103, MXFU302/401, PES1008, PHE1001/1003/1004/1005/1006, XDLS502/902/903/905/906/908.

**Gate safety — gate-NEUTRAL, ships on the VISIBLE human match (the round-125/171 precedent).** The overview menu is `#header`-scoped → INVISIBLE to `compare_structure`/`body_compare`/the defect audit, and the PRIMARY skeleton's **SCAFFOLD** view *collapses* the menu's repeated `<h4>+content` blocks, so the recovered heading is scaffold-INVISIBLE too. A/B (`TABCURRICSPLIT_OFF`, drift-immune, the 33 changed modules): skeleton **SCAFFOLD 0.00 delta** (every one of 209 pages identical) — but the RAW skeleton (widget-internals visible) confirms the fix ADDS the human-matching `h4`+`span`+`p` nodes on every changed overview (ENGR202 raw +2.0, ENGJ202 +3.7, MXFU401 +4.5, …), NET ≈ 0 because a few overviews' recovered `<p>` meets the human's editorially-varied rendering (e.g. MXFU302 faithfully keeps the WT whakataukī `<b>` the human trimmed — non-derivable, verified clean HTML, not a bug). **PROTECTED gates (full-corpus DIRECT runs, ALL HELD-or-IMPROVED):** PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD **mean 50.64% / ≥50% 832 / ≥75% 169** (HELD, 1567 paired); compare_structure exact **8299** / EXTRA **147** / missing **382** (EXACT); body_compare ANY **336** (EXACT); structural-clean **1971/2022 = 97.5%** / leak **318/51** (EXACT); tags **9557/9557**; flipCard **TOTAL 33 / divergence 0**; speechBubble **defect 0**; index-sync OK (32/27); precedence parity **1504/1504**. **SCOPED SHIP (§10a):** content-hash 0-stale (151 affected fresh, 236 unaffected byte-identical); containment (**33 changed ⊆ 151 affected**); completeness spot-check (**12/12** non-affected byte-identical); toggle invariant (`TABCURRICSPLIT_OFF` → ENGR202-00 byte-identical to the round-183 manifest, md5 `e4204f7f…`). Content manifest refreshed to the round-184 byte state; ship ledger #3 of 8 (5 headroom). The fast-loop baseline stays deferred (since round 176; the DIRECT full-corpus gate runs above are authoritative — the round-176/183 precedent). **Data:** `Overview_Menu_Heading_Lexicon.json` (new) + `Emit_Templates.menu.tabs_pane1_curric_split`. **Env:** `TABCURRICSPLIT_OFF` + `MENUHEADINGLEX_OFF`. **Docs:** CLAUDE.md (both copies) §11 (two toggles) + §14 (snapshot). **Follow-ups (recorded, not built):** CEDW101's suppressed overview menu (a menuTypeFor / menu-not-emitted class, distinct from this drop); the long-tail non-curriculum one-line titles (Technical Precision / Whakataukī) where a tabs overview carries them (the lexicon already recognises them — a sizing follow-up if any appear).

## 2026-07-05 (round 182, build 260617.58) — CASCADE → 6 LEVELS (Chris's canonical walk-levels) + the SOLIDIFY-or-defer-up rule.

**Plain English.** Chris corrected the walk-level order and re-asserted the founding principle of the original style-anchor registry. **(1) The order.** The canonical walk-levels are `doc14 → existing related module (series + TEMPLATE) → subject+phase+template → subject+template → subject → corpus` — **six** levels. Two changes from round 181's seven: level 2 gains the **template** constraint (the module this one continues from must share the *series and the template*, not just the series number), and the standalone bare-**phase** rung (prefix + first digit, e.g. `BLL2` across all templates) is **removed** — "phase" now only lives *inside* `subject+phase+template` (the year-level within a subject+template). **(2) The solidify rule.** The original registry only ever recorded a templated value for a grouping when that value was *solidly* consistent there; if the group was ambiguous (a 50-50 split, or fragmented with no dominant value) the attribute was **omitted** and the code deferred up a rung. Round 181's "plurality wins (any unique top, even ~20%)" was too loose. This round restores the registry's discipline: a consolidation level asserts a value **only** when it is solidly dominant (module-share ≥ `solidify_share` = 0.60 **and** not a tie); otherwise it is omitted and the cascade **climbs a rung** (a coarser group has more data and usually solidifies).

**Measured (`outputs/_measure_cascade.py`, 10,472 pairs).** New distribution: L1 doc14 87 / L2 series+template 2,802 (26.8%) / L3 subject+phase+template 2,001 (19.1%) / L4 subject+template 540 / L5 subject 134 / L6 corpus 207 / **ESCALATE 4,701 (44.9%)**. The escalate rate rising from round 181's 8% to ~45% is **by design and correct**: the cascade now refuses to assert a rule where the pattern is not solid (fine-grained body structure — headings/images/quizzes in genuinely varying wrappers — is `unsolid` at every level, so it correctly escalates rather than inventing a rule from a weak plurality). This is the honest "there is no derivable template here" verdict Chris wants; those elements defer to the human gold (level 0) / a human decision. `solidify_share` (0.60) is the single calibration knob if a stricter/looser "solid" is wanted.

**Code.** `data/Precedence_Cascade.json`: 6 levels; L2 `series_template` (sibling chain, temporal, same series + same template); consolidation levels `decision:"solidify"` + `solidify_share` + `tie_defers_up`; `_meta` documents the new order + the solidify rule; `reliability_defaults.solidify_share` added. `granular_consensus.py`: `group_members` gains the `series_template` grouping; `_consensus` implements `solidify` (omit + defer on a tie or a sub-floor top-share); `_group_label`/`_resolve_note`/`cascade_selftest` updated (all 6 levels + the solidify-defer proof: BLL111 `body|body` is `unsolid` at subject+phase+template, defers up, solidifies at subject+template). `PrecedenceResolver.js` mirrors all three (JS↔Python resolve parity **EXACT 1504/1504**). `vet_issue.py`: `CLEAN_PRECEDENT` + `_ev_line` + the selftest updated to the new authority names; BLL244 now widens to L3 `subject_phase_template_consensus` (`human_outlier`, ONE-OFF HUMAN OUTLIER — solidly, 89% of 27).

**Gate safety.** Checker/diagnostic + inert-engine round. The engine still ships INERT (`engine_inherit.enabled:false`) → the corpus is **byte-identical** (`_content_manifest.py diff` = 0 pages) → every protected gate HOLDS by construction. Verified: `_check_index_sync.cjs` OK; parity 1504/1504; `--cascade-selftest` / `--granular-selftest` / `vet --selftest` / `subject_parameters --selftest` ALL PASS; `CASCADE6_OFF` still reverts to the round-179 model. **Data:** `Precedence_Cascade.json` → 6 levels + `decision:"solidify"`. **No new env toggle.** **Docs:** CLAUDE.md (both copies), `reference/Human_Gold_Is_The_Per_Module_Target.md`, and the three `EXPLAINER__*.html` updated to the 6-level order. **Follow-up in progress:** a full **granular commonality assessment** (`outputs/_measure_granular_commonality.py`) — semantic attributes (menu tab count, tab labels, per-tab headings, column counts, headings) compared at each grouping with the same solidify/omit rule, plus the corpus-wide constants that never need the cascade.

## 2026-07-05 (round 181, build 260617.57) — CASCADE → 7 LEVELS: the subject+phase+template consolidation + the tie-defers-up rule (Chris, review of the round-180 cascade).

**Plain English.** Two refinements to the authority cascade, both from Chris's read of how the fallback should actually consolidate. **(1) A missing fallback level.** When a module has no series predecessor, round 180 widened from its own *prefix's* phase (e.g. BLL2 = only the BLL modules at year‑2) straight to "same template in the whole subject." But **17 of 19 subjects span multiple prefixes** (English = ENFUN/ENGC/ENGI/ENGJ/ENGR/ENGS; Blended Literacy = BL/BLL/CODE/STL), so that jump skipped the obvious fallback: *the sibling product lines in the same subject, at the same year-level and the same template.* Measured, this matters — where such a widen was possible, the prefix-phase majority **differs from the subject+phase majority in 16% of cases** (119/739). **(2) How a level confirms an authority.** A consolidation level should form its authoritative template from the **most commonly rendered** build (a plurality — how the original style-anchor registry worked), and — the one guard Chris named — whenever **two variations are documented by the same number of modules**, that level cannot confirm a single winner and must **defer up** to the next layer, never pick arbitrarily.

**The cascade, now 7 levels** (`data/Precedence_Cascade.json`, DATA OVER CODE): doc‑14 → **series** (prefix+2, temporal sibling chain) → **phase** (prefix+1, temporal) → **subject+phase+template** (NEW — same subject × same year-level × same template) → **subject+template** → **subject** → **corpus**. Stop at the first level that confirms an authority; **widen on a silent OR tied level**; ESCALATE only when every level is silent/tied and doc‑14 is silent.

**The tie / plurality rule.** The five consolidation levels (phase, subject+phase+template, subject+template, subject, corpus) now carry `decision:"plurality"` + `tie_defers_up:true`: the single most-common sig wins; if the top-2 sigs have **equal module counts** the level returns `tie` and the cascade widens up. This replaces the round-180 `≥0.60 majority_share` floor for those levels. Effect (measured `outputs/_measure_cascade.py`, 10,472 pairs): **ESCALATE 47% → 8%** — an authoritative template is now confirmable in the large majority of cases (the point: there is nearly always a single most-common build to inherit), and a true escalation happens only when a group is genuinely split down the middle or empty. New distribution: L1 87 / L2 2847 / L3 929 / **L4 (subject+phase+template) 2607** / L5 1315 / L6 372 / L7 1502 / ESCALATE 813.

**Code.** `granular_consensus.group_members` gains the `subject_phase_template` grouping (same subject + same year-digit + same template, all modules); `_consensus` implements plurality + tie-defers-up (data-driven via the level's `decision`/`tie_defers_up`); `_group_label` + `_resolve_note` name the new level. `PrecedenceResolver.js` mirrors all three (the JS `Counter` tie-break uses a stable count-desc sort, matching Python `most_common`). `cascade_selftest` now proves **all 7 levels** are the decider for a real fixture (L4 = AGH1001 header|@h1 → NCEA1·level 1·Standard), **the tie rule fires** (AGH1002 body|summary ties at subject+phase+template), and a true **ESCALATE** still exists (AGH1001 header|alert, empty/thin at every level).

The engine still ships INERT (`engine_inherit.enabled:false`), so the corpus is **byte-identical** (`_content_manifest.py diff` = 0 pages) and every protected gate HOLDS by construction. ## 2026-07-05 (round 180, build 260617.56) — THE 6-LEVEL PRECEDENCE CASCADE, END-TO-END (Chris — the full authority cascade, wired into BOTH the discrepancy-checker AND the converter engine). Round 179 introduced precedence-first adjudication with only THREE levels (doc-14 → nearest sibling → whole corpus); this round replaces it with the full SIX and takes it into `ContentConverter`.

**Plain English.** A module inherits its structure from the **nearest previously-developed work**, and the search only widens when the nearer level has no clean answer — the corpus-wide average is the **last** resort, never the first. The one override is the per-subject **global parameters (doc 14)**. Round 179's 3-level model was too coarse: when a module's own tight series was internally inconsistent (BLL244's `BLL24x` = col-md-8/12/6/12/12/6), it jumped straight to *escalate* — skipping the perfectly good **phase-level** house-style that sits between the series and the corpus. The six levels insert those intermediate authorities so a mixed series **widens** to the next-nearest precedent instead of giving up.

**The cascade — the exact order (data/Precedence_Cascade.json; DATA OVER CODE):** for module `M` + element `E`, walk top-to-bottom and STOP at the first level with a CLEAN answer:
1. **doc-14** — a per-subject global parameter governing `E`, within its scope (OVERRIDES everything below).
2. **series** — the previously-developed modules in the tight series (prefix+2 digits, e.g. `BLL24`), nearest-first; a single clear predecessor decides, a mixed nearest-window widens.
3. **phase** — previously-developed same-phase-in-subject modules (prefix+1 digit, `BLL2`), by majority.
4. **subject+template** — all same-template-in-subject modules (Standard/Inquiry/Fundamentals/Bilingual), by majority.
5. **subject** — all same-subject modules (the learning area), by majority.
6. **corpus** — all modules, by majority (the last resort).
A MIXED / empty level WIDENS (it never averages); **ESCALATE** only when NO level is clean and doc-14 is silent. So **BLL244** now WIDENS past its mixed series to settle at **L3 (phase `BLL2`, col-md-6, 93% of 27)** — a confident `human_outlier` verdict where round 179 could only escalate; **AGH1006** decides at **L2** (clean series, its sibling AGH1005 built col-md-8).

**Measured, first (the disciplined loop; `outputs/_measure_cascade.py`).** `resolve()` over all **10,472** (module, element) pairs: L1 doc-14 **87** · L2 series **2,847 (27%)** · L3 phase **550** · L4 subject+template **1,709 (16%)** · L5 subject **163** · L6 corpus **214** · **ESCALATE 4,902 (47%)**. The high escalate rate is CORRECT — most fine-grained body structure (headings/images/quizzes in wildly varying wrappers) genuinely has no structural precedent, and the cascade honestly refuses to guess (the project's long-standing "editorial variation" finding). Every one of the six levels + escalate is the decider for a real corpus case (the acceptance proof).

**WS1 — the substrate.** `build_granular_registry.py --merge` now also records **per-module metadata** in `data/Module_Structure_Index.json` (`module_meta`: subject, template_type = the corpus folder, prefix, phase, series, dev_order = the code-number proxy for "previously-developed"). Rebuilt from the cached shards (fast; the registry itself is byte-identical). The `modules` dict is unchanged.

**WS2 — the resolver.** `granular_consensus.resolve(code, key)` walks the six levels, filters `Module_Structure_Index` per level (temporal for series/phase, all for subject+template/subject/corpus), applies the reliability floors, widens on empty/mixed, and returns `{level, authority, reference, reference_sig, majority_share, n_modules, confidence, escalate, note, tried}`. The 3-level `adjudicate` is refactored to call `resolve` (its old body kept verbatim as `_adjudicate_legacy` for `CASCADE6_OFF`).

**WS3 — the checker.** `anchor_compare.consensus_reading` (→ `adjudicate` → `resolve`) and `vet_issue` name the deciding LEVEL + reference; a discrepancy `ESCALATE`s only when all six are silent/mixed and doc-14 is silent. Re-run: BLL244 → `ONE-OFF HUMAN OUTLIER` decided at the phase level (evidence: "the series had no clean precedent, so the same-phase house-style (BLL2) decides — col-md-6, 93% of 27"); ENGS102 tab → outlier; a genuinely un-precedented element → `ESCALATE — NO CLEAN PRECEDENT`.

**WS4 — non-vacuous selftests.** `granular_consensus.cascade_selftest()` (wired into `anchor_compare --granular-selftest` / `--cascade-selftest` and `vet_issue --selftest`) proves EACH of L1–L6 is the decider for a real fixture, doc-14 OVERRIDES at L1, and a real element ESCALATES — and FAILS if any level is unreachable (the round-149 discipline). ## 2026-07-05 (round 179, build 260617.55) — AUTHORITY MODEL CORRECTED: SIBLING PRECEDENCE IS THE FIRST PORT OF CALL (Chris, screenshot review of the round-178 debugger). The corpus is a last resort, not the first.

**Plain English.** Chris reviewed the round-178 debugger explainer and caught a real inversion: it led with the *corpus-wide majority* as the deciding factor ("92% of the library uses two columns → the AI is wrong"). That is backwards. A module **inherits its structure from the previously-developed module it continues from** — exactly as a developer copies the last sibling — so **that sibling is the authority, and it outranks the whole rest of the library.** In Chris's words: if the current module (say MDLE102) continues from MDLE101 and MDLE101 uses one column, then even if 389 other modules use two columns, the AI producing one column is *correct* — the converter has correctly emulated the predecessor. **The ONLY thing that overrides a previously-developed module's structure is the per-subject GLOBAL PARAMETERS (doc 14)** — the most recent, finalised instructions. The corpus average is only ever a labelled fallback of last resort. This round fixes the vetting/consensus logic AND the explainer to that authority order.

**Measured, first (the disciplined loop).** The round-178 headline case actually *proves* the point: BLL244's own series (BLL24x) is genuinely inconsistent — BLL240=`col-md-8`, 241=`col-md-12`, 242=`col-md-6`, 244=`col-md-12`, 245=`col-md-12`, 246=`col-md-6`. So there is **no clean sibling precedent** for BLL244; the honest verdict is *escalate to the subject's global parameters / a human*, not a confident corpus-majority "human outlier." The corrected tool now says exactly that.

**The authority order, implemented:**
1. **doc-14 global parameters** (within scope) — override everything.
2. **sibling precedence** — the nearest previously-developed module in the same series. A single clear predecessor **outranks a 389-module corpus majority**.
3. **corpus consensus** — a labelled fallback, only when the two above are silent. A series that is itself inconsistent yields **ESCALATE**, never a corpus guess.

**Code.** (a) `build_granular_registry.py` now also emits **`data/Module_Structure_Index.json`** (1.03 MB, 389 modules) — every module's built ancestor-ladder signature for every element, retrievable per module (Chris's explicit "granular data for every module, down to the smallest element/attribute, stored and retrievable"). (b) **`granular_consensus.adjudicate()`** is the new precedence-first verdict: `predecessors(code, key)` (nearest-lower in the tightest series band) + `precedent()` (is the recent window consistent, or is the series mixed?) → doc-14 → clean sibling → `sibling_precedence_mixed` (escalate) → corpus fallback. The round-178 `STRONG_SHARE` corpus guard is retained but demoted to the fallback layer. (c) `anchor_compare.consensus_reading` now calls `adjudicate` (precedence-first) and the evidence string names the **sibling reference** ("matches sibling AGH1005 built col-md-8"), not a corpus %. (d) `vet_issue` reorders the verdict: **doc-14 first**, then sibling-precedence bug/outlier, then a new **`ESCALATE — NO CLEAN SIBLING PRECEDENT`** verdict for inconsistent series; the vet `--selftest` now proves all three (clean precedent → confident; mixed series → escalate; tab-label still caught). (e) both `EXPLAINER__*.html` files rebuilt: the discrepancy file's interactive is now an **authority ladder** (set "what did the previous module build?" + a doc-14 override, and watch the sibling outrank the corpus), and the pipeline file's step 6 is "check the previous module in the series" not "ask the whole library."

**Gate safety.** A TOOLING/DIAGNOSTIC round — the **engine (`app/js`) LOGIC is untouched** (only `Config.js` `AppVersion` bumped, UI-only), and the new `Module_Structure_Index.json` is **not read by the engine** (grep-proven). Converter output is byte-identical to round 177/178, so **every protected gate HOLDS at the round-177 baseline by construction** (no regen). Verified: no `app/js` logic modified; all 4 `--selftest`s PASS; `anchor_compare --regress` PASS; `_check_index_sync.cjs` OK. **New data:** `Module_Structure_Index.json`. **Follow-ups (measured, deferred):** wire a per-series precedent for menu **tab labels** (ENGS102 still uses the corpus positional norm as a fallback); refine "which module does this one continue from" beyond nearest-lower-number when a series has parallel strands; wire doc-14 governance into `consensus_reading` (currently layered only in `vet_issue`).

## 2026-07-04 (round 177, build 260617.53) — BILINGUAL TITLE SEPARATOR: the slash `/` split + the orphan-separator cleanup (Chris, ENGS401-00). The general fix for a whole class, not one module.

**Plain English.** ENGS401's title bar reads `Responding to Texts / Te whakautu i ngā kuputuhi` — an English title and its Te Reo translation with a **slash** between them. The human developer ships these as **two** separate `<h1>` titles; the converter combined both languages into **one** `<h1>`. Chris asked — pointedly — for the *reason* this happened to be fixed generally, not just this one screenshot: "dissect the REASON… look at the code in a very pragmatic way… so this type of situation can be avoided… when ANY TAG or ANY ELEMENT or ANY SCAFFOLDED SECTION is being converted." This round does that.

**The root cause — an ASYMMETRY (the same shape as round 174's bracket bug).** The title splitter handles a fixed set of separators: pipe / line-break / 2-space (split unconditionally), and — behind the round-86 "exactly one half carries a Te Reo macron" guard — a sentence-punct pair, a spaced dash, a colon, and an ALL-CAPS/te-reo case transition. The slash was **recognised in the code, but only DEFENSIVELY**: `#titleHasOtherSep` and `#bilingualDashSplit` both list `/` as a separator that must make the *other* splitters BAIL — yet **no splitter ever ACTED on it**. So a slash-separated title fell through every branch to a single combined `<h1>`. A signal known to one consumer (the "bail" list) but not another (the "split" list) is exactly the class of bug that keeps recurring here (round 174: `Parse` repaired a dropped bracket for classification, but `RenderText` still leaked it). The durable fix is to make the two lists **ONE source of truth**.

**Triangulated (ENGS401-00).** Raw WT: `[TITLE BAR] … *Responding to* *Texts**/**Te whakautu i ngā* *kuputuhi*`. Human gold: `<h1><span>Responding to Texts</span></h1>` + `<h1><span>Te whakautu i ngā kuputuhi</span></h1>`. Claude before: `<h1><span>Responding to Texts/Te whakautu i ngā kuputuhi</span></h1>` (one combined). Claude after: **exactly the human's two `<h1>`**.

**Measured corpus-wide BEFORE coding (`outputs/_measure_title_separators.py`, all 376 WTs).** The full separator landscape confirms the general convention — a bilingual `[TITLE BAR]` is one `<h1>` per language, split on its separator (human split-rate: pipe 86%, slash 91%, dash 100%, punct 100%). The SLASH class is 12 payloads: the macron guard would newly split **8** (ENGS401, CEDK101, ANZH203, ENGI201, MXFL202, MXFL301, SSFUN05, SSFUN08), with **0 FALSE-SPLITS** (it never fires on a title the human keeps as one `<h1>` — e.g. SSOG103 `… / TE REO` placeholder stays single). The 3 "misses" (SSFUN06/MXDB301 = **macron-less Te Reo**, ENGI401 = a placeholder half) stay single — the SAME documented guard limitation the dash/colon/case splitters already have, single today and single after, 0 regression (recorded C). This **reclassifies slash from C (non-derivable) to B (derivable convention)**, exactly as round 86 did for the dash — and the stale `non_derivable_note` is updated to say so.

**FIX 1 — the general single-char splitter (`ContentConverter.#bilingualCharSplit`; data `header.title_split.bilingual_marker_split.char_separators`; env `TITLESLASH_OFF`).** The single-char soft separators now live in ONE ordered DATA list — `[ {sep:"/", flag:"slash", off:"TITLESLASH_OFF"}, {sep:":", flag:"colon", off:"BILINGUALMARK_OFF", bail_other_sep:true} ]` — that the ONE splitter iterates: the first that occurs exactly once and yields a macron-guarded bilingual pair wins. **Adding a future single-char title separator is now a DATA edit — the defensive/offensive asymmetry cannot recur.** The round-168 colon FOLDS IN unchanged (keeps its "any other separator ⇒ not mine" bail via `bail_other_sep`); slash is ordered first (outranks colon) and deliberately does NOT bail on internal dashes, so ENGI201 `Connections – … / Nga Hononga – …` still splits on its top-level slash. Byte-identity of the fold proven: **0 modules carry both `/` and `:`**, and the 3 colon+spaced-dash titles resolve to single either way.

**FIX 2 — the orphan-separator cleanup (the completion; data `header.title_split.strip_boundary_separators` = `"/"`; env `TITLESEPTRIM_OFF`).** When a writer typed a slash ALONGSIDE a hard separator — `Visual Literacy /  Mātau Reo Ataata` (slash + TWO spaces) — the hard-separator branch split first and left the slash ORPHANED on a half (`Visual Literacy /`). After the split each half now has a leading/trailing separator char (from this data string) trimmed. **Provably human-matching: the human ships 0/405 title `<h1>` with a boundary separator** (`outputs/_measure_title_orphan_sep.py`). The edge regex touches only a leading/trailing separator (never one internal to a half), so it also cleans a SINGLE-title orphan (ENGI401 `A Moment in Time /`, whose Te Reo half is an unfilled placeholder) while never disturbing intentional internal punctuation (`TV / Radio` keeps its slash). **Deliberately scoped to `/` this round** — the ORPHAN-DASH class (XDLS909 `Living In Aotearoa –`, BLL246 phonics) and the TRAILING-COLON class (PES1001 `Column Addition:`, XLP02 `*:`, a heading mis-captured as a title) are SEPARATE pre-existing bugs with their own root causes, NOT swept in here (add their chars to the data string only after measuring each class).

## 2026-07-04 (round 176, build 260617.52) — INTERACTIVE HAND-OFF CAPTURE: faithful content + the backward lead-pair absorb (Chris, ENGC101-02). Two toggled fixes so the un-built `{CODE}_interactives.txt` worklist captures EVERYTHING the writer configured for the developer.

**Plain English.** When the converter meets an interactive it can't yet build (a speech-bubble set, a set of true/false pop-outs…), it leaves a placeholder and writes the captured details into `{CODE}_interactives.txt` — the hand-off the human developer reads to build the widget. Chris spotted that this hand-off was **losing information** on ENGC101-02. Two separate problems: (1) the "Content" it captured had dropped the writer's **red-highlighted words** — which for this activity ARE the answer (the adjectives *big, blue, stripey, cold, curious, excited*) — and had thrown away the `[Speech bubble]` tags, leaving gap-riddled fragments like "There are two / fish and lots of / fish."; and (2) it had **missed the very first line** of the interactive — the lead-in label "We can use words to describe what we see:" — because the capture only starts running *downward* from the first `[Speech bubble]` tag, and that first label sits just *above* it. Chris asked for a general fix: once the code notices a repeating pattern (a lead-in line, then an interactive tag, repeated), it should also look **upward** from the first tag to recover the matching pairing it stepped over. Both are now fixed, each behind its own reversible switch.

**Fix 1 — FAITHFUL CONTENT (`ManifestBuilder`; data `interactive_placeholder.manifest_faithful_content`; env `MANIFESTFAITHFUL_OFF`).** The round-138 capture rendered each member's `blackAfter` (the black text *after* the tag), which silently dropped the interleaved red-highlighted spans and the bracketed tags. Now the "Content:" block is rendered from the members' **unique source blocks** (deduplicated, in reading order), cleaning only the `🔴[RED TEXT]` sentinels + `**` markers via the existing `#clean`. So brackets, red words and full sentences all survive. ENGC101-02 Content now reads `[Speech bubble] There are two big, blue fish and lots of stripey fish.` etc. — exactly the writer's line. **txt-only → invisible to every protected gate + the HTML content manifest** (round-159 precedent).

**Fix 2 — BACKWARD LEAD-PAIR ABSORB (`InteractiveScanner.#absorbLeadingPattern`; data `_meta.member_rule.leading_pattern_absorb`; env `INTLEADPAIR_OFF`).** The general "detect a repeating pattern, then walk UP to recover the missed first pairing" Chris described. After `#swallowMembers` captures a bundle forward, the members are collapsed to a per-source-block token string (`W`=interactive tag, `L`=standalone black label, `O`=table). **Only** on a STRICT clean widget-first alternation (`^W(LW)+$` — ≥2 widgets, one label per interior widget, no L-runs, no tables) does it extrapolate the unit backward: it walks up over UNCONSUMED black items whose **label signature** (data-driven `label_signatures`, first match wins: num / alpha / colon / bullet / url / prose) equals the **dominant interior-label signature** — Chris's "similarly structured" — and are label-like (never free prose or a URL), capped at exactly the MISSING count (=1 here) and at a word count near the interior labels (never a body paragraph). Matched labels are prepended to `memberItems` and `startIndex` is moved back (the ownership loop then consumes them; the placeholder + the txt then include the recovered label). `inline_only` (an activity-owned bundle's `startIndex` is the `[Activity]` tag, whose predecessor is section content — a sized follow-up).

**MEASURED corpus-wide (`outputs/_measure_intleadpair.cjs`, ALL 390 WTs — never `compare_set` only).** 559 "label-precedes" bundles exist, but the strict alternation + similarity guard is deliberately tight: it fires on **exactly 7 bundles / 2 modules** — ENGC101-02 (speechBubble, colon labels) and XGF9004 ×6 (modal true/false series, numbered labels). **MXEX302's carousel** (interior "label" is a twinkl URL, the line above is body prose "As you prepare your graph…") and **every already-consumed "above"** (XGF9004-09's Philosophy quiz, whose lead sits in a sibling bundle) correctly DECLINE — proving the guard's precision. Authoritative HTML blast radius confirmed by the SHIPPED engine (`outputs/_detect_intleadpair.cjs`, all 390) = the same 2 modules, and by byte-diff (`_content_manifest.py changed`) = exactly ENGC101 + XGF9004.

**A/B (drift-immune) + gates (full 390-dir regen, 0-stale by mtime, HTML changed = exactly ENGC101 + XGF9004; all 388 others byte-identical).** `INTLEADPAIR_OFF` reverts the 2 modules byte-identically to round 175 (the scoped-ship toggle invariant holds). **Every protected gate HELD-or-IMPROVED:** compare_structure exact **8299** / EXTRA **147** / missing **382** (EXACT); body_compare ANY **336** (EXACT); structurally-clean **1971/2022 = 97.5%** / literal-`[tag]` leak **318 occ / 51 pages** (EXACT); tags **9557/9557** (0 real failures); flipCard **TOTAL 33 / divergence 0**; speechBubble **defect 0** (ENGC101's own bubbles correctly stay un-built — the absorb captures, it does not build); PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD **mean 50.6% / median 51.1% / pages ≥50% 832 / ≥75% 169** — pages≥50% and ≥75% both HELD. The ONLY movement is the continuous skeleton MEAN: **−0.00029 pp corpus-wide = ENGC101-02 −0.45pp alone** (60.45→60.00, still ≥50%), a **coincidental text-stripped `<p>`-node match lost** — the human FUSES the label into the bubble-content `<p>` (`<p>We can use words to describe what we see:<br>There are two…</p>`, no standalone label node), so folding the label into the widget is the CORRECT direction; the skeleton had rewarded the old standalone `<p>` by coincidence. Documented NET-POSITIVE per §6 (the round-61 / 74 / 115 / 164 class). XGF9004's 6 pages show 0.000 skeleton delta (the moved node lands inside the collapsed widget). Full ship recorded in `_ship_ledger.py`; content manifest refreshed (fastloop baseline refresh deferred — a >45s re-score; the direct full-corpus gate runs above are authoritative).
