## 2026-07-04 (round 175, build 260617.51) — SCOPED SHIP (Chris): the ship step can now rebuild ONLY the modules a change actually affects. Process/tooling round — ZERO converter-output change (byte-for-byte round 174).

**Plain English.** When we ship a converter change, the final safety check rebuilds every module (all ~390) even when only a handful actually change. Chris asked: can the ship step rebuild only the modules a change actually affects, the way the fast inner loop already does — including for tag-level changes like round 174, which today are forced to a full rebuild? This round delivers that as a **scoped ship**: rebuild only the affected set, PROVE every other module is byte-for-byte identical to the last ship, and read the exact protected-gate numbers off the fast-loop baseline — no full-corpus regen. The full ship (`ship.sh`) stays as a periodic backstop. **This round changes no HTML at all** — the corpus is byte-identical to round 174 (proven by `outputs/_content_manifest.txt`); what changes is how few modules we rebuild to prove that.

**Why it's rigorous, not a shortcut (the completeness argument).** Every fix in this project ships behind an `*_OFF` env toggle whose whole purpose is to reproduce the exact pre-change output. So the **previously shipped corpus IS the toggle-OFF state**, and a change whose guarded code path only fires where the Writers Template matches some pattern `P` is a **provable byte-for-byte no-op on every module that does not match `P`**. The complete affected set is therefore *every* module whose WT matches `P` — a total guarantee, not a sample, *if* the detector for `P` is complete. Scoped ship then proves that completeness three independent ways (containment, a sampled spot-check, and the exact decomposition gate proof), with a periodic full-ship backstop bounding any residual risk.

**What was built (all in `reference/tests/`, plus one detector in `outputs/`).**
- **`scoped_ship.sh --affected <file> --toggle <NAME>`** — the scoped ship checkpoint. Phases: (0) assert the `*_OFF` toggle EXISTS (a fix without a faithful toggle can't be scoped-shipped — the safety invariant); (regen) print the pre-sized `_batch_plan.py` lines for the affected set + the spot-check sample; then under `--no-regen`: (1) content-hash freshness, (2) **containment** — the set that ACTUALLY changed (byte-diff vs the last-ship manifest) must be ⊆ the detector's set, else FAIL "under-scoped → use `ship.sh`", (3) **completeness spot-check** — a random sample of NON-affected modules must be byte-identical under the fix (a mis-specified `P` is caught here), (4) the exact decomposition gate proof (`_fastloop_diff`), (5) `--commit` refreshes the baseline + manifest, (6) the periodic-backstop cadence check.
- **`_content_manifest.py`** (deliverable C) — an md5-per-page content manifest (the golden-manifest pattern of rounds 149–158, made a permanent per-ship artifact): `snapshot` / `diff` (→ changed modules) / `changed` / **`fresh`** — the content-hash 0-stale check that **defeats the mtime false alarm** (round 148's "stale-by-mtime but byte-proven inert"): affected modules must be regenerated (mtime, scoped to them only), every OTHER module must be byte-identical to the manifest (mtime ignored). A module is "truly stale" only if its inputs changed OR its output differs from the manifest.
- **`regen_affected.cjs` v2** (deliverable A) — added `--wt-regex "<pat>"` (a regex over each module's parsed WT — for a tag-level trigger the old rendered-marker mode could only classify corpus-wide) and `--from-list <file>` (consume a round's measurement probe output verbatim: "the probe IS the detector"), plus a 60% corpus-wide guard that routes universal changes to the full `ship.sh`.
- **`_scoped_spotcheck.py`** — the completeness spot-check (`plan`/`verify`); **`_ship_ledger.py`** (deliverable D) — records full vs scoped ships and requires a full ship every N (cadence 8 / hard 16); **`_fastloop_diff.py --commit`** — the scoped baseline refresh (patch the affected modules into the baseline + refresh the manifest, exact by decomposition); **`ship.sh`** now refreshes the content manifest + records the full ship in the ledger.
- **`outputs/_detect_bracketfix.cjs`** — the COMPLETE round-174 detector: it runs the SHIPPED `DocxExtractor.RepairContentTags` guard over EVERY module's WT (all 390) and reports where the repair fires — a guaranteed superset of the modules whose output changes, complete by construction.

**A KEY FINDING (why the detector must scan the whole corpus).** The round-174 measurement probe (`_measure_malformed_brackets.cjs`) scanned only the 197-module `compare_set`, so it enumerated **36** affected modules and **missed ENGC101 — the very module the fix was named for** — because ENGC101 sits outside `compare_set` in the full 390-dir corpus. The complete detector finds **51** (ENGC101 + 14 others the probe never saw). A scoped ship driven by the probe's 36 would have shipped a stale, broken ENGC101; the containment byte-diff and the completeness spot-check both catch exactly this (demonstrated below). Lesson wired into the workflow: **the affected-set detector must cover all 390 WTs, not just `compare_set`.**

**ACCEPTANCE — round 174 replayed under scoped ship (drift-immune, byte-identity restored).** From the shipped round-174 corpus: (1) the complete detector → **51** affected; (2) regen those 51 with `BRACKETFIX_OFF=1` (→ the round-173 state), full fast-loop snapshot = the round-173 baseline, whose aggregates reproduce the round-173 numbers EXACTLY (≥50% **831**, cs exact **8293**, missing **381**, body **336**, leak **318/51**, clean **97.48%**); (3) byte-diff → **25 truly-changed** modules ⊆ 51 (containment HOLDS); (4) regen the 25 back with the fix ON → corpus **byte-identical to round 174** (0/2022 pages differ); (5) `_fastloop_diff.py <51>` reproduces the round-174 full-corpus numbers **EXACTLY**: skeleton ≥50% **832 (+1)**, cs exact **8299 (+6)**, missing **382 (+1)**, ≥75% **169**, mean **50.62%**, EXTRA **147**, body **336**, clean **97.48%**, leak **318/51** — every value matching the round-174 changelog, INCLUDING its documented cs-missing +1 net-positive (which the mechanical verdict correctly flags — the net-positive judgement is the operator's, as round 174 did). FAILURE-MODE tests all pass: a corpus-wide marker ("Te Kura", 389/390) trips the 60% guard → routed to `ship.sh`; a deliberately under-scoped affected list (missing ENGC101) is caught LOUDLY as both DRIFT and UNDER-SCOPED and BLOCKS; the completeness spot-check flags a truly-changed module placed outside the affected set; content-freshness catches an un-regenerated affected module while IGNORING the mtime of byte-identical unaffected modules (the false alarm defeated); **`_fastloop_validate.py` still PASSES** (the decomposition is exact — the `--commit` edit is safe).

**PROTECTED gates — UNCHANGED by construction (byte-identity round).** No converter code changed (only `reference/tests/` tooling, `outputs/` detectors, the UI-only `Config.js` AppVersion, and docs), so the corpus is byte-for-byte round 174: skeleton mean **50.6%** / ≥50% **832** / ≥75% **169**; structural-clean **97.5%** / leak **318/51**; compare_structure exact **8299** / EXTRA **147** / missing **382**; body **336**; tags **9557/9557**; flipCard **33 / div 0**; speechBubble **defect 0** — all identical to round 174 (`_content_manifest.py diff` = IDENTICAL, 0 pages). No new env toggle or data flag (process round). Tools added: `scoped_ship.sh`, `_content_manifest.py`, `_scoped_spotcheck.py`, `_ship_ledger.py`, `outputs/_detect_bracketfix.cjs`; extended: `regen_affected.cjs`, `_fastloop_diff.py`, `ship.sh`.

## 2026-07-04 (round 174, build 260617.50) — MALFORMED-TAG BRACKET REPAIR (Chris, ENGC101-00 "H2] Know:"): a dropped square bracket no longer loses a tag.

**Plain English.** Writers occasionally forget one of the two square brackets around a tag — typing `H2]` instead of `[H2]`. On ENGC101's overview page a writer dropped the opening `[` off the `[H2]` that labels the **Know** section. Claude didn't recognise the tag, so the **Know** heading vanished and the raw text `H2]` leaked onto the page as `<h5>H2]</h5>`. The human developer read straight through the typo and produced `<h3>Know</h3>`. Chris asked for a **general** fix — one that copes with a missing opening OR closing bracket on **any** tag, not just this one. This round delivers that: a dropped bracket is now repaired once, at the source, so every part of the converter sees a clean, well-formed tag.

**Why it broke (the asymmetry).** `TagNormaliser.Parse` — the tag *classifier* — already repairs both edge forms: a dangling `[H2` (missing `]`) and a leading `H2]` (missing `[`). Proven: `Parse(" H2] ")` → `h2` correctly. But ~10 OTHER consumers read the red span's raw bracket structure for their own purposes and never went through that repair — most importantly `TagNormaliser.RenderText` (regex `/\[([^\[\]]*)\]?/g` *requires* a real `[`), which returned the literal `"H2]"`. So the tag was classified right but the heading text and the overview-menu partition still saw a broken span → the leak + the lost heading. Fixing each of the ~10 consumers is whack-a-mole; fixing `block.text` once at the source fixes all of them.

**Triangulated (ENGC101-00).** Raw WT: line 17 `🔴[RED TEXT] [H2] [/RED TEXT]🔴 **Understand:**` (clean), line 23 `🔴[RED TEXT] H2] [/RED TEXT]🔴 **Know:**` (missing `[`), line 33 `[H2] **Do:**` (clean). Human gold: `<h3><span>Understand</span></h3>` / `<h3><span>Know</span></h3>` / `<h3><span>Do</span></h3>`. Claude before: `<h3>Understand</h3>` / `<h3>Do</h3>` / `<h5>H2]</h5>` + `<p><b>Ngā āhuatanga reo…</b></p>` (Know lost, `H2]` leaked). ANZH404-00 has the identical bug on its **Do** heading (`H2] **Do:**`) — a genuine recurring class, not a one-off.

**Measured corpus-wide (`outputs/_measure_malformed_brackets.cjs`, 197-set).** 721 malformed-bracket red spans across 116 modules. Two forms:
- **MISSING-CLOSE** (`[hover trigger: <def>` — 559 occ): deliberately NOT touched. `Parse.dangling` + `RenderText`'s optional `]?` already absorb it (0 clean render-leaks measured), and it is the deferred split-bracket infoTrigger lever (§15).
- **MISSING-OPEN** (`x]` — 162 occ, 159 at span start): the ENGC101 class. Split by match quality: **CLEAN token** (Parse `how` ∈ exact/denumbered — the token IS a tag, e.g. `H2]`, `Body]`, `Image]`, `Button]`, `YouTube]`, `MODULE INTRODUCTION]`) = **~73 occ / 37 modules**; **EMBEDDED token** (a tag word buried in writer prose, `how="embedded"` — `that when they click/hover on the letter…]` → audio, `Please create a dropdown menu for each item]` → dropdown) = **47 occ**, correctly REJECTED by the discriminator. This `how≠embedded` guard is the whole safety story: it repairs the 73 clean forgotten-brackets and declines every prose/instruction false-positive.

**Fix (source-level, one choke point).** `DocxExtractor.RepairContentTags(blocks, normaliser)` — wired into `TrimFrontMatter`, which BOTH the browser (`App.js`) and the gate harness (`batch_convert.cjs`) already call — rewrites `block.text` so a content red span opening with a lone `x]` becomes `[x]`, but ONLY when the token `x` resolves to a known tag by a WHOLE-token match (`red_runs.repair_missing_bracket.clean_hows` = exact / denumbered / denumbered_head). Original case preserved (RenderText needs it). Valid `[…]` pairs and mid-span lone brackets are never touched. GENERAL across every tag (lexicon-driven via the normaliser), no per-module code. Data `Input_Doc_Rules.red_runs.repair_missing_bracket` (`enabled`/`forms`/`clean_hows`/`exclude_tags`); env `BRACKETFIX_OFF` reverts to leaking the literal.

**Result.** ENGC101-00 `<h5>H2]</h5>` → `<h3><span>Know</span></h3>` (matches the human, `H2]` leak gone); ANZH404-00 **Do** recovered; CEDT104's forgotten `[Button]`/`[Audio]`/`[YouTube]` now build the actual button/audio/video widgets. The BLL140 `that when they click/hover…]` audio *instruction* and CEDT104's `Please create a poi activity…]` are left as prose (declined).

**A/B (drift-immune, `_ab.py BRACKETFIX_OFF=1`, 12 affected modules across light/heavy/widget-building):** skeleton HOLDS-or-IMPROVES (CEDT104/CEDO501/MXDI301/AGH1004 +0.07 mean / +1 page ≥50%; the OSBY201/MXDB301/MXFU heavy group −0.01 mean with pages held = the documented net-positive class), compare_structure exact +1, and **defect/leak/body/tags ZERO delta** on every group. The `H2]`→`Know` change is largely gate-neutral by construction (the skeleton text-strips the leaked literal; the overview-menu headings are `#header`-scoped) — it ships on the visible human match + PRIMARY held-or-improved (round-86/103/104/125 precedent).

**PROTECTED gates (full 390-dir regen, 0-stale verified by mtime — 0/2022 stale, ALL HELD-or-IMPROVED):** PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD mean **50.6%** (HELD) / ≥50% **832 (+1)** / ≥75% **169** (HELD, 1567 paired); structural-clean **1971/2022 = 97.5%** / literal-`[tag]` leak **318/51** (EXACT); compare_structure exact **8299 (+6 IMPROVED)** / EXTRA **147** (HELD) / missing **382** (+1, net-positive per §6); body_compare ANY **336** (EXACT); tags **9557/9557**; flipCard **TOTAL 33 / divergence 0**; speechBubble **defect 0**; anchor_compare **386/390 + row.supervisor & menu-structure regressions PASS + all 6 selftests PASS**; index/manifest sync OK. Tools added: `outputs/_measure_malformed_brackets.cjs` + `_agg_malformed.cjs`.

### ROUND 172 (260617.49) — 2nd-TAB TWO-COLUMN LI | SC (screenshot #1, ENGR202-0.0 / ENGS102-0.0)

**Plain English.** Round 166 taught the converter the two-column Learning-Intentions | Success-Criteria overview layout, but only for the FIRST tab. When the same block lives on the 2nd tab, Claude stacked it in one wide column; the human always lays it out as two `col-md-6` columns.

**Triangulated (ENGR202).** Human 2nd-tab pane = `<div class="row"><div class="col-md-6 … paddingR"><h5>Learning Intentions</h5>…</div><div class="col-md-6 … paddingL"><h5>Success Criteria</h5>…</div></div>`; Claude before: one `<div class="col-md-8 col-12">` with LI then SC stacked.

**Mechanism.** The LI/SC arrives on tab-2 via round-166's `curric_split` `tab2Prepend` (a flat single-col string). The registry's own `curric_split` `cols` ALREADY encode the human's tab-2 `col-md-6 paddingR|paddingL` pair (no new mining). So `#tabsPane1Partition` now ALSO splits the moved runs at the first SC run (LI-left / SC-right) into `tab2Cols` reusing those two `col-md-6` cols; a byte-NEUTRAL `{tab2Body}` shell slot (default = the pre-round hard-wired `col-md-8`, proven byte-identical on HES1003/PHE1001) + a SkeletonBuilder tab2Body render emit them. **Result.** Fixes **ENGR202, ENGS102** (both screenshot modules) **+ MXEO401** — clean LI/SC-only 2nd-tab → two columns matching the human. The other 7 review modules **safely DECLINE** (no regression): ANZH301/303/304/404, MXDB301, MXDI201/202 mix LI/SC with Planning/Connections/Assessment on one Claude tab (a deeper multi-tab structure — the human uses 2–3 separate tabs; two-columning just the LI/SC would strand the rest), and TRR203 is reo (`isReoModule` decline, the round-166 class). `#header`-scoped; byte-neutral for every other tabs menu by construction.

## 2026-07-04 (round 169, build 260617.46) — BILINGUAL TITLE MARKER-SPLIT: OSAH301-0.0 EN+Te Reo in one <h1> (Chris, screenshot review)

**Screenshot #6 (OSAH301-0.0):** the human ships two separate title `<h1>`s — English in Title Case, Te Reo below; Claude jammed both into ONE `<h1>` with the English left ALL-CAPS ("ONLINE ABUSE AND HARASSMENT Tūkinotanga ā-ipurangi me te whakatīwheta").

**Root cause.** OSAH301's `[TITLE BAR]` separates the two languages with a `✅` emoji (`*ONLINE ABUSE AND HARASSMENT* ✅ *Tūkinotanga…*`). The emoji is dropped upstream (DocxExtractor), collapsing the two halves to a single space, and the split chain fired only on pipe `|` / newline / 2+space / dash / matching-terminal-punct — none present → one combined `<h1>`. The ALL-CAPS is a side-effect (`#normaliseTitleCase` only lower-cases a WHOLLY-uppercase string; the merged line's lowercase Te Reo tail blocks it).

**Consistency (measured, before coding).** Splitting bilingual EN/Te Reo into two `<h1>` is a near-universal human convention — a subagent measured **94/96 = 98%** of bilingual human headers do it (probe `outputs/_measure_title_separation.py`). NOT a one-off.

**Fix.** Two guarded splits added to the chain AFTER dash (`ContentConverter.#bilingualColonSplit` + `#bilingualCaseSplit`), BOTH behind the shared round-86 macron guard (`#bilingualTwoLangGuard`: EXACTLY one half carries `āēīōū`, neither half placeholder boilerplate) so they can never fire on a single-language or already-handled title:
- **COLON** — a single `:` boundary (CEDO501 `TE WHAI MŌNI: YOUR MONEY`, TWHK903 `Digital Citizenship: Tāurungi Matihiko`).
- **CASE-TRANSITION** — the maximal ALL-CAPS word prefix is the English, the non-caps remainder the Te Reo (OSAH301). The ALL-CAPS English then self-heals through `#normaliseTitleCase`.

Measured `outputs/_measure_title_markersplit.py`: **4 clean splits (OSAH301, CEDO105, CEDO501, TWHK903), 0 false positives** (every would-split module ships 2 human title `<h1>`; XDLS912 is pre-empted by the existing dash split). OSAH301/CEDO501/TWHK903 match the human's two-title split exactly; CEDO105 is the one module where the human EDITORIALLY overrode the WT title ("Can robots move like people?") — Claude renders the (correct) WT split, an absorbed net-positive collateral.

**Data flag** `header.title_split.bilingual_marker_split {colon,case_transition}`; **env `BILINGUALMARK_OFF`** reverts to one combined title.

**A/B (`_ab.py BILINGUALMARK_OFF=1` OSAH301 CEDO501 TWHK903 CEDO105):** skeleton SCAFFOLD mean **+0.29** / pages ≥75% **+1**; compare_structure / body_compare / defect / leak **ZERO delta** (title is `#header`-scoped). **PROTECTED gates (full corpus, affected modules regenerated 0-stale; the ~340 untouched modules are byte-identical → round-148 scoped-regen precedent, full mtime re-baseline defers):** skeleton mean **50.6%** / ≥50% **831** / ≥75% **169**, compare_structure exact **8240 (+2)** / EXTRA **147** / missing **378**, defect clean **97.5%** / leak **318/51**, tags **9557/9557**, flipCard **divergence 0**, speechBubble **defect 0** — all HELD-or-IMPROVED. Shipped with round 168 in one regen (per-toggle A/B isolates each).

Blast radius **45 modules** (body-heading italic in non-ENG/non-reo subjects). **PROTECTED gates (see round 169 — shared regen):** all HELD-or-IMPROVED. The tiny human-kept minority in HIS/XDLS/MXEX/XGF (book/vocab titles) is the documented NET-POSITIVE class (r164/165 precedent); the ENG-reading exclusion protects the largest keep bucket.

## 2026-07-03 (round 167, build 260617.44) — reoMode LAYOUT-TABLE GRID: the ENGS201-01 [body]/[image] FRONTEND LEAK (Chris)

**In plain English:** Chris opened ENGS201 page 1 side by side and spotted raw writer tags —
`[body]` and `[image]` — printed as literal text at the top of the page, where the human simply
shows the intro sentence beside its picture. The cause: ENGS201 uses the standard Te Kura writers-
template header ("MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE - TE ARA WHAKAMUA"), which the engine reads as a signal to
enter **reoMode** — the bilingual pathway. In reoMode, any table the bilingual machinery doesn't
recognise is wrapped in a grey "un-built widget" box that deliberately shows the raw writer tags
for a developer to build later. That's the right treatment for a real widget, but ENGS201's intro
was just a plain side-by-side **layout table** (a sentence in one cell, its image in the other) —
NOT a widget. The human renders that as a simple two-column row; reoMode was skipping the step
that turns a layout table into a grid, so it fell into the widget box and leaked its tags. The fix
teaches the reoMode pathway the same layout-table step the normal pathway already uses: a clean
image|body layout table now becomes the human's `row > col + col` grid (tags gone, matching the
human), while genuine widget/spec tables keep their honest un-built box exactly as before.

**Scope of the deeper cause (measured, deferred):** the MTK header is on **374 of 390 modules**
(`outputs/_measure_mtkflag_reomode.cjs`) — it is the house template name, not a bilingual marker —
so ~357 non-bilingual modules run in reoMode unnecessarily. The truly bilingual corpus is the 19
`TRR*`/`PNR*` modules, every one caught by the reliable code-prefix signal; **0** modules rely on
the MTK flag alone. Demoting the flag is the correct long-term fix, BUT it un-masks a large
PRE-EXISTING multi-path leak surface that reoMode's blanket widget-boxing was hiding (e.g. ENGFUN02
compound-tag glossaries render `[H3]/[Body]` as `<p>` text; those are 150 leaks that exist today,
in and out of reoMode). That is its own cleanup track, not this round. **This round is the precise,
gate-safe fix for exactly the class Chris flagged** — a layout table leaking inside the reoMode box.

**THE VERIFIED DEFECT (triangulated, ENGS201-01):**
- raw WT: `┌─ TABLE ─┐ │ 🔴[body]🔴Origin stories tell us… ║ 🔴[image]🔴 https://…istock…gm1468188986`
- human `ENGS201_1.0.html`: the intro sentence in a col beside its image — 0 literal tags.
- Claude (before): `<div class="cv2-interactive bilingual-unbuilt"><table><tr><th> [body] Origin
  stories…</th><th> [image] <a…></a></th></tr></table></div>` — the tags LEAK as visible text
  inside the grey box (masked from the defect gate because cv2-interactive is leak-excluded, r72).

**THE FIX (`ContentConverter.ConvertPage`, reoMode table fall-through):** before emitting the
bilingual-unbuilt placeholder, try `TablesAndGrids.layoutTableGrid` — the SAME detector the normal
(non-reo) path runs (single-row OR every-cell-tagged, and it BAILS on any widget-member cell tag).
A clean layout table becomes the grid; a widget/spec/data table still returns null and keeps the
placeholder untouched. **LEAK-SAFE guard:** a gridded cell can carry a MID-cell tag that
`renderCellParts` doesn't strip (only the LEADING cell tag is stripped), which would leak as
visible text (the grid is NOT leak-excluded, unlike the box). So `#htmlLeaksResolvedTag` re-checks
the finished grid — if it still shows a resolved `[tag]`, it falls BACK to the placeholder. Net:
**the fix can never ADD a leak** (proven below). Data `elements.dual_language.reo_layout_table_grid`;
env **`REOLTABLE_OFF`** reverts to the always-placeholder behaviour. Tool
`outputs/_measure_mtkflag_reomode.cjs`.

**A/B (`_ab.py REOLTABLE_OFF=1`, drift-immune) + byte-identity:**
- OSAH501 (clickDrop-in-table), ENGFUN02 (compound-tag glossary), TRR203/PNR101 (bilingual):
  **BYTE-IDENTICAL** on/off — the fix touches ONLY clean reoMode layout tables; widget/spec tables,
  paragraph leaks and the whole bilingual corpus are untouched.
- 8-module A/B: **defect-clean / leak occ / leak pages ALL ZERO-delta** (leak-NEUTRAL, the whole
  point); **compare_structure exact +15** (the grids match the human's row>col); skeleton SCAFFOLD
  mean −0.09, **pages ≥50% / ≥75% HELD**. The grid-leak guard caught ENGR201 (6→0) + ENGC202 (4→0).

**PROTECTED GATES — full 390-dir regen, 0-stale, ALL HELD-or-IMPROVED:**
- **Structural-defect / leak: clean 1971/2022 = 97.5% / leak 318 occ / 51 pages — EXACT to r166
  (leak-NEUTRAL, held).**
- **compare_structure: exact wrapper chain 8238 (r166 8146, +92 IMPROVED) / EXTRA 147 (HELD) /
  missing 378** (+23 = the net-positive offset: the gridded layout tables are now real, comparable
  structure instead of a collapsed placeholder — +92 exact matches dominate).
- **Skeleton (PRIMARY): mean 50.6% / median 51.1% (r166 50.64% — HELD); ≥50% 830 / ≥75% 167**
  (r166 831/168, −1/−1 = shared-corpus drift + the −0.09 mean threshold-crossing; the drift-immune
  A/B proves the fix HOLDS pages — documented net-positive, r61/74/115/164 precedent).
- **body_compare ANY 338** (r166 337, +1 drift — HELD); **tags 9557/9557** (0 real failures);
  **flipCard TOTAL 33 / divergence 0**; **speechBubble defect 0**; **anchor_compare 386/390 +
  row.supervisor & menu-structure regressions PASS + all 6 known-answer selftests PASS**; index

- ENGS201-01: the intro table is now `row > col-md-6{<p>} + col-md-6{<img>}` = the human's layout,

## 2026-07-03 (round 166, build 260617.43) — OVERVIEW-MENU TAB-1 TWO-COLUMN SHELL + the MENU-STRUCTURE SAFETY NET (Chris, ENGJ402)

**In plain English:** Chris opened ENGJ402 side by side and the difference was impossible to miss.
On the human's overview page the menu's first tab is a tidy TWO-COLUMN layout — the curriculum
panes (Understand / Know / Do, clean headings, no colons) down the left, the Learning Intentions /
Success Criteria (English-only headings, h5) down the right. Claude's page stacked everything in
ONE narrow half-width column, colons kept, headings still bilingual. The content was all there —
the SHAPE inside the tab was wrong, on 101 of the 166 modules with a tabs overview menu. This
round measures the human's within-tab conventions at every grouping, rebuilds the pane from a
GENERATED registry, and — Chris's second ask — hardens the safety net so a whole-region menu miss
can never again sit invisible for 80+ rounds. After the fix, 87 of the 101 now render the human's
column layout (82 with the exact column classes); the remaining 14 are principled declines where
the content itself was never captured (recorded, not chased). The one-column families
(OS*/TRR/PNR/CED*501/MX* early-phase) are untouched — 0 forced two-cols.

**THE VERIFIED DEFECT (triangulated + census, `outputs/_measure_menu_tab1.py` — site-level, both
sides, r147 page-role parse).** Human pane-1 TWO-col on **101/166** tabs overviews; Claude TWO-col
on **0**. THREE root causes: **(a) the archetype short-circuit** — every two-col transform shipped
since r81 (colon split, bilingual LI/SC reduce, lead-ins, banner) was gated
`archetype === "two_col_li"`, so NONE ran inside the tabs shell; **(b) the single-col mining bug**
(the r147 sub-page-dilution / r165 cv2-contamination class, new instance) — `pane1_col_by_phase`
(hand-mined 12/06/26, no generator) recorded the FIRST col of a PAIR as if it were the whole pane;

containing them, so "What **DO** I need to get started?" hit `inTab1` and the `inTab2 && !inTab1`
rule stranded the whole get-started section in tab 1 (the human ships it in tab 2 on 60 modules).

**THE MEASUREMENT (the r142 cross-tab mandate, answered per the kickoff).** (a) two-col is
GROUP-scoped, not universal — the mined registry encodes it (76 subject|phase groups, 25 series
deviation rows); the guard population (OS*/TRR 13/PNR/CED*501/MX*|1-3 — 65 modules) mines as

feasibility = capture (96/101 two-col humans have curriculum, the 14 curric-but-one-col guards are

`paddingR col-12` spellings etc.) = the r161 dev-editorial class, no series rows. (d) lesson menus
UNTOUCHED (partition gates on `page.isOverview`; human lesson tabs = 32, mostly one-col).

Claude 202/530 → strip (trailing only; ENGR302's short "Know: ideas within…" subtitle form KEPT,
long-glue ≥9 words SPLIT — the MXDI paragraph-in-heading form); piped LI/SC heads reduced to the

## 2026-07-03 (round 164, build 260617.41) — ALERT-REGION BOLD STRIP: writer **bold** inside an alert/important/tip box is stripped to match the human developer (backlog burn-down round 3 — Tier-2 style-transfer ticket 1 SHIPPED net-positive)

widgets) untouched. The visible change: on ~43 pages across 25 modules the alert/tip boxes read as
clean text, matching the human's page. The known, accepted cost: in a handful of boxes the human
CHOSE to keep a bolded vocabulary word (mana, apartheid, iteration — 17 sites corpus-wide); there
is no rule in the writers' documents that separates those from the thousands they strip, so those
few now differ. Net: box-text matching the human went from 73% to 95%.

SITE level).** Catalogue row: "bold STRIPPED in alert", 16-subject scope

## 2026-07-03 (round 161, build unchanged 260617.38 — TOOLING round, engine/data untouched) — anchor_compare GRANULARITY: the rendering-rules miner that sees group-scoped, region-conditioned, and value-swap conventions (Chris)

**In plain English:** the rule catalogue behind `anchor_compare --rules` kept missing real habits of
the human developer because it only looked for ONE shape of rule ("an ancestor gains a class when
some child is present") holding over the WHOLE corpus. The menu italic strip (round 145), the BLL
supervisor pairing (round 160) and the activity col-widening (Chris's hypothesis) were all invisible
to it — each was found by hand. The new miner finds all three ON ITS OWN, plus a ranked backlog of
conventions we haven't implemented yet, each with its counts, its scope, and where it does NOT hold.

**THE NEW MINER — `outputs/_mine_rendering_rules.py` → `outputs/Rendering_Rules_Catalogue.{json,md}`.**
FOUR rule shapes: **(a) added-token** (the legacy shape — now ALSO mined per group, not just
globally); **(b) layout-form** (a col's width-token FORM conditioned on what it wraps — token
swap/removal, structurally invisible to the old miner which dropped every `col-*` token as noise);
**(c) style-transfer** (WT `*italic*`/`**bold**` spans located in the human page and scored
kept-vs-stripped by REGION: menu / body / activity / alert / table / widget / acks — the old miner
never even parsed `#header`, so the menu was a blind spot); **(d) composition** (ordered
direct-child structure of flagged containers: paired-vs-standalone, inner rows, sibling order).
Every shape is mined over the GROUP LADDER all → template → subject → series, crossed with page
role (ov/les/sub/single), and reported at the COARSEST level that passes (consistency ≥0.9, leak
≤0.05, in-group support ≥10) with the failing families listed as fragments — mining per group, not
annotating a global rule. Page-role parsing strips the module code FIRST (the r147 digit-code
lesson: `AGH1001.04` = page 4, `TEFUN02.html` = single-file); `-RR`/`claude|copy` strays excluded;
paths via `_corpus`. PIPELINE (each step one sandbox call, 45s-safe): `--vocab` (14s) → `--scan H
k 4` ×4 + `--scan C k 2` ×2 (~5s each) → `--merge` (11s) → catalogue + ranked backlog + selftest.

**KNOWN-ANSWER SELFTEST (the acceptance bar — all four rediscovered UNPROMPTED, plus legacy parity):**
(1) menu italic strip: GLOBAL, strip 0.989 (4,143/4,189 span-hits), Claude 1.00 → implemented
(r145); keep-italic fragments = the reo-content families MXDI(0.73)/TWHA(0.62) — TRR/PNR carry <8
asterisk-italic menu spans in their WTs, so through this lens the bilingual exclusion shows via
TWHA/MXDI (recorded in the selftest comment). (2) BLL supervisor pairing: composition rule at
**subj:BLL** — paired [panel col + content col] 0.95 over pairable sites (99 paired, control
subjects ≤0.02) + the universal inner-row rule at 0.998 (215/215-class, r160). (3) col-width:
human widens the col wrapping an `.interactive` activity off `col-12+col-md-8` in **33.4%** of
2,850 instances (plain activities 6%), Claude 0% of 1,497 — DECOMPOSED by widget type below
(30 splits) + group cells; the ≥0.9 cells are enforceable, the rest recorded residue (C).
(4) row.supervisor ← super-content: GLOBAL 0.95, implemented (r143.2), and `--regress` PASS.
LEGACY ACCOUNTING: all **30/30** old scaffold rules re-found by the new (a)-shape miner at global
scope (the old `Child_Ancestor_Rules.{json,md}` keeps being produced unchanged alongside).
DETECTION proven (r149 tradition): a doctored catalogue (BLL pairing removed) → `--selftest` rc 1;
restored → rc 0.

**anchor_compare.py integration (diagnostic-only, no gate touched):** new **`--rules2`** runs the
miner's merge from the chunk caches (prints the chunked recipe if caches are missing); **`--audit`**
now ALSO runs the miner's `--selftest` when `Rendering_Rules_Catalogue.json` exists (reads the
cached JSON — no re-mine; a FAIL fails the audit, closing the r97–104 silent-pass hole for the new

row.supervisor regression **PASS**, legacy catalogue **30 rules** EXACT, granularity selftest

## 2026-07-03 (round 160, build 260617.38) — SUPERVISOR-NOTE PLACEMENT (Chris, BLL225): the universal inner panel row + the BLL-family side-by-side pairing + the within-activity scan that closes the activity-box gap — three data flags / three env toggles

**In plain English:** Chris spotted (BLL225 overview) that the human anchors the supervisor icon to
the paragraph it annotates — title in its own row, then ONE `row.supervisor` holding the hidden note
panel and the paragraph side by side — while Claude emitted the note as its own standalone row above
the heading, so the icon floated too high. Measuring every human supervisor note (457 sites, 306
pages) split the problem into three separate, individually-reversible fixes.

**THE MEASUREMENT (tools `outputs/_measure_supervisor_nonactivity.py` + `_measure_supervisor_boxgap.py`).**
Human non-activity sites 215 (177pp/118m): **paired 101 — 99 of them BLL**; every other subject
(17 subjects, 95 sites) ships the standalone row even in the IDENTICAL WT context (control:
MXFL101_0.0 — note at section top, intro following, human leaves it standalone) → the pairing is a
**BLL-family convention**, not global. Within BLL, both writer orders ([supervisor note]
[Introduction][body] BLL225 / [Introduction][supervisor note][body] BLL111) produce the SAME human
output; the 19 BLL standalones are all "nothing to pair with" (single-file parent page-top,
end-of-page). Sub-variant: the BLL1 single-file phonics parents (BLL130-160) put the section h2
INSIDE the content col — 20 sites, EXCLUDED from the fix (recorded partial). Content col class is
per-series: BLL2 paddingR 17/7, BLL1 plain 37/13. Universal sub-find: the human wraps the panel's
two col-12s in an INNER row **215/215**; Claude 0/214 — the by_tag template had UNDER-COPIED its own
gold source BLL146-0.0 (the r143.1 activity-panel class, which the idoc reveal JS keys on). WT note
buckets corpus-wide: 126 non-activity / 69 directly-after / 50 mid-activity; human ships 234
activity super-content boxes vs Claude's 76 (the r143 immediate trigger only) — the ~115 boxes
beyond ALL WT notes are human-added/duplicated notes (BLL110-230 parents 4-17 boxes off 1 WT note;
ENFUN/MXFUN/SSFUN/TRR114 with 0 WT notes) = **non-derivable editorial, recorded C-decline**; the
BLL122 human 2A-vs-WT-1A relocation likewise (Claude keeps the writer's 1A — build-the-writer's
precedent).

**FIX 1 — inner panel row (`callouts.by_tag.'supervisor note'.inner_row`; env `SUPINROW_OFF`).**
`#calloutOpen` swaps to the inner_row open/close pair when the def carries one (legacy strings kept
verbatim in-file for the toggle). Every non-activity site now matches the human panel structure
(156/156).

**FIX 2 — BLL side-by-side pairing (`callouts.by_tag.'supervisor note'.pair_with_content`; env
`SUPPAIR_OFF`).** Scope: subjects ["BLL"] (prefix match), BEFORE the page's first [Activity] opener.
A PRE-PASS swaps a note-before-heading past the heading (qualifying heading = rendered [H1-3] OR the
mid-page [title bar]-family SECTION_MARKER — the [Introduction] alias; swap_heading_tags) so both
writer orders reach the emit site as [heading][note][body]. The own_row emit branch then absorbs the
next unconsumed **[body]** element as the sibling content col (`content_col_open_by_series`: BLL2
paddingR / BLL1 plain; note col always FIRST, human 0 exceptions) — re-opening the box close to row
level (derived by stripping the LAST </div> off whatever close form is live, so A×B toggle
combinations stay correct). A bare-black follower was already gathered INTO the panel by
#calloutOpen → pairing declines, behaviour unchanged by construction. Claude paired **0 → 80**
(human 101; the 21 residue = the excluded h2-inside parent variant + editorial one-offs).

**FIX 3 — within-activity scan (`activity_wrapper.super_content.scan_within_activity`; env
`SUPSCAN_OFF`).** The human hoists a MID-activity note into the box panel as FIRST child (BLL225-2.0
2E verified: [Activity][body][note][video][end activity] → panel + title+body+video INSIDE one box).
The r143 lookahead was immediate-only, AND the bundle-owned activity path (activity + captured
widget) had NO lookahead at all (`activityOpen(..., null, ...)` — BLL124-02 2C/2D standalone below
their boxes). NEW shared closure `scanSupNote(from)` walks forward to the activity's natural
boundary MIRRORING the auto-close semantics (section heading after content honouring
title_heading_tags + heading_closes_only_after_content + ACTHEAD_OFF legacy max / any
activity_close_before directive or tag / CONTAINER_CLOSE / PAGE_BOUNDARY / SECTION_MARKER), SKIPPING
bundle-consumed members (a note beyond an embedded interactive still belongs to the box — and a
consumed next-opener can't be crossed: it stops at the first UNCONSUMED boundary). Both open paths
use it: the CONTAINER_OPEN case (immediate hit still jumps i, r143 unchanged; a scan hit keeps i and
the note is skipped at its own loop visit via a consumedBy guard) and the bundle actOwner path
(reoOwner EXCLUDED — bilingual notes are their own family). r143 regression guard: BLL241-2 2A
byte-shape unchanged, and its 2C spill case now boxes too. Activity super-content boxes **76 → 134**
(BLL124 now 1A/2B/2C/2D/2E matching the human's WT-derivable set exactly; the human's extra 2A has
no WT note). NOTE (logged follow-up, NOT this round): an own_row callout whose >12-word payload the
writer typed INSIDE the red span renders panel-content-less apart from gathered black (BLL111's note
prose — pre-existing, human recovers it; needs its own measured round).

**PROOFS.** A/B: all three toggles OFF regenerates BLL225/BLL124/ENGR102 **byte-identical to the
r159 manifest** (md5 vs `outputs/_manifest_r159.txt`); ON leaves note-less modules byte-identical

(`interactive_placeholder.manifest_unbuilt_only`; env `MANIFESTALL_OFF`).** The txt is the hand-off
WORKLIST — an interactive the converter already BUILT into the generated HTML is not work. Built
entries are OMITTED and the per-entry list RENUMBERS over the un-built only. MEASURED corpus-wide:
**444 built entries dropped / 5,631 kept / all 387 txt files rewritten** (verified post-regen: 5,631

counts (telemetry) with its NOTE lines rewritten so they no longer promise "Status: BUILT" entries

## 2026-07-02 (round 146) — HOVER-WEAVE HYGIENE: the HIS1002-16 sentinel leak + the URL-host mis-weave class (Chris, review queue 0a) — SHIPPED (build 260617.25)
The review's quick-win 0a: ONE occurrence of the internal infoTrigger sentinel (U+E001, defect class E)

**TRIANGULATED.** WT (HIS1002 parsed line 1930): `[Hover/rollover for the pounamu koru image: For each

sentinel to the nearest preceding item WITH TEXT — an `[image]` item whose blackAfter is a bare URL. The
media URL-strip then consumed `…Pounamu_0.jpg⟨IT0⟩For` as "the URL", orphaning `⟨IT1⟩` past every cleanup
regex and into the page.

**MEASURED corpus-wide BEFORE coding** (`outputs/_measure_sentinel_hosts.cjs`, engine-level, full compare
set + OSSC301 + HIS1002): **295 sentinel weaves = 288 CLEAN / 6 MEDIA-TAIL hosts / 1 INSTRUCTION-def.**

paths (round-75 `info_trigger_inline` + round-82/86 `hover_definition_inline`), in
`InteractiveScanner` (`#hoverHygieneCfg` / `#hoverDefIsInstruction` / `#urlTailHost`):

   anchor is non-derivable → the existing no-anchor fallback (def dropped, marker consumed — matching the
   human at MXFU201, who drops the text entirely).
Data flag `elements.hover_weave_hygiene` (instruction_cue_pattern + media_tail_pattern live in data); env
**`HOVERHYG_OFF`** reverts all sites to the round-145 behaviour (verified byte-identical).

## 2026-07-02 (round 145) — GENERAL MODULE-MENU ITALIC STRIP (Chris) — SHIPPED (build 260617.24)
Chris observed the human strips the writer's italics from module-menu items and asked whether it is a
consistent, enforceable convention. MEASURED it corpus-wide, first per-module then — the decisive cut —
**per ELEMENT ROLE** (`outputs/_measure_italic_transfer.py`). The aggregate is NOT a single rule (the
human keeps 58% of Claude's italic overall; per-module keep-rate is bimodal 0%→811%), but bucketing by
role exposes clean rules the average hid:

| element role | human strip-rate | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **module menu item** | **99%** (2173/2200; Standard 99% / Inquiry 93%) | RULE → strip |
| **acknowledgements** | **0%** (2/451, all templates) | RULE → keep (already correct) |
| heading / title | 85% (Standard only 69%) | editorial (C) |
| callout / table / plain-body / activity-body | 43–66% | editorial (C) |

The menu 99% is the shippable win (the acks 0% Claude already honours; the mid-range roles have no
discriminator → left as C, consistent with the first-pass finding). The WT wraps menu learning-intentions
/ curriculum / descriptions in `*italics*` (`#inlineMarkup` → `<i>`); the human menu carries none
(`<i>Ākonga will:</i>`, `<i>We are learning:</i>`, whole italic lesson descriptions). Menu italic-stripping
already existed but ONLY for the ENG/banner CURRICULUM panes (rounds 81/109/142); this **generalises it to
EVERY menu pane and family.**

**Implementation (DATA-OVER-CODE + reversible).** `ContentConverter.#buildMenu`, after the existing
family strips, runs a general pass over ALL panes (`tab1/tab2/content/left/right`) via a new
`#stripTextItalic` helper — removes `<i>`/`<em>` KEEPING inner text; a Font-Awesome icon `<i class="fa…">`
is never touched (measured 0 icon `<i>` in any menu, human or Claude, so structurally safe). Gated by data
flag `menu.strip_italic_all` (Emit_Templates) + env `MENUITALIC_OFF` (reverts to the round-142 family-only
strip; verified — CEDO102/CEDK501/OSAH501 menu italic returns). **EXCLUDES reo/bilingual modules**
(`#isReoModule`: `reoTranslate` body_class OR TRR/PNR code prefixes = all 19 bilingual modules): MEASURED
the human KEEPS italic on BOTH panes of a bilingual menu — the reo line AND its English translation
(TRR108 `He kaingākaunui…` + `Mokopuna care about…`, TRR301; 32 spans). Deliberately NOT keyed on
`run.mtkFlag` — that is a broad Māori-CONTENT signature that fires on ordinary English modules with reo
content (CEDO102 Tangaroa/Māui) whose menu the human DOES strip.

**PROTECTED gates — HELD-or-IMPROVED.** The edit touches ONLY `#buildMenu` (the `#module-menu-content`
region) → body HTML is byte-identical, so the body-scoped gates are inert (the A/B confirms it). A/B

## 2026-07-02 (round 144) — HARDEN `anchor_compare` INTO A TRUSTWORTHY SAFETY NET: 0 silent drops + the child→ancestor rule catalogue (Chris) — DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY (no converter output, no AppVersion bump, protected gates inert)
The safety-net diagnostic had **failed closed and silent**: after the round-128 nested-corpus migration
(`01-(Finalized|Claude)_Modules_/<Template>/<CODE>/`), `pair_pages` still built the Claude-side dir with a
raw `os.path.join(CLAUDE, code)` (only the human dir was repointed to `_corpus.mdir`), so the path no longer
resolved and the tool produced **ZERO records for EVERY module** — not just BLL241 (Chris tested BLL241 and got
"no paired page 2"; it was actually the whole corpus). This round makes the tool complete, loud, and able to
catch the exact class of miss that burned three iterations of round 143.

**(1) REVIVED + the coverage safety-net (Problem 1 — 0 silent drops).** Fixed the two nested-path bugs
(`pair_pages` cdir + `build_corpus_all`), and a latent crash the revival exposed: `wt_items` returned a 2-tuple on
its no-`parsed.txt` early paths while callers unpack 3 (any of the 14 bilingual TRR modules lacking a parsed.txt
would crash a real run) → now returns `[], {}, {}`. New **`--coverage`** mode sweeps the WHOLE corpus (union of
human+Claude codes, all 4 templates) in ~15s and reports, per template, modules-that-produce-records vs hard
drops, plus every partial-coverage module — and **exits non-zero ONLY on a TOOL failure** (a `zero_pairs` pairing
bug, a null-test violation, or the regression miss); a genuine DATA gap (Claude never built the module; the human
side is an acks-only stub) is reported just as loudly under a `!!!!` banner but does not trip red (nothing the tool
can fix, and a permanent-red safety net is worthless). Result: **386/390 modules produce records** (Standard
276/277, Inquiry 49/49, Fundamentals 45/45, Bilingual 16/19); the 4 drops are all DATA gaps and named
(TRR104/105/115 = `_run.json` only, no Claude HTML; BLL155 = human is an acks-only page); 140 partial modules are
pure page-count asymmetry (the human's `0.0/0.1` sub-pagination vs Claude's `00/01` — measured **0 both-sides-
unpaired**, i.e. the doc-order fallback already exhausts `min(C,H)` pairs, so there is NO fixable pairing failure to
chase). The **`--self` null test now passes for every template** (a cheap self-pairs-to-itself proxy runs
corpus-wide in `--coverage`; full self-score = 0.0 on CEDO102/OSAH501/TEFUN02/TRR102, incl. the no-parsed.txt
bilinguals).

**(2) FULL ancestor chain is never normalised away (Problem 2a — the round-143.2 miss).** `diff_bundle` reduced
each wrapper bundle to callout-names + col-width + roles, THROWING AWAY every other ancestor class token — so a
`row` vs `row supervisor` (a deep child dictating the TOP row's class) was invisible, which is exactly why the
narrow-anchor diff missed it three times. Added `bundle_classes()` + a **full ancestor-class ladder diff**
(`wrapper_class_missing` / `wrapper_class_extra`, weights 1.5 / 0.75) that surfaces any SEMANTIC class present on
one side's ancestor chain and absent on the other's (col-widths stay owned by `width_diff`, callout wrappers by
`wrapper_missing`, `row`/padding are noise). **Regression test (`--regress`, also in `--coverage`/`--audit`):** takes
the real human BLL241-2.0 (`row supervisor`) + a synthetic PRE-143.2 Claude with `supervisor` stripped and asserts
`wrapper_class_missing(supervisor)` fires — **PASS**. (Live BLL241 correctly shows NO supervisor diff since 143.2
shipped it on both sides; it did surface a genuine NEW finding — Claude over-wraps activity 2B/2D in an extra
`row supervisor` the human leaves plain, plus a missing `alertPadding` — a converter-triage item, not a tool bug.)

**(3) The child→ancestor rule catalogue (Problem 2b — the backlog this tool exists to generate).** Extended
`outputs/_measure_child_ancestor_classes.py` from the round-143 prototype into a corpus-wide miner with:
**NEAREST-ANCESTOR attribution** (a trigger F is attributed to its nearest base-B ancestor, not every ancestor
above it — without this the feature leaks all the way up and `row.supervisor` is swamped: it was invisible in the
first cut for exactly this reason); **both-direction discrimination** (consistency = of E-with-F the share carrying
X; leak = of E-without-F the share carrying X, must be ~0); **attributes as well as classes** (@onclick/@style/
@role/@tabindex/@data-* on either side); **all four templates**; **cross-tab per template + per series** (the
MEASUREMENT MANDATE — a rule that fragments at the finest grouping is flagged with the offending series so a real
rule is told apart from an editorial minority); **scaffold vs widget-internal split** (widget interiors are
placeholdered by design, reported separately as informational, not backlog); and **implemented-or-OPEN tagging by
re-mining the CLAUDE corpus** — if Claude reproduces `(E,X<=F)` it's IMPLEMENTED, if Claude builds F but drops X
it's an OPEN gap (proven both ways by a unit test; row.supervisor was OPEN pre-143.2, IMPLEMENTED now). Output:

shows `row.supervisor` holds per-template (Standard 0.95 / Inquiry 0.96 / Fundamentals 0.84) but has series
exceptions (CEDT/ENGR/MXEO) — the editorial `col-md-12` minority Chris already knew about, now measured.

**THE ONE COMMAND:** `python3 anchor_compare.py --audit` = whole-corpus coverage safety-net + the row.supervisor
regression + the rule catalogue, in ~33s (under the sandbox wall). Also `--coverage`, `--rules`, `--regress`

## 2026-07-02 (round 143) — A SUPERVISOR NOTE BELONGS INSIDE ITS ACTIVITY BOX, NOT below it; and don't title a lesson with a widget's panel label (Chris, BLL241-2) — SHIPPED (build 260617.23)
**UPDATE 143.2 (Chris — the ACTUAL modal fix + a PROCESS correction).** The real fix is a **child-dictates-ancestor**
rule I kept missing: the **top content `.row` wrapping a supervisor-note activity must carry `.supervisor`**
(`<div class="row supervisor">`) — the reveal JS keys off `.row.supervisor`, so without it the note renders inline,
not the icon modal. I missed it for THREE iterations because I anchored every diff **at the activity element** and
never compared the **parent row's class**. Chris's process mandate (now adopted + saved to memory): diff the WHOLE
enclosing structure (ancestors + descendants), run `anchor_compare` on every change, and MINE the corpus for ALL
such child→ancestor dependencies rather than fixing one example. I built `outputs/_measure_child_ancestor_classes.py`
and measured it corpus-wide: **104/104 human `.supervisor` rows contain a super-content note** (the rule) — and,
applying the wider window, the human's supervisor col stays **`col-md-8`** (dominant 123-151 vs `col-md-12` minority
~11 = editorial, NOT a rule, so left as-is). Impl: `emit()` gains a `{rowClass}` slot on `content_row_open`; the
activity opener sets it to ` supervisor` when a supervisor note is present (`activity_wrapper.super_content.row_class`).
A/B `SUPNOTE_OFF` (5 mods): **skeleton +1.96** (was +1.81) / compare_structure exact +1, all else ZERO. Full 0-stale
regen re-verified: defect 97.5%/318, compare_structure 7906/146/354, body 340, tags 9557, flipCard div 0,
speechBubble 0 — HELD. (`anchor_compare` also has a real gap — it produced 0 records for BLL241 via a silent
page-pairing drop; logged as a follow-up to harden.)

**UPDATE 143.1 (Chris — modal regression fix).** The first cut of the containment fix nested the note but rendered
it as a plain **always-visible box** instead of the hidden icon-triggered **modal** (BLL241-2 2A/2C; the overview's
own-row note was unaffected and still worked). Cause: my `super-content` panel omitted the human's **inner
`<div class="row">`** (the human is `super-content row` → `row` → `col-12,col-12`), so the `idoc_scripts` reveal JS
didn't process it. Matching the human byte-for-byte (added `panel_open`'s inner row + a matching close) restores the
modal AND tightens the skeleton — the A/B below rose from **+0.68 to +1.81**. Build bumped to 260617.22; full
0-stale regen re-run, all gates re-verified HELD (defect 97.5%/318, compare_structure 7906/146/354, body 340, tags
9557, flipCard div 0, speechBubble 0).

**Plain English (for Chris).** You flagged BLL241 lesson 2's activity 2A: the "Alien words" box came out **hollow** —
just the heading sat in the green activity box, and the intro text, the image and the alien words all **spilled out
below it** as loose content. The human keeps the whole thing in one tidy box. The cause: when a **[Supervisor note]**
sits right after an [Activity] heading, the converter was treating that note like the start of a NEW container, so it
**closed the activity box** after the heading, dropped the note in its own strip, and everything after it fell
outside. The fix teaches it that a supervisor note right after an activity heading is that activity's own note — it
now builds the exact box the human builds (`activity super-content-button` with the note tucked in as the first
child, then the title + body + image all inside). I measured first: this "note-after-heading" pattern is **77
activities** corpus-wide, and 2A/2C on BLL241-2 are textbook cases; activities WITHOUT a note (2B/2D/2E) were already
fine and are untouched. **Bonus:** because the box now holds its content, the page-structure score went **up**, not
just held.

**Also — the "fog" title.** You spotted lesson 2's header saying **"fog"** instead of the phonics letter-teams. The
real title ("oe, ow, ir, …") is **not in the Writers Template at all** — the developer types it in per lesson, so we
can't reproduce it. "fog" was the converter grabbing the **first heading it found**, which here was `[H3] Fog` — a
label buried inside the click-and-reveal widget in 2B, not a title. The fix only lets it harvest a heading that comes
**before the first activity** (a genuine lesson title) or an explicit "Lesson N:" heading; a heading buried after an
activity is widget content and is ignored. So "fog" is gone (the page now falls back to the module title). I
measured the blast radius — **13 of 496** lesson sections harvest a post-activity heading, and the human titles
**none** of them with it (the BLL phonics letter-teams are non-derivable; HIS1001 shows its module title, not the
section heading "HIROSHIMA"), so this only removes wrong picks.

**WT → human → Claude (BLL241-2 2A).** WT: `[Activity 2A] Alien words` → `[Supervisor note] The purpose…` →
`[body] Do you think…` → `[image]` → `Words for speech bubbles: whamidge…`. HUMAN (`BLL241-2.0`): ONE
`<div class="activity super-content-button" number="2A">` = `<div class="super-content row">…note…</div>` +
`<div class="row"><div class="col-12"><h3>Alien words</h3> + body + img</div></div>`. CLAUDE (round 142):
`<div class="activity" number="2A">…<h3>Alien words</h3></div>` (heading-only) → a separate `row supervisor` note →
a separate row with the body/image. ROOT CAUSE: the supervisor note's `CONTAINER_OPEN` directive is in
`container_auto_close.activity_close_before.directives`, so `autoClose` closed the box before the note; the note
then hit the `own_row` callout branch (stack now empty) and the body flowed into loose rows.

**The fix.** (1) CONTAINMENT — the [Activity] opener looks ahead (`ContentConverter` CONTAINER_OPEN/activity branch)
for an immediately-following supervisor note; when present, `#activityOpen(…, supervisorNote)` emits
`<div class="activity{mods} super-content-button">` + the nested `super-content row` panel (from `panel_open` +
the note's rendered text + `panel_close`) + a fresh `content_open` row>col; the title+body then flow into that col
and the box auto-closes at the next [Activity]/section as usual. The note item is marked `consumedBy`. data
`activity_wrapper.super_content`; env `SUPNOTE_OFF`. (2) TITLE — `PageSplitter` restricts the first-heading harvest
to a heading before the first [Activity] opener (or a "Lesson N:" heading). data
`body_region.lesson_title_dedup.harvest_before_activity_only`; env `LESSONTITLE_OFF`.

**PROTECTED gates — all HELD-or-IMPROVED (full 0-stale regen; per-toggle A/B).** A/B `_ab.py SUPNOTE_OFF=1`

## 2026-07-01 (round 141) — A HEADING BETWEEN WIDGET PANELS IS A LABEL, NOT A NEW SECTION: one clickDrop no longer fragments into three pieces (Chris, BLL241-02) — SHIPPED (build 260617.19)

**Plain English (for Chris).** You flagged BLL241 page 2: the "Vocabulary activities" click-and-reveal (three
picture panels — Fog, Loops, Glide) came out **shattered** — the heading + first panel sat in the 2B activity
box, a **second, unnamed** dashed "un-built interactive" box held the last panel, and the middle "Loops" panel
leaked out as **plain body text** in between. In the Writers Template it is clearly **one** interactive. The
converter has a rule (added a few rounds back for a different module) that says "a lone heading after a widget's
content means the writer is starting a NEW section, so close the widget here." That rule was tripping on the
panel headings: when it reached "Loops" it looked ahead for a sibling heading to tell it "this is just a panel,
keep going" — but it bumped into the **next panel's picture tag first** and gave up, wrongly deciding Loops was a
new section. The fix teaches it that **a heading sitting right after the widget's own panel marker is that
panel's label, never a new section** — so all three panels now stay together in ONE box inside the 2B activity,
which is exactly what you asked for ("at the very least, all correctly contained within one un-built interactive
container within an activity box"). I measured the whole class first: the change touches **32 modules**, and it
also *tidied up* two other modules (XGF9001 / ENGJ301) whose accordions were fragmenting the same way. One guard
I added after measuring: it only merges a **clean single-type panel cluster** — a messy page that had already
mashed a click-reveal + a slideshow + speech-bubbles into one giant box (XDLS908) is left alone rather than made
bigger. NOTE: this contains the interactive cleanly as a placeholder; **building** the click-reveal widget for
real on the page is a larger follow-up I can do next if you want it.

## 2026-07-01 (round 140) — "INTERACTIVE" IS A QUALIFIER, NOT A CONTAINER: one activity no longer split into two boxes (Chris, BLL241-01) — SHIPPED (build 260617.18)

**Plain English (for Chris).** You flagged BLL241: Activity 1C ("Speed listening and reading") was drawn as
**two** activity boxes instead of one — the heading + intro sat in the 1C box, then the audio player and the
11 drag-words (match, catch, watch…) dropped out into a second, *unnamed* box below. In the Writers Template
it is clearly **one** activity. I traced it to a single wrong word in the converter's dictionary: the bare word
**"interactive"** was listed as a synonym for "start an activity box". So when the converter hit
`[Interactive Stop Watch]` (the writer's note asking for a stopwatch on the right of the activity), it read that
as *"begin a new activity"* — closed 1C after the intro, and opened an unnamed box that swallowed everything
after it. The fix teaches the converter that **"interactive" is a description, not a box-starter** — a box is
only started when the writer actually writes "activity" **or** names a real widget (drag-and-drop, flip cards,
a slider…). This isn't a one-off patch: I measured all 197 modules first. 23 use an "interactive" bracket;
**every genuine "interactive activity" box (`[interactive activity]` appears 57 times) is kept untouched**, and
the same misfire is fixed everywhere it occurs (the stopwatch, "interactive tool" ×24, lone "[Interactive]", an
"interactive timer", a "sliding scale", …). One nuance the measurement caught and I fixed before shipping: in
the Fundamentals modules a lone `[Interactive]` is often followed by the widget's name in the surrounding prose
("[Interactive] Drag and drop…"), where the human *does* build a box — so the fix keeps the box whenever a
widget is named anywhere in the line, and only drops it for a pure instruction like the stopwatch. BLL241's 1C
is now one box; nothing else regressed.

**WT → human → Claude (BLL241 Activity 1C).** WT (parsed): `[Activity 1C] Speed listening and reading` →
`[body] Time yourself…` → `[Interactive Stop Watch] Placed over on the right side of the activity please – only
minutes and seconds required. Please make the activity look like this:` → `[IMAGE image4.png]` → `[Audio]…` →
`[audio and words to be dragged…]` → match/catch/…/hatch → `[Activity 1D]`. HUMAN (`BLL241-1.0`): ONE
`<div class="activity alertPadding interactive" number="1C">` holding heading + body + the drag-words + activity
buttons. CLAUDE (round 139): `activity number="1C"` (heading + body only) → CS note → a **numberless**
`<div class="activity">` with the audio + words. TRACE (`_dbg_actsplit.cjs`): the `[Interactive Stop Watch]`
item resolved to `primary.tag="activity"` (alias "interactive"), so `autoClose` closed 1C and the numberless
opener captured items 15–27.

**Measured first (the MEASUREMENT MANDATE).** `outputs/_measure_interactive_alias.cjs` runs the LIVE normaliser
over every distinct bracket containing "interactive" across the 197-set (38 modules corpus-wide, 23 in
compare_set). Three buckets: **widget-wins** (48 forms — `[Interactive – drag and drop]` → the widget is
primary, untouched), **genuine container** (`[interactive activity]` ×57 etc. — ALL carry the word "activity",
which yields a SEPARATE alias:"activity" tag → kept), and the **bug class** (`[Interactive Stop Watch]`,
`[interactive stopwatch]`, `[interactive tool]` ×24 / 8 modules, lone `[Interactive]` ×11, `[insert interactive
timer…]`, `[interactive: Sliding scale…]` — "interactive" is the ONLY container signal → mis-opens a box). The
clean discriminator: the bug class NEVER contains the word "activity".

**Shipped — DATA-described demote (mirrors round-65 `condition_primary_demote`, no per-module code).**
`TagNormaliser.Parse`, after resolving `primary`: when `primary` is an activity `CONTAINER_OPEN` whose alias is
a listed qualifier ("interactive") AND no other activity tag comes from a non-qualifier alias AND no INTERACTIVE
(widget) alias appears anywhere in the span's free text (substring-scan, len>=4, robust to "sliders??"), DROP the
qualifier-only activity tag(s) and re-resolve `primary` → the span falls through to instruction/noise and no
longer opens or splits a box. Widget-primary spans are inert (activity is never primary there: INTERACTIVE 7 >
CONTAINER_OPEN 5). Data `Tag_Lexicon._meta.qualifier_alias_demote` (`enabled`, `tag:"activity"`,
`open_directive:"CONTAINER_OPEN"`, `aliases:["interactive"]`); env `INTERACTIVEQUAL_OFF` reverts.

**PROTECTED gates — A/B (`_ab.py INTERACTIVEQUAL_OFF=1 BLL241 HPFUN101 HPFUN202 TRR106 OSAH401 OSAH501 ENGC102`,
the drift-immune proof).** The ONLY metric the fix moves is **skeleton SCAFFOLD mean +0.08**; compare_structure
exact/EXTRA/missing, body_compare ANY, defect-clean %, and literal-[tag] leak all **HELD EXACTLY**. Per-module
skeleton (OFF→ON): **BLL241 55.7→56.4** (the fix), HPFUN101/202/303, TRR106, OSAH401 all flat (the first cut
regressed HPFUN101 −1.8 by deleting its widget-named boxes — the free-text-widget guard restored it to flat
BEFORE shipping). All 23 affected modules + OSSC301 regenerated, **0 stale** (107 HTML files verified newer than
the edited sources). Corpus snapshot (shared-corpus drift since round 139 → the A/B is authoritative, not the
absolutes): skeleton pages ≥50% **763→769**, ≥75% **105** HELD; compare_structure exact 8210 / **EXTRA 150
(≤151)** / missing 378; defect-clean **96.1%** / leak **383 (≤424)**; body_compare ANY 274; **tags 9557/9557 /
REAL FAILURES 0**; **flipCard divergence 0**; **speechBubble defect 0** (OSAH501 8/8 exact, OSAH301 1/1). Tools
`outputs/_measure_interactive_alias.cjs`, `outputs/_dbg_actsplit.cjs`, `outputs/_dbg_norm.cjs`.

## 2026-07-01 (round 139) — INQUIRY [page N]-DELIMITED panel fire: two more BLL phonics modules now build their tabbed scaffold (Chris) — SHIPPED (build 260617.17)

**Plain English (for Chris).** You picked the Inquiry template family as the next lane, and asked me to
start with the smallest, safest win: the three BLL modules (BLL140, BLL220, BLL240) that were supposed to
build their tabbed inquiry pages but weren't. Before writing any code I measured *why*. Round 100 taught the
converter to recognise the BLL inquiry pages by a specific fingerprint — a list of labelled `[Tab N]` tabs at
the top, then a run of *empty* `[Tab N]` markers that each open one panel. BLL140 and BLL220 write it

through the crack between two existing rules — building **zero** panels, crumbs, or side-nav (they scored
~5%). This round widens the fingerprint to also recognise that `[page N]`-delimited form, and reuses the
machinery already in the converter to open those panels. Result: **BLL140 now builds all 8 of its panels
(exactly matching the human), BLL220 all 6** — going from a blank page to the full tabbed inquiry scaffold.
Every other module is byte-for-byte unchanged. **Two honest notes:** (1) BLL240 turned out to be a *different*

form* (the writer points at other modules to copy from), so the 6 panels of content simply aren't in the
template. The converter correctly produces almost nothing because there's almost nothing to convert — that's
right behaviour, not a bug, and I've recorded it so we stop chasing them.

## 2026-06-28 (round 138) — EXTRACT-INTERACTIVES hand-off mode (Chris) — a second OFF/ON output mode that pulls un-built interactives out of the page into a coded {CODE}_interactives.txt, SHIPPED (build 260617.16)

**Plain English (for Chris).** You asked for a switch — sitting next to the image placeholder/direct
choice, default OFF — that gives a second way to hand a module to whoever builds the interactives.
This round adds it. **Switch OFF (the default, exactly what happens today — nothing changes):** each
un-built interactive still renders as the dashed box in its correct spot, so you can keep eyeballing
the boundaries. **Switch ON (the finalised Phase-1 hand-off):** the un-built interactives are NOT
drawn on the page at all — at each spot the page shows ONE loud, unique code, e.g.
`⟦INT · OSAH401-03-02 · dropDown⟧`, and that interactive's raw content is written into the module's
`{CODE}_interactives.txt` under the **same** code. The code is the link: a builder reads the .txt,
sees the content and its code, searches that code in the page HTML, and knows exactly where the
finished widget drops in. It reuses the manifest the converter already writes (nothing reinvented),
and the codes are deterministic (re-running gives the same codes). Bonus: it doubles as a boundary
stress-test — if an interactive over-captures, the over-captured content lands conspicuously in the
.txt, the same thing OFF mode lets you see in the box.

**Confirmed with you before building.** (1) SCOPE = the un-built PLACEHOLDER boxes only; built widgets
stay rendered; the 204 bilingual content-table placeholders in 17 Te-Reo modules are a separate,
manifest-untracked class — DEFERRED. (2) The .txt = REUSE the existing `{CODE}_interactives.txt`
manifest, each extracted block headed by the code. (3) The code format = your suggestion, with a
page-local running number.

corpus: **5154** in-scope un-built boxes across **366 modules / 1332 pages** (heaviest page 74 boxes,
heaviest module XGF9004 79). The proposed id `{CODE}-{NN}-{seq}` (seq = per-page running number,
document order) is **COLLISION-FREE corpus-wide** (5154 ids, **0 collisions**). **0** inline-`<span>`
placeholders (so scope is cleanly "the dashed boxes"). 204 bilingual-unbuilt boxes / 17 modules out
of scope.

**Shipped — DATA-described shape + the minimal engine branch (no per-module code).** A run-wide
`ConversionRun.interactiveMode` ("inline" default / "extract"), carried uniformly like `imageMode`
(UI checkbox `#mode-extract`, default OFF; env `INTEXTRACT_ON` for batch / `_ab.py`). Data
`Emit_Templates.json … interactive_placeholder.extract` holds the marker + the `id_format` /

Placeholder` gains an extract branch placed AFTER the built / empty-bundle / instruction-only guards

## 2026-06-28 (round 133) — Bilingual ACTIVITY scanner integration BUILT + PARKED; the page-split is the prerequisite (Chris) (build 260617.11)

**Plain English (for Chris).** This round did exactly what the kickoff asked — taught the converter to build
the Te Reo "activity boxes" by re-using the existing box-builder (the scanner reads the "Activity 1A:" rows
and the existing machinery wraps the widget). It works: TRR102 goes from 0 boxes to 13 correctly-numbered
ones. **But** when I measured it, the boxes make one module's automated match-score slightly *worse*
(−0.33), because the Te Reo pages are still split into the wrong pages — so the new boxes land on pages that
don't line up with the human's (lesson-1 content is sitting on the overview page, "page 1.0" actually holds
lesson-2 content, and so on). You chose **page-split first, then boxes**. So this round: the box-building is
fully built, tested and ready behind a switch, but **parked OFF** so it can't hurt anything; the live output
is unchanged and every quality check holds. And I did the full investigation of *why* the pages are wrong, so
the page-split can be fixed cleanly next — it's the real thing blocking the whole Te Reo build, not just boxes.

**BUILT + parked (behind `activity_wrapper.reo_bundle_activity` — DEFAULT-OFF — + env `REOACT_OFF`).** The
bilingual activity NUMBER is a table ROW (`Activity 1A:`/`Ngohe 1A:`), not an `[Activity N]` TAG, so the
`InteractiveScanner` opener-lookback never owned these widgets. NEW reoMode post-scan pass: walk the items,
track the most recent `Activity NX:` row, hand its number to the FIRST following widget bundle
(`bundle.activityId` + `bundle.reoActivity`, **claimed-per-row → one number = one box**). `ContentConverter`'s
existing bundle path opens the wrapper via a synthetic owner (NO lead — the bilingual intro heading/body is
its OWN section OUTSIDE the box, matching the human; `.interactive` forced per the round-58 widget-type rule).
Overview-guarded (`page.isOverview` → no box; the human ships 0 activities on every `_0.0`). Reuses the engine,
no parallel path — exactly the round-132 diagnosis's prescription. **PROVEN: TRR102 0 → 13** correct
`div.activity[number]` when enabled.

**Why PARKED (the measured blocker).** A/B (`_ab.py REOACT_OFF=1 TRR102 OSAH501 ENGC102`): the ONLY effect of
the fix is **skeleton SCAFFOLD mean −0.33** on TRR102; every other gate ZERO-delta; standard canaries
byte-identical (reoMode-scoped). The boxes are *correct structure in the wrong place* — the bilingual
page-split misaligns the lesson pages, so the wrappers add structure the (misaligned) human page lacks.
Per the hold-or-improve non-negotiable, NOT shipped active. `enabled:false` → live output = round 132.

**Class heterogeneity (measured — `outputs/_measure_bilingual_activity.py`).** Human ships **252** `div.activity`
across the 19 Bilingual modules. The TRR102 `[Interactive]`-bundle + clean `Activity NX:` row pattern is **only
one sub-pattern**: TRR102/103/106 use it; TRR108/114/203 use prose-checkbox `[Body] ☐ Activity 1A:` rows with
NO widget tags (form no bundles) + non-sequential numbers the human renumbers; the `1.1`-positional family
(PNR/TRR104/105/109/111/115/304) has no clean row. So even after page-split, the prose-checkbox + positional
families are their own follow-up rounds.

**PAGE-SPLIT diagnosis (the next round's spec — `outputs/_measure_bilingual_pagesplit.py`, spec §9d).** Human
**86** pages vs Claude **45** (14/19 under-paginate). THREE marker conventions ([end page]+[LESSON N CONTENT];
[H2] Lesson N; Hei Mahi N) + THREE root-cause bugs (from TRR102's splitter trace): (a) `[LESSON N CONTENT]`
isn't parsed as a numbered lesson → implicit break loses the number + the module-intro absorbs lesson 1 onto
the overview; (b) a mid-doc `[Title Bar]` (a lesson heading) trips the sub-document path → duplicate-label
relabel chaos; (c) no `[H2] Lesson N`/`Hei Mahi N` TABLE-ROW boundary detection → those modules collapse to
1 page. The fix is reoMode-scoped PageSplitter (its own gate-proven round — the splitter is the most
corpus-wide-sensitive component), ship WITH the content unfold per round-99.

round-132 changelog's 242 = pre-existing shared-corpus drift), tags **9557/9557**, flipCard divergence **0**

## 2026-06-28 (round 132) — Bilingual Stage 3 cont.: ACTIVITY container grouping + the scanner-integration diagnosis (Chris) (build 260617.10)

**Plain English (for Chris).** The human wraps every activity on a Te Reo page in a tidy "activity box"
(`<div class="activity">…`). This round teaches the converter to build those boxes by grouping an activity's
instructions + its widget into one box. It works for the activities the writer typed out as plain tables —
but the deeper measurement found that MOST Te Reo activities are written as tagged widgets (`[Interactive]
[Flipcards]`, `[Interactive] [Carousel]`), which a different part of the engine (the "scanner") already
grabs. The engine ALREADY knows how to put a widget in an activity box — it just isn't told the activity's
number for these Te Reo widgets (the number sits in a table row, not a tag). So the proper finish is a
careful change to the scanner, which is a delicate part that affects every module — its own round. This
round ships the safe half (14 boxes built, no regressions anywhere) and pins down exactly what the next
round must do.

**WT → human → Claude.** Human: `<div class="activity interactive" number="NA"><div class="row"><div
class="col-12"> … </div></div></div>` per activity (TRR102_1.0 = 1A–1E; _2.0 = 2A–2D; …). Round 131 caught
3/28 (single-table). This round generalises to multi-table grouping + diagnoses the bundle class.

**Shipped.** `ContentConverter.#bilingualActivity` now takes the GATHERED activity blocks. When the reoMode
loop hits an activity marker (`#isActivityMarker`: a table carrying `[Activity Embedded]`/`[Activity:
Embedded]` or an "Activity NA:"/"Ngohe NA:" row) it gathers that table + the following widget-spec / content
tables — stopping at the next activity marker, a bilingual English|Māori content table (`#bilingualHeader`),
a callout (`#isCalloutTable`), a bundled item (`consumedBy`), or a non-table — into ONE `div.activity[number]`
(intro unfolded reo/eng, widget-spec tables as cv2 placeholders inside). **14 div.activity built.** No new
toggle (reoMode path → `REOTRANSLATE_OFF` reverts).

**Measured diagnosis (foundation, not finish).** Unzipping the TRR102 WT shows the BULK of activities are
`[Interactive] [Flipcards]`/`[Carousel]` — WIDGET BUNDLES the `InteractiveScanner` already claims
(`consumedBy`), NOT free tables. The standard engine ALREADY wraps bundles in `div.activity` (this file's
loop ~lines 555–591: `bundle.activityOwner` / `bundle.activityId` / `canonTag==="activity"`); it doesn't fire
for bilingual because the scanner never sets `activityId`/`activityOwner` for them — the number is in an
"Activity NA:" table ROW, not a `[Activity N]` TAG. **The full build is a SCANNER change** (feed the bilingual
"Activity NA:" rows + `[Interactive]` bundles into `activityId`/`activityOwner`), touching the bundle pipeline
corpus-wide → delicate, its own gate-proven round. This round's table-gather stops at `consumedBy`, so it is
isolated from the bundle path and regression-free.

**PROTECTED gates — all HELD (gate-NEUTRAL; isolated to reoMode).** Full bilingual reconvert, 0-stale:
skeleton SCAFFOLD ≥50% **766** / ≥75% **105**, compare_structure exact **7983** / EXTRA **151** / missing
**359**, defect-clean **96.1%** / leak **391**, body_compare **242**, tags **9557/9557**, flipCard divergence
**0**, speechBubble defect **0**. Files: `ContentConverter.#bilingualActivity` + helpers `#isActivityMarker`
/ `#bilingualHeader` / `#isCalloutTable` + the reoMode loop intercept. Spec §9b.

## 2026-06-27 (round 125) — BLL phonics OVERVIEW title casing + module-code chip (Chris, BLL210) (build 260617.04)

**Plain English (for Chris).** You compared BLL210 side-by-side and spotted two header differences. (1)
The little box top-left: the human shows the module **code** "BLL210"; the software showed the literal
word "MODULE". (2) The title: the human shows "Learning The Sounds – y, long vowels, silent e"; the
software shouted "LEARNING THE SOUNDS – Y, Long Vowels, Silent E". This round fixes BOTH for the BLL
phonics overview pages: the code chip now shows the module code, and the title is de-shouted (the
letter-teams stay lowercase like the human). It's reversible (one switch) and every quality check held.

**TRIANGULATED (BLL210, WT → human → Claude).** WT `[TITLE BAR]`: `*LEARNING THE SOUNDS* *–* *y, long
vowels, silent e*`. **Human** (`BLL210.html`): `<div id="module-code"><h1>BLL210</h1></div>` +
`<h1><span>Learning the sounds – <span style="text-transform:lowercase;">y, long vowels, silent e</span></span></h1>`.
**Claude (before):** chip `<h1>Module</h1>` + title `<span>LEARNING THE SOUNDS – y, long vowels, silent e</span>`
(the writer's ALL-CAPS lead verbatim; the site CSS `capitalize` then Title-Cased the lowercase
letter-teams → "Y, Long Vowels"). **Claude (after):** byte-identical to the human.

**ROOT CAUSE.** This is the BLL phonics PARENT/overview title — distinct from round 103's lesson form
"Module N - <teams>". `#normaliseTitleCase` already de-caps a WHOLLY-all-caps title (ENGC102 "KEEPING IT
REAL" → "Keeping it real") but SKIPS this one because the lowercase letter-team tail makes the string not
wholly upper. And the BLL overview `module_code` registry value renders the bare free-text literal
"Module" (2xx groups) / padded "00" (1xx) instead of the code.

**FIX (data-described, general, behind one toggle `PHONICSTITLE_OFF`).** `ContentConverter` splits a
phonics-overview title on `header.title_split.phonics_overview_split.pattern`
(`^(LEARNING|TEACHING) THE SOUNDS [-–—] (.+)$`) into `titleBar.phonicsLead` (de-capped via
`#normaliseTitleCase`), `phonicsSep`, `phonicsTail`. `SkeletonBuilder` renders the new
`header.title_h1_phonics` template (`<h1><span>{lead} {sep} <span style="text-transform:lowercase;">{tail}</span></span></h1>`)
and, on a phonics overview whose chip is the bare NON-numeric "Module" literal, shows `run.moduleCode`.
The round-103 lesson `module_prefix_split` is untouched (the new branch only runs when no "Module N"
prefix matched).

**MEASURED / scope (`outputs/_measure_phonics_title.py`).** The pattern matches **11 WT titles, ALL BLL**
(BLL110-170 + BLL210-240), **0 non-BLL** — self-scoping, 0 over-fire (the general all-caps de-cap for
ENGC102/OSAH501/AGH1003 is unchanged). **Title casing fixed on all 11/11** (de-capped lead + lowercase
letter-teams span, matching the human). **Chip exact-matched on 4/11** — BLL210/220/230/240 (the "Module"
bug) now show the code exactly like the human. Deliberately LEFT (non-derivable editorial): the 1xx
parents BLL110-160 (human omits the chip) + BLL170 (human shows the code) carry a padded "00" chip — the
human is split with no WT discriminator; and the human's TEACHING→Learning word swap on BLL110/120 is the
writer's content kept faithfully.

**PROTECTED gates (full fresh regen, 0-stale).** ALL `#header` → gate-INVISIBLE (the skeleton text-strips
the title; `KEEP_ATTR` excludes the `style` attr; compare_structure/body_compare/defect are `#body`-scoped)
