## 2026-06-27 (round 124) — TABBED LESSON NAVIGATION, stage 1: build the "[tabs] + bullet list" form the converter used to flatten (Chris) (build 260617.03)

**Plain English (for Chris).** Some lessons have a little **tabbed panel** — a strip of clickable tab
headings, each one revealing its own slice of content. The writers build these in the Word template, but
the converter wasn't building them: it left an orange "un-built" box (or a flat table) where the tabs
should be. This is a BIG class — the human builds proper tabbed navigation on **~127 modules** where
Claude flattens it. This round is **stage 1**: the cleanest, safest slice — a `[tabs]` panel the writer
wrote as a simple **bulleted list** ("• Term – description" per bullet). Claude now turns each bullet into
a real tab (the **Term** becomes the tab label, the description becomes the panel). It's reversible (one
switch turns it off) and every quality check held. It's deliberately small and safe — see "What's left"
below for the bigger, messier slices that need your steer.

**TRIANGULATED (HES1003, WT → human → Claude).** WT page 2.0: `[tabs]` followed by a flat 6-bullet list —
`• Whanaungatanga – can be described as…`, `• Aroha – …`, `• Mana – …`, `• Tiaki – …`, `• Wairua – …`,
`• Rongo – …`. **Human** (`HES1003_2.0.html`): `<div class="tabs"><ul class="nav nav-tabs"><li><a>Whanaungatanga</a></li>…(6 labels)…</ul><div class="tab-content"><div class="tab-pane"><p>…</p></div>…(6 panes)…>`.
**Claude (before):** an orange `cv2-interactive (un-built) #3: tabs` box holding the raw `<ul>`. **Claude
(after):** the human's 6-tab structure exactly (labels Whanaungatanga/Aroha/Mana/Tiaki/Wairua/Rongo).

**The signal + the build.** The reliable, derivable signal is the writer's explicit **`[tabs]` tag**. When
the captured widget has NO `[Tab N]` sub-tags and its members are a flat `• Term – description` bullet list,
`InteractiveBuilder.#tabsFromList` builds one tab per top-level bullet: nav label = the Term (before the
en/em-dash), pane = the description. Data `interactive_builders.tabs.list_opener`
(`split_pattern`/`bullet_prefix`/`min_tabs`/`max_label_words`/`max_trailing_lines`/`max_trailing_words`);
env **`TABLIST_OFF`** reverts to the placeholder. The existing `[Tab N]`-delimited builder is untouched
(the new branch only runs when there is no `[Tab N]`).

**NEVER HALF-BUILD (the guards).** It declines to the honest placeholder unless EVERY line is a clean
top-level `• Term – desc` bullet (≥2 of them, each Term ≤6 words), with no nested/indented sub-bullet, no
data table, image, video or extra widget type, and no red writer-instruction. Tabs-scanning does not stop
at a heading, so a `[tabs]` bullet list usually SWEEPS IN the next section's short lead (HES1003's
"Activity 2A", whose own activity box follows separately) — exactly what the human DROPS, so a SMALL
(≤2 lines / ≤6 words) trailer is dropped to match; a LARGER trailer means a real section was absorbed →
bail (keep the placeholder, lose nothing). The human REWRITES each pane's prose editorially, so only the
tab STRUCTURE + the derivable Term labels are reproduced (the pane text is the writer's own — invisible to
the text-stripped skeleton gate).

**MEASURED (the class + the over-fire sweep).** Corpus-wide the human builds body tabbed-nav on **127
modules / 260 tab-groups**; only **24 groups are text-only**, the other **236 are image/table/video-rich**.
The explicit `[tabs]` tag is in **39 modules** (34 with an un-built placeholder). This stage fires on the
**1** module whose `[tabs]` is the clean flat-bullet form (HES1003). **Over-fire check:** on the **6**
`[tabs]` modules the human renders as an **accordion or carousel** instead of tabs (EXPFUN06, ENFUN05/08,
OSBY501, HPFUN902, MXFU401) the builder did NOT fire — confirming the `[tabs]` tag is *not* a reliable
"build tabs" signal and the conservative guards hold. Tools: `outputs/_measure_tabnav.py`,
`outputs/_dbg_tabs.cjs`.

**PROTECTED gates (full fresh regen, 0-stale; A/B `TABLIST_OFF`).** HES1003-02 now matches the human's
6-tab structure: **raw structural match +8 (51→59%)**, scaffold HELD. Corpus-wide every protected gate
**HELD** at the round-123 baseline: skeleton SCAFFOLD mean **49.0%** / pages ≥50% **763** / ≥75% **105**;
structural-clean **96.0%** / literal-`[tag]` leak **424**; compare_structure exact **7808** / EXTRA **151** /
missing **336**; body_compare ANY **242**; tags **9557/9557**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0**;
speechBubble **defect 0** (43 built). No content lost (HES1003's activity box + content still render).

**WHAT'S LEFT (the deferred stages — need Chris's steer).** The other ~126 modules split into forms that
are NOT cleanly derivable from the `[tabs]` tag alone: (a) **heading-delimited text tabs** (`[H3]`/`[heading]`
per tab — PHE1005, EXPFUN06), entangled with the **tabs-vs-accordion-vs-carousel** editorial choice (no tag
discriminator yet); (b) **image-rich tabs** (a picture + text per pane, 2-column — PHE1003), the biggest
slice, needs faithful media + column rebuild; (c) **table-driven tabs** (the human turns a labelled/compare
TABLE into tabs — AGH1006 Advantages/Disadvantages, ~80 modules), the hardest discriminator. Each is its
own measured round; several need the scanner to terminate the tabs at the section boundary (today it
over-captures the next section). Reversible (`TABLIST_OFF`), data-described, general. Tool
`outputs/_measure_tabnav.py`.

## 2026-06-27 (round 123) — SIDE-ALERT side-by-side pairing: the freed tip-box sits beside its content, not below it (Chris, the round-122 logged follow-up) (build 260617.02)

**Plain English:** Round 122 finished freeing the writer's `[Side alert]` tip-boxes so each stands on its
own — but they landed in their OWN row, stacked BELOW the activity/content they belong to. The human
developer instead places each tip-box in a narrow column to the RIGHT of that content, side-by-side in one
row. Round 122 even logged this as the next job ("the side-by-side pairing recovers the skeleton"). This
round does exactly that: a side-alert now pairs as the right-hand column beside the preceding main content,
matching the human's layout. The software now pairs **63 of 64** side-alerts (was 0) — the same 99% the
human does.

**TRIANGULATED (BLL210, WT → human → Claude).** WT (`…_parsed.txt` 140/292): a `[side alert]` is authored
right AFTER the content it relates to (after Activity 1C / 2D). Human: each `alertActivity` is the RIGHT
sibling of a `col-md-8` main column inside ONE `<div class="row">` (`row > col-md-8{content} +
col-md-3/4{alertActivity}`). Claude (round 122): the `col-md-8` content row CLOSED, then the side-alert
opened its OWN `<div class="row"><div class="col-md-4"><div class="alertActivity">` BELOW it.

**MEASURED FIRST — the derivability test (`outputs/_measure_sidealert_pairing.py`, corpus-wide).** Of the
human's **100 alertActivity** boxes in the 43 `[side alert]` modules, **99 are PAIRED** side-by-side with a
preceding content column (**99.0%**); only **1** (BLL160) is own-row — the 1% editorial exception. The
preceding column is `col-md-8` in 92/99. A clean, strongly-derivable (B) positional convention.

**FIX (data `callouts.side_column_backward_pair:true`; env `SIDEPAIR_OFF`) — GENERAL + REUSABLE.** The
callout emit site already calls `rowFor("section")` for a boxed callout, which CLOSES the preceding content
row — so `parts` ends with `content_row_close` (= close `col-md-8` + close row) and the preceding column is
the default `col-md-8 col-12`, already matching the human. For a `side_column` callout, ContentConverter now
**un-closes that row** (pop the `content_row_close`), **appends the alert column** (`#sideAlertCol`, factored
out of `#calloutOpen`) as the right sibling, and **re-closes the row** — yielding
`row > col-md-8{content} + col-md-4{alertActivity}`. It falls back to the round-122 own-row form when there
is no preceding content row to pair with (page-start / consecutive alerts), so it can never mis-pair. The
behaviour keys on the def's `side_column`, so any FUTURE side-column callout pairs the same way — no
per-module code. The EXACT side width (col-md-4 dominant 48 vs col-md-3 44) stays editorial.

**RESULT.** Claude side-alert pairing **0 → 63/64 (98.4%)**, matching the human's 99/100. The single residual
(BLL140-00) is where the preceding structure isn't a standard `col-md-8` content-row close — a sized
follow-up.

**PROTECTED gates — full fresh regen (273 dirs, 0-stale).** **Drift-immune per-toggle A/B (`_ab.py
SIDEPAIR_OFF=1`):** firing set BLL210/120/110/160 — **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD mean +2.04** (8.48→10.51),
**compare_structure exact +5** (56→61), EXTRA/missing/body/defect/leak HELD; canaries ENGS302 (the different
`[Alert box on right]` positional form) / OSAH501 / ENGC102 — **ZERO delta on every metric** (the fix is
self-scoping to side-column callouts). **Full-corpus snapshot:** compare_structure exact **7808 (+32 vs
round-122 7776)** — the paired boxes now match the human's `row>col-md-8+col-md-4` wrapper chain across all
43 side-alert modules — EXTRA **151** / missing **336** HELD; skeleton SCAFFOLD mean **49.0%** / pages≥50%
**763** / ≥75% **105** HELD (the affected boxes are on low-scoring overview pages that don't cross the 50/75
thresholds, so the per-page mean + the most-granular structural gate improve while the threshold COUNTS
hold); body_compare ANY **242** HELD; defect-clean **1883/1962 = 96.0%** / leak **424** HELD; tags
**9557/9557 / REAL FAILURES 0**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0**; speechBubble **defect 0** (43 built) —
all HELD-or-IMPROVED. No protected gate regressed; compare_structure improved +32.

Reversible (`SIDEPAIR_OFF`, independent of `SIDEALERT_OFF`), data-described, general. FOLLOW-UP: the 1
residual own-row (BLL140-00, preceding structure not a standard content-row close); the exact side-column
WIDTH (col-md-4 vs col-md-3, editorial). Tools `outputs/_measure_sidealert_pairing.py`,
`outputs/_measure_sidealert.py`.

## 2026-06-27 (round 122) — GENERAL widget boundary: a standalone CALLOUT tag stops the widget eating it (Chris, BLL210 side-alert follow-up) (build 260617.01)

**Plain English:** In round 121 the software learned to build the writer's `[Side alert]` tip-boxes as
`alertActivity`, but 9 of the 64 sat RIGHT BESIDE an activity's interactive widget and got swallowed into
that widget's box (rendered inside the un-built placeholder) instead of standing on their own. Chris asked
for a GENERAL fix — not a side-alert special case — so that ANY writer tag in that position (a standalone
element immediately beside/after a widget whose capture eats the next tag) is emitted as its own element.
This round does that as a single data-driven, reusable rule, and now all 64 side alerts stand alone.

**ROOT CAUSE.** The interactive scanner has a data-driven list of tags that HARD-TERMINATE a widget's
member capture (`Interactive_Boundary_ChildTag_Bank._meta.member_rule.terminators_absolute` — it already
listed the callout tags `alert`/`important`/`whakatauki`/`quote`). Round 121 gave `[Side alert]` its own
canonical `side alert` (so it stops matching the bare `alert` substring) — but `side alert` was NOT in
that list, so a side alert abutting an activity widget was absorbed as a member (it used to terminate
*as* `alert`).

**FIX (data `…member_rule.callout_tags_terminate:true`; env `CALLOUTTERM_OFF`) — GENERAL + REUSABLE.**
`InteractiveScanner.ScanPage` now folds EVERY `Emit_Templates.callouts.by_tag` key into the absolute
widget-capture terminator set. So every registered standalone callout — `alert`/`important`/`wananga`/
`whakatauki`/`quote`/`supervisor note`/`side alert` and **any FUTURE tag added to `callouts.by_tag`** — is
automatically a hard widget boundary, with NO separate list to maintain. This is the general form of the
round-121 mechanism: add a tag's output shape to `by_tag`, and it is BOTH built correctly AND protected
from widget absorption, in one place. A callout beside/after a widget emits as its own element (the human
convention).

**RESULT.** All **64/64** `[Side alert]` now build standalone `alertActivity` (was 55; BLL210 1→3).
`outputs/_measure_sidealert.py`: claude alertActivity 55 → **64** (= the full `[Side alert]` population;
the human's extra 36 are a separate non-`[Side alert]` class).

**PROTECTED gates — full fresh regen (0-stale).** **Over-close PROVEN ZERO-delta** on widget-heavy
OSAH501/OSBY201/CEDR204 (A/B `CALLOUTTERM_OFF=1`) — adding `wananga`/`supervisor note` as terminators
changes nothing there (a widget never legitimately contains a supervisor-note/wananga box). compare_structure
exact **7776 (+7 vs round-121 7769** — the freed boxes now match the human's standalone `alertActivity`
wrapper chains); EXTRA **151** / missing 336 (HELD); defect-clean **96.0%** / leak 424 (HELD); tags
**9557/9557 / REAL FAILURES 0**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0** (HELD). **HONEST TRADE (documented,
Chris-requested build prioritised):** skeleton SCAFFOLD pages≥75% **105 (−2)** / ≥50% **763 (−1)** +
body_compare ANY **242 (+1)** — NOT a content error (all 64 sections/boxes correct, no content lost) but a
POSITIONING gap: the freed boxes render in their OWN row, while the human pairs them SIDE-BY-SIDE with the
preceding main content (`col-md-8` + `col-md-4` in one row). The most-granular structural gate
(compare_structure) IMPROVED; the text-stripped skeleton dips on the own-row-vs-side-by-side placement of
the 9 freed boxes (a few pages cross the 75% line). This is the round-94 `pendingSideAlert` side-pairing —
the LOGGED follow-up that recovers the skeleton.

Reversible (`CALLOUTTERM_OFF`), data-described, general. FOLLOW-UP: side-by-side pairing of a freed callout
with its preceding main content (recovers the skeleton; round-94 territory). Tool `outputs/_measure_sidealert.py`.

**Plain English:** Chris flagged that BLL210's ACTIVITIES weren't right — in particular the small
"side alert" tip-boxes the writer places next to activities ("If a letter is written as /e/…",
"Remember that if a word…"). The human developer renders these as a special **`alertActivity`** box in
a narrow side column; the software was rendering them as ordinary alert boxes. This round makes the
software recognise the writer's `[Side alert]` tag and build the correct `alertActivity` element —

**TRIANGULATED (BLL210, WT→human→Claude).** WT (`…_parsed.txt` 89/140/292): `[Side alert] If a letter
is written as / e /…`, `[side alert] Remember that if a word…`, `[side alert] If you feel you need more
practice…`. Human: each is `<div class="col-md-4 offset-md-0 col-12"><div class="alertActivity"><p>…`
— a narrow SIDE column holding an `alertActivity` (NO `alert` class, NO inner row>col-12 wrap, NO h4
lead). Claude: a plain `<div class="alert">` (it matched the bare `alert` substring; the "side" was
dropped). The activities themselves are correctly sectioned (1A-1F per section); the un-built widgets
inside them are the Phase-1 placeholders (fair). The genuine derivable defect is the side-alert class.

## 2026-06-26 (round 120) — BLL phonics inquiry HYBRID [page N] panel split: build the right sections (Chris, BLL210) (build 260616.99)

**Plain English:** Chris opened BLL210 and found the software had built the WRONG sections — the human
developer's tabbed lesson has 9 sections (Introduction, The letter y, Long vowels, Silent e, a_e, e_e,
i_e, o_e, u_e) but the software built only 7, and the last sections were mislabelled. This round finds
the cause and fixes it, so BLL210 — and 5 sibling phonics modules — now build exactly the right sections
with the right side-tab labels. Chris flagged that "the right sections + correct paginated boundaries"
must be enforced; this is that.

**TRIANGULATED (BLL210, live engine — the parsed.txt confirmed the markers; the live debug confirmed the
flow).** The human builds 9 inquiry panels (crumbs Intro/1..8 = Introduction + The letter y..u_e); Claude
built 7 (crumbs Intro/1..6, dropping o_e + u_e). Each section is authored as a HYBRID boundary — an empty
`[Tab N]` AND a `[Page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY AND a `[H#]` label, in the order `[Tab N][Page N][H#]` (BLL210)
or `[Page N][Tab N][H#]` (BLL130). But TWO sections (Long vowels, Silent e) open on a `[Page N]` ALONE
(no `[Tab N]` of their own).

**ROOT CAUSE (engine-debugged).** BLL210 is `_bllInquiry` mode (labelled crumb-list + empty `[Tab N]`
openers, round 100). It split panels on empty `[Tab N]` (line ~1029) + the round-101 consumed-opener
recovery (the trailing `[Tab N]` swallowed into each section's last `modal`), but **NOT on `[page N]`**
(that was the `cedInquiry`-only path, off here). So a `[page N]`-alone section (Long vowels, Silent e)
MERGED into the previous panel — and because the crumb LABELS come from the labelled crumb-list by panel
INDEX, every later panel's label shifted by 2 (o_e/u_e content rendered under the e_e/i_e labels). The 6
sentinels (`[Tab 1]`, `[Tab 4]`, + 4 recoveries) gave 6 panels where the human has 8.

**MEASURED the class corpus-wide FIRST.** Across the inquiry candidates the BLL phonics family under-builds:
BLL130 −1, BLL150 −2, BLL160 −1, BLL170 −1, BLL210 −2, BLL230 +1 (all the hybrid `[Tab N]`/`[page N]`
structure); BLL140/220/240 build 0 (a DIFFERENT detection failure — not this round); CEDK102/CEDR204/
CEDT101 −1 (a pre-existing cedInquiry over-build — untouched).

**FIX (data `inquiry_tabs.bll_page_split.enabled:true`; env `BLLPAGE_OFF`).** In `_bllInquiry` (NOT
`cedInquiry` — mutually exclusive) a top-level `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY ALSO opens a panel (closing any
open activity first, the round-101 idiom). **SYMMETRIC DE-DUP** so the `[Tab N]`+`[page N]` pair is ONE
boundary regardless of order: a `[page N]` is a no-op when the PREVIOUS body item is a tab-family opener
or a page boundary; AND an empty `[Tab N]` is a no-op when the previous item is a `[page N]` boundary. So
`[Tab N][page N]` (BLL210) and `[page N][Tab N]` (BLL130) both split ONCE; a consumed-opener's `[page N]`
defers to the recovery. General + data-described (no module hard-coding); the firing discriminator is
UNCHANGED (`_bllInquiry`), so a module with no standalone `[page N]` is byte-identical.

**RESULT — the whole BLL phonics family now matches the human panel count + labels + section-content
alignment:** BLL130 **7**, BLL150 **6**, BLL160 **6**, BLL170 **7**, BLL210 **9** (Intro/The letter y/Long
vowels/Silent e/a_e/e_e/i_e/o_e/u_e, each panel's first content heading matching its crumb), BLL230 **8**.

## 2026-06-26 (round 119) — INQUIRY [Tab N] opener ENDS the overview menu region: complete the under-built inquiry panels (Chris, anchor_compare inquiry round) (build 260616.98)

**Plain English:** Some lessons use a "tabbed" layout — a row of side tabs, each opening a panel of
content (TWHA901's overview has 11: Introduction, Agency, Resilience, … Curiosity). The software was
building only 9 of those 11 tabs on TWHA901 (and was short on TWHA903/906 too) — two of the panels
were getting silently merged into their neighbour. This round finds and fixes the cause, so the page
now builds all 11 tabs with the correct side-navigation, matching the human developer's page. It was
chosen by Chris from a fresh full-library `anchor_compare` run: TWHA901 was the SINGLE biggest
"writer tagged content the software dropped" case in the whole library.

**HOW IT WAS CHOSEN.** A fresh full-corpus `anchor_compare` (374/376 modules; consensus rebuilt
corpus-wide, null self-test 0.0) was aggregated by frequency (`outputs/_anchor_compare_class_ranking.md`).
The most-COMMON differences are editorial (column widths / layout nesting / menu styling — declined
again, see that file). The genuine derivable headline — `wt_loss` (writer tagged it, human built it,
Claude dropped it) — is dominated by the inquiry/fundamentals template families; **TWHA901 is the #1
`wt_loss` module corpus-wide (35)**. Chris picked the inquiry tabs.

**TRIANGULATED (TWHA901, live engine — the stale `_TWHA_inquiry_diagnosis.md` was PRE-round-112 and
is now superseded).** The scanner DETECTS all 11 `[Tab N]` openers correctly; the loss is in the
PARTITION. Debug-instrumenting `#partitionItems`/the body loop showed `page.items` has 19 tab items
but `bodyItems` has only 17 — `[Tab 1: Introduction]` and `[Tab 2]` are **`inBody=false`,
`consumedBy=undefined`**: they were routed into the MENU, not the body. So they never reach the panel-
sentinel push, and Introduction+Agency(+Resilience) collapse into panel 0. Both the diagnosis's "two
separate drops" (split-bracket + consumed-opener) turned out to be **one cause**: the partition swallow.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `#partitionItems`'s CONTENT-BASED overview-menu fallback (`menu.overview_section_labels`,
used when a combined-doc/single-file overview has no `[Module Introduction]` marker) walks the items
setting `inMenu=true` on a learning-design menu-section heading (Learning Intentions / Success Criteria
/ Planning / Connections / Assessment). The LAST menu section's `inMenu=true` then keeps swallowing the
following items — and `[Tab 1]`/`[Tab 2]` are tags, not headings, so nothing flips `inMenu` off — until
the first non-menu inquiry heading (`[H3] Agency`). So the first one or two panel openers are eaten by
the menu.

**FIX (data `menu.inquiry_tab_ends_overview_menu.enabled:true`; env `INQMENU_OFF`).** An inquiry
`[Tab N]` opener ENDS the overview menu region: once the first tab-family tag is seen, `pastFirstTab`
is set and the rest of the page is body (panels are always body content). Scoped to the
`overviewMenuIdx` content-fallback path; a module with NO tab-family tag on that path is **byte-
identical** (the guard only fires where a tab tag exists = inquiry-only). General + data-described (no
module hard-coding).

**RESULT — panel counts now match the human:** TWHA901 **9→11**, TWHA903 **4→5**, TWHA906 **5→7**
(all EXACT), with correct `class="crumbs"` side-nav (Introduction / Agency / Resilience / … / Curiosity).

cause — labelled tabs CONSUMED by the scanner [TWHA902] and in-bracket labels `[Tab N – Label]` whose
following content the `_labeledTabs` counter misreads, disabling inquiry mode [TWHA905 builds 0/7] —
a sized follow-up, NOT this round). Note: the panel-internal CONTENT fidelity (the `<li>` lists and
`[interactive: tick box]` widgets inside each panel) is a deeper layer the `wt_loss` content metric
still counts (TWHA901 stays 35) — this round corrects the panel STRUCTURE/count, which the structure
gates capture, not the internal list rendering.

## 2026-06-26 (round 118) — RED-RUN SPLIT-TAG BRIDGE: reassemble a uniform-red [tag] Word split with a stray space (Chris) (build 260616.97)

**Plain English:** In the Writers Template, the writer's tags are coloured red. Microsoft Word sometimes
chops a single red tag into pieces internally (for spell-check etc.). Chris flagged a case where a tag was
split across several red fragments. The converter ALREADY rejoins the common case (consecutive red pieces —
e.g. `[Tab 1: I` + `ntroduction` + `]` → `[Tab 1: Introduction]`, confirmed live). This round closes the one
remaining gap: when Word loses the red colour on an interior SPACE, the tag splits into two red spans with a
black space between — this now rejoins too, so the whole tag is read as one.

**HONEST SCOPE (important).** Chris's specific example (`[Tab 1: Introduction]`) was ALREADY handled by the
live `DocxExtractor` (the consecutive-red merge, round 79) — verified by direct inspection
(`outputs/_rawred.cjs`): the live parser outputs ONE span. The fragmented form Chris saw exists only in the
stale `*_parsed.txt` REFERENCE files (generated by an older parser; they lag the live engine). So this round
does NOT change the TWHA901 Introduction-panel drop (that is the separate partition issue,
`outputs/_TWHA_inquiry_diagnosis.md`). What it DOES fix is the **whitespace-gap** fragmentation variant the
consecutive merge missed.

**TRIANGULATED (raw Word XML, `outputs/_rawred.cjs`).** ANZH304: `[Please embed this journal story (as in
ANZHFUN01 phase 2]` — one uniform-red instruction, but Word split it `[red "[Please embed this journal story"]`
`[black " "]` `[red "(as in ANZHFUN01 phase 2]"]`. AGH1004: `[hover definition: the shape and features…]`
split the same way. The current red-merge loop (`while pieces[i].red`) breaks at the black space → two
fragmented marker spans.

**MEASURED FIRST (`outputs/_measure_redfrag.cjs`, live parser, compare_set under REDBRIDGE_OFF).** The
recoverable class — two red spans separated by WHITESPACE-only where the LEFT is mid-tag (more `[` than `]`) —
is **15 occ / 12 modules** (AGH1004, ANZH304, CEDT104, CEDT501, ENGJ301, EXPFUN06, OSAI201, OSBY301, OSBY401,
PHE1005, XGF9003, XTAS102). Rare because the consecutive case (already merged) dominates. The `[tag: black
label]` forms (a writer's intentional black label inside red brackets, e.g. `[Button: Interactive link:
<black>]`) are NOT this class — their gap is real content, not whitespace.

**FIX (data `Input_Doc_Rules.red_runs.bridge_split_tag`; env `REDBRIDGE_OFF`).** `DocxExtractor.#parseParagraph`'s
red-merge loop now BRIDGES a stray non-red whitespace run mid-merge — but ONLY when (a) the accumulated red
text is MID-TAG (an unbalanced `[`), (b) the gap run is whitespace-only, AND (c) the NEXT run is red. So it
reassembles ONE split tag and can NEVER merge across real black content or between two complete tags. General
+ data-described (no module hard-coding). Verified: ANZH304/AGH1004 reassemble to one span ON / fragment OFF;
`[Tab 1: Introduction]` (consecutive) still one span; `[Body]` + black "New Zealand…" stays its own span
(balanced brackets → no bridge).

**PROTECTED gates — drift-immune A/B (`_ab.py REDBRIDGE_OFF=1`, two batches: OSBY301/OSBY401/PHE1005/XTAS102/
ENGJ301 and AGH1004/ANZH304/OSAI201): ZERO effect on EVERY metric** (skeleton SCAFFOLD / compare_structure /
body_compare / defect-clean / leak all identical ON vs OFF) — the reassembled tags are gate-excluded
notes/instructions or inline content, so they don't move the structural gates. The fix is gate-NEUTRAL by the
tight guard. **Full fresh regen (365 stale → 0-stale, `_stalecheck.sh` OK).** Absolute corpus baselines
UNCHANGED from round 117 (1509 paired): skeleton pages≥75% **106** / ≥90% 6 (identical), tags **9557/9557 /
REAL FAILURES 0**, flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0**, speechBubble **defect 0** — all HELD.

Reversible (`REDBRIDGE_OFF`), data-described, general. New tools `outputs/_rawred.cjs` (raw live-parser block
inspector), `outputs/_measure_redfrag.cjs` (firing-set sizer). NOTE for future triangulation: the
`*_parsed.txt` reference files LAG the live parser (they show the old fragmented form) — trust `_rawred.cjs`
(the live `DocxExtractor`) over `_parsed.txt` when a red-run merge is in question.

## 2026-06-26 (round 117) — MENU LEAD-IN HEADING promotion: "We are learning:" / "I can:" → <h5> (Chris, anchor_compare top derivable class) (build 260616.96)

**Plain English:** Every lesson (and the overview) has a side-menu holding the learning intentions —
labels like "We are learning:" and "I can:" followed by a bulleted list. The human developer renders those
labels as small HEADINGS; the software was printing them as ordinary paragraphs. This round makes the
software match the human. It was chosen as the FIRST fix from a full-library `anchor_compare` run (Chris's
kickoff): of the genuinely-fixable inconsistencies it was the cleanest, largest, and lowest-risk (the menu
sits in the page header, so it can't disturb the main-page quality checks).

**HOW IT WAS CHOSEN.** A full-corpus `anchor_compare` (374/376 modules — TRR106/TRR114 have no converted
HTML at all) was aggregated by frequency into `outputs/_anchor_compare_class_ranking.md`. The raw top classes
(width/nesting/human_only) are mostly non-derivable editorial; triangulation flagged this menu-heading class
as the most-common cleanly-derivable one. Chris picked it from the top-3.

**TRIANGULATED (HES1007 lesson 1, WT→human→Claude).** WT: `[Lesson Overview]` → "We are learning:" + 2
bullets → "I can:" + 3 bullets → `[Lesson content]`. Human `#module-menu-content`: `<h5>We are learning:</h5>`
`<ul><li>…</li></ul>` `<h5>I can:</h5>` `<ul>…</ul>`. Claude (pre): the SAME bullets but `<p>We are learning:</p>`
/ `<p>I can:</p>` — the labels left as paragraphs.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `#promoteNamedHeadings` (round 46) already runs on the menu, but its phrase list has
"we are learning **TO**" (the WALT) — the lesson-menu labels fold to the bare "we are learning" / "i can",
which were never in the list, so they stayed `<p>`.

**MEASURED corpus-wide FIRST — the naive global add is NET-NEGATIVE.** `outputs/_measure_menuheading.py`
(over the dumped anchor_compare records): blindly adding the bare phrases to the global promotion gives, in
the menu, WIN 323 / LOSS 784 — because the human is INCONSISTENT (sometimes the label is `<h5>`, sometimes
`<p>`). Triangulating the win vs loss families (CEDR501/ENGI302 promote; BLL153/ENGJ202/ENGS401 keep `<p>`)
exposed the DISCRIMINATOR: the human promotes a lead-in to a heading UNLESS it is a **secondary lead-in under
a learning-design PARENT heading** ("Learning Intentions" `<h5>` → "We are learning:" `<p>`). Verified
corpus-wide on the human ground truth (`outputs/_measure_menuheading2.py`, 2502 lead-ins): the rule "promote
unless immediately preceded by another LD label, bullets reset the group" agrees with the human **83.9%**
(correct 2099 / wrong 403); the residual losses are dominantly the engFamily two_col menus that already SKIP
promotion (round 81 `skipMenuPromo`). Human level is dominantly **h5** (1164 vs h3 83 / h4 50). "i will be
able to" EXCLUDED (the human never promotes it).

**FIX (data `Emit_Templates.body_region.menu_lead_in_headings`; env `MENULEADIN_OFF`).**
`ContentConverter.#promoteNamedHeadings(html, isMenu)` gains a menu-only conditional branch: a `<p>` whose
folded text is in `phrases` (["we are learning","we are learning about","i can"]) is promoted to `<h{level}>`
(h5) UNLESS `precededByLabel` — the nearest preceding `<h*>`/`<p>` element is itself an LD label (`ld_labels`
= parents + lead-ins) AND no `<ul>`/`<li>` intervenes (bullets = a fresh group). The body call passes
`isMenu=false` (unchanged — the body never promotes these); the menu call passes `true`. Existing round-46
phrases are UNTOUCHED (no menu/body regression, no round-46 change). General + data-described (no module
hard-coding).

**RESULT.** HES1007/CEDR501/ENGS301/PES1007/OSGM501/OSBY501/MXFU402/OSOH501 lesson menus now render
"We are learning:" / "I can:" as `<h5>` matching the human (anchor_compare re-check: 93 menu lead-ins now
`h5←h5 identical` on the affected sample, 2 residual). The parent-guard correctly keeps the secondary
lead-ins `<p>` where a "Learning Intentions" parent heading is present.

**PROTECTED gates — drift-immune per-toggle A/B (`_ab.py MENULEADIN_OFF=1 <codes>`, two batches):**
- **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD — IMPROVED +0.51** (10-mod batch HES1007/CEDR501/ENGS301/ENGJ202/BLL153/
  AGH1001/PES1007/OSGM501/OSBY501/MXFU402; pages≥75% +1) and **+0.31** (5-mod batch ENGC302/MXFU301/ANZH401/
  ENGJ402/OSGM301) — both batches include the eng_family parent cases + the "i will be able to" exclusion.
- **compare_structure / body_compare / structural-defect-clean / literal-[tag] leak — HELD EXACTLY** on every
  A/B batch (the menu is `#header`-scoped → INVISIBLE to these body-scoped gates).
- **Full fresh regen (348 stale → 0-stale, `_stalecheck.sh` OK).** Absolute corpus baselines (1509 paired):
  skeleton SCAFFOLD **49.0%** / median 50.0% / pages≥50% **764** / ≥75% **106**; compare_structure exact
  **7734 (81.8%)** / EXTRA **189** / missing **327**; body_compare ANY **241**; defect-clean **1883/1962 =
  96.0%** / leak 424 occ/79 pages; tags **9557/9557 / REAL FAILURES 0**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0**;
  speechBubble **defect 0** — all HELD-or-IMPROVED (the per-toggle A/B is the drift-immune proof; the menu
  change cannot move the body-scoped gates).

Reversible (`MENULEADIN_OFF`), data-described, general. New tools `outputs/_aggregate_classes.py` (the
full-corpus class ranking), `outputs/_measure_menuheading.py`, `outputs/_measure_menuheading2.py`.
DEFERRED (measured, sized): the existing round-46 phrases ("you will show…" / "we are learning to") are still
promoted UNconditionally — the same parent-guard would FIX ~50 residual over-promotions under a parent
heading, but applying it to the existing set risks a small round-46 regression (17 human-promoted-under-parent
cases) so it is left as a follow-up; and the ENGJ-family lesson menus where Claude DROPS the "Learning
Intentions" parent heading entirely (a separate menu-structure issue, not this round).

## 2026-06-26 (round 116) — CAROUSEL ↔ trailing-[speech bubble]-table BOUNDARY + the linked/bulleted speechBubble BUILD (Chris, OSAH501-03) (build 260616.95)

**Plain English:** On OSAH501 lesson 3 the writer laid out TWO widgets back-to-back — a "What to do if
there is an incident" **carousel** (4 image+caption slides) immediately followed by a **Lawdog speech
bubble** (the dog image + a "Remember… / For further resources:" message with a bulleted Netsafe contact
list). Claude was leaving the carousel as an orange "un-built" box AND dumping the speech bubble's raw
table inside it. The human builds BOTH as separate widgets. This round makes the converter do the same:
the carousel stops at its last slide, the speech bubble gets its own bundle, and both build. This is the
anchor_compare principle in the flesh — the writer tagged two widgets, the human built two, the tags
correspond to the elements, so we build two.

**TRIANGULATED (OSAH501-03, WT→human→Claude).** WT (`…_parsed.txt` 341-371): `[H3] What to do…` → `[carousel]`
→ 4×(`[Slide N]` + `[image]` + `[body]`) → a 1×2 `[image] ║ [speech bubble]` TABLE (the bubble = 2 bold
`<p>` + 5 `•` bullets, two of them carrying `[LINK:]` hyperlinks). Human (`OSAH501-03.html` 774/845): a

img)(col-md-8 > bubble-basic no-hover bubble-right > div > p/p/ul)`. Claude (pre): `cv2-interactive #12:
carousel` placeholder whose member walk had ABSORBED the speech-bubble table (so `#carousel` saw a table
and bailed), and the bubble never got a bundle of its own.

**ROOT CAUSE (engine-probed, `outputs/_probe_osah_bundles.cjs`).** The carousel's `#swallowMembers`
treated the FOLLOWING `[image]║[speech bubble]` table as carousel data and swallowed it (`bundle.tables`
gained it) — exactly the failure round 96 had already fixed FOR FLIPCARD (`table_display_terminates_types`)
but the slideshow types were never added to that list. One absorbed display-table both (a) made `#carousel`
bail to a placeholder and (b) denied the speech bubble its own bundle.

**MEASURED corpus-wide FIRST (engine, `outputs/_measure_carousel_termtable.cjs`; candidate pre-filter
`outputs/_measure_carousel_candidates.py`).** 28 candidate modules (a slideshow opener + a display-invocation
table anywhere); the ENGINE firing set — a carousel/slideshow bundle that actually ABSORBS a table whose
direct invocation is a display widget — is **6 modules, all `[speech bubble]`: OSAH501-03, OSAI201-03,
OSAI101-01, OSAI301-01, OSAI401-04, ENGS401-01.** EVERY one is a currently UN-BUILT carousel placeholder
where the HUMAN builds `row carousel` + a SEPARATE `row speechBubble` (verified: each human file has
`row carousel`×1 + `row speechBubble`≥1; each Claude file had the carousel un-built). So the fix can ONLY
build toward the human — it never fires on a carousel that wasn't already a placeholder. (The static sizer
under-counted 6→2; the round-63 reference OSAI201-03 had silently DRIFTED to a broken placeholder — this
round repairs it.)

**FIX (3 parts, each data-flagged + env-toggled).**
1. **BOUNDARY (data `_meta.member_rule.table_display_terminates_types_slideshow: [carousel, rotateBanner]`;
   env `CARTBL_OFF`).** `InteractiveScanner.#swallowMembers` adds a guard mirroring the round-96 flipCard
   one: a slideshow bundle TERMINATES before a following table whose `#tableDirectInvocation` is a different
   display widget (`display_terminator_types` = speechBubble/flipCard/tabs). A plain image/video carousel
   table (no invocation) is still absorbed. The main loop's `#interactiveInTable` then opens the table as
   its own free-body speechBubble bundle.
2. **speechBubble image-only media (data `speechBubble.image_only_media:true`; env `SBLINKMEDIA_OFF`).**
   `InteractiveBuilder.#speechBubble` bailed at `media.length !== 1` — but `#harvestMedia` collects the
   bubble body's own `[LINK:]` URLs (mailto:help@netsafe.org.nz, the netsafe report link) ALONGSIDE the one
   iStock image, so any bubble that links out bailed. Now: count the iStock IMAGES (`#istockFilename`) and
   require EXACTLY ONE; still bail on a video or a 2nd image; the non-image link URLs are the bubble's own
   hyperlinks.
3. **speechBubble numbered-list guard (env `SBNUMLIST_OFF`).** The guard that bails on a numbered list
   matched `\d+[.)]` ANYWHERE — so the phone number "0508 NETSAFE (0508 638 723) within New Zealand" tripped
   it. Now it matches a number only at a " / "-PART start (a real list marker), so a phone number mid-bullet
   no longer blocks the build.

basic wrapper + `<p>/<p>/<ul>`) matching the human. OSAI201-03/OSAI101-01/OSAI301-01/OSAI401-04/ENGS401-01
now build + separate their speech bubbles (their carousels build where the per-slide capture is clean —
OSAH501 — and stay honest placeholders where the OSAI family authors the slides as a bare image list, a
SEPARATE pre-existing slide-shape issue, NOT regressed and noted as a follow-up).

## 2026-06-26 (round 111) — Task A: the [end X] leftover-leak (closer-residue suppression) (Chris) (build 260616.90)

Chris's Task A asked for a GENERAL `[end X]` "close the last-opened matching X" convention, framed as a
big generalisation (3,687 `[…end…]` tags / 375 modules). **MEASURED the class corpus-wide FIRST
(`outputs/_measure_endclosers.cjs`) and the loop reframed the task: the general convention is ALREADY BUILT.**

**FINDING — 97.9% already resolve.** Of the 3,687 `[…end…]` occurrences, **3,609 / 97.9%** already resolve to a
closer/boundary primary. The mechanism exists across three stages and is general, not per-form:
- `TagNormaliser.#resolveFragment` step 3 (prefix `^(?:end(?: of)?|/)`) emits a typed `end <canon>` CONTAINER_CLOSE
  / PAGE_BOUNDARY; step 3b (round-96 suffix `X ends?$`, CONTAINER_OPEN heads) does the reversed word-order; the
  lexicon `end other` bag + the catch-all `end` alias cover the rest.
- `ContentConverter` CONTAINER_CLOSE case pops the open container (type-agnostic LIFO); `InteractiveScanner`
  breaks the open widget bundle on ANY CONTAINER_CLOSE (line ~900); `PageSplitter` owns page/lesson.

The 40-occ "OTHER" residue is almost all content that CORRECTLY isn't a closer (iStock URLs `…west-end…` /
`…the-end…`, `[open-ended text box]`, instructions "check answers at the end") — the kickoff's "don't fire on
'at the end of the day'" guard is already satisfied by the resolver. The genuine resolution-gaps (`[carousel end
here]`, `[clickdrop ends here]`, `[quiz ends]`) produce NO output leak (the scanner already absorbs them).

**THE REAL ISSUE — downstream RESIDUE, not resolution.** Only ~21 `[end X]` survive into the page, every one an
ALREADY-UNDERSTOOD closer that printed as a LONE `<p>` because of the render context, NOT a resolution miss:
- standalone `<p>[End page]</p>` (a black/coalesced run): HIS1002 (black WT tag), HIS1005/HIS1006/ENGFUN02 (red,
  coalesced), measured RED vs BLACK per instance.
- a flowing **quote box** swallowing the close as a paragraph: HIS1005-03/-05 `<p>[End of Important box]</p>` /
  `[End of alert box]` inside `quoteText`.
- inside a built accordion's `accContent`: HIS1006-02 `[End Task]`; XGF9004 `[End interactive]`; XDLS502
  `[end supervisor note]`. (The TABLE-CELL cases — ENGS202/301 `[End page]`, CEDR501 `[End of … slideshow]` — are
  EXCLUDED: those cells leak the WHOLE overview/carousel block (`[Video]`/`[Slide N]`/…), a layout/widget-capture
  miss, not a closer-only fix. Recorded as a separate measured follow-up. ENGFUN02 fundamentals (150 leaks) also
  out of scope — a broken-page issue, its 4 `[End page]` a rounding error there.)

Chris chose (plain-English fork via AskUserQuestion): **"fix the real leftover leaks."**

**FIX (kickoff algorithm step 4 — SUPPRESS the literal closer). Data `body_region.closer_residue_strip
{enabled:true}`; env `ENDCLOSER_OFF`.** `ContentConverter.#stripCloserResidue` (an OUTERMOST body post-pass, before
`#inquiryPanels` so `inquiryActive` is unaffected) removes a lone `<p>\s*[bracket]\s*</p>` when the bracket (a)
carries the standalone word `end`/`ends` AND (b) resolves via the REAL `TagNormaliser` to CONTAINER_CLOSE /
PAGE_BOUNDARY (class `tag`). The **`end` word-guard is the precision floor** — measured (`outputs/_measure_closer_pstrip.cjs`)
it EXCLUDES a mis-resolved heading `[Lesson Summary]` (→ lesson/PAGE_BOUNDARY but no "end" → kept as the human's
heading) and the `[next page]` page-break openers; the **resolver-guard** excludes content (`[… near the end of a
book]` resolves to an OPENER `important` → kept). A bracket carrying embedded CONTENT (`[Lesson 2] THE WORLD
COURT`) is never a LONE `<p>`, so it is untouched.

**PROTECTED gates — clean full-6 A/B (ENGFUN02 HIS1002 HIS1005 HIS1006 XDLS502 XGF9004, ON vs `ENDCLOSER_OFF=1`,
both states regenerated + scored):**
- **skeleton SCAFFOLD 39.1% = 39.1%** (median 39.3% = 39.3%) — **HELD**; the −0.09 in a 2-module sub-sample washed
  out as small-sample alignment noise.
- **compare_structure exact 30 / EXTRA 0 / missing 6 — HELD EXACTLY**; **body_compare 2 / 2 — HELD**.
- **defect literal-`[tag]` leak 9 / 9 — HELD** (NEUTRAL by construction: the audit's `LITERAL_TAG` vocabulary lists
  only `[H#]/[Body]/[Image]/[Activity]/widgets` — it never counted closer tags, so removing them can't move the
  count; the 21 removed are REAL visible learner-facing junk the audit simply doesn't score).
- **tags 9557/9557 / REAL FAILURES 0 — HELD**; **flipCard TOTAL 37 / divergence 0 — HELD**; **speechBubble defect
  0 (17 built) — HELD**.
- **Surgical correctness:** OFF-vs-ON diff across the 6 modules removes ONLY closer `<p>` lines; the non-closer-
  removal sanity check is EMPTY (0 content lost). **Provably scoped:** the footprint scan over all 1962 pages finds
  lone-`<p>` end-closers in ONLY these 6 modules, and regenerating non-affected modules is **byte-identical**
  (BLL230/OSAI501/ENGC102 = 0 changed files) — the pass cannot alter any page without such a leak.

Gate-NEUTRAL, render-POSITIVE (21 visible `[End X]` removed; human ships 0) — ships on the "visible human-match,
gate-neutral" precedent (rounds 86/104). Reversible (`ENDCLOSER_OFF`), data-described, general (no module
hard-coding). The full-corpus 0-stale regen is folded into the session's combined backstop sweep (the per-toggle
A/B + the byte-identical scoping proof are the substantive gate proof, per the round-94/96 pattern). New tools
`outputs/_measure_endclosers.cjs`, `outputs/_measure_closer_pstrip.cjs`. DEFERRED (measured): the table-cell
closer leaks (ENGS202/301/CEDR501 — bigger layout/widget-capture misses); the ENGFUN02 fundamentals page;
black-text structural-tag leaks (`[LESSON N] Title` — round-73 black-strip territory). CLAUDE.md §11 + §14 updated.

## 2026-06-25 (TOOLING — no build bump) — anchor_compare MATCHER FIXED: rewording-tolerant relocation (Chris)

DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY (the measuring harness, NOT the converter — no AppVersion change, no converter
output change, protected gates UNAFFECTED). Full write-up: harness spec **Rev 9**
(`reference/Comparison_Harness_Design_Spec.md`) + plain-English `FINAL_MODULE_DATA/Measuring_Tool_Fix__PLAIN_ENGLISH.md`.

Chris's standing spec: the `wt_loss` matcher must decide a real loss by CONTENT tied to the same WT
tag — NOT exact text, NOT page position; the human's HTML has been revised so wording/placement/
structure all drift; moved+reworded content that's present somewhere in the Claude FILE is NOT a
loss; only genuinely-different/absent content is. Round 110 measured the old tool ~88% false alarm.

FIX (env `RECONTOL_OFF=1` reverts): `reconcile()` now (1) searches the ENTIRE other side — ALL pages,
not just paired ones (`build_corpus_all`), fixing the over-pagination blind spot (Claude 16 pages vs
human 5 → relocated content on unpaired pages was invisible); (2) builds its search blob from the
RAW page text so content inside a COLLAPSED Claude widget is found; (3) accepts a relocation when the
element survives VERBATIM, its 6-word head survives, or a 3-word run with a ≥6-char distinctive word
survives anywhere (`_phrase_present`) — rewording- and move-tolerant, with the distinctive-word/
contiguity requirement as the precision floor so genuinely-different content stays a real loss.

RESULT (measured all 340 modules, `outputs/_measure_wtloss_relocated.py`): `wt_loss` **4984 → 606
(−87%)**; 164 modules now 0; biggest residue = the KNOWN-deferred inquiry/fundamentals under-builds
(TWHA901/EXBP901/CEDT101/TEFUN08) — the genuine learnable set. Self-test still 0.0; skeleton gate
unchanged (1505 paired pages). Worked: HIS1006 126→1, XDLS912 113→1. The old formatted findings file
carries a SUPERSEDED banner; per-module new totals in `outputs/_wtloss_fixed_corpus.tsv`.

## 2026-06-25 (round 108) — INQUIRY CED CONSUMED crumb-list cut (Chris — anchor_compare CED follow-up) (build 260616.87)

Follow-up to the full `anchor_compare` run: after round 107 cleared the template OVER-fire, the worst-first
triage was led by the CED inquiry families UNDER-building (e.g. CEDW201 6.22, CEDW101 6.05, CEDO102 5.23,
CEDT208 4.91) — `MACRO[body_class(H:inquiry|C:container-fluid); crumbs_section(H:y/C:n); inquiry_section(H:y/C:n)]`:
the human ships a crumbs + `inquiryPanel` landing, Claude shipped a plain `container-fluid` page. Round 102
shipped the CED `[Page N]`-split for the ORPHAN crumb-list cut (CEDK101/CEDT404); this round extends it to the
CONSUMED crumb-list cut, the documented round-102 follow-up. `anchor_compare` was used as the microscope across
the whole loop (triangulate → fix → verify), the dedicated probes for the class discriminator, the protected
gates for ship.

**TRIANGULATED + MEASURED (`outputs/_probe_cedconsumed.cjs`, instrumenting the REAL `#detectInquiryCed` path).**
The brief's mental model ("the labels are eaten by the scanner so they never reach the detector") was MEASURED
WRONG — the detector scans `page.items` and DOES read the consumed labels. The four consumed modules each have
their `[Tab N]` crumb-list eaten by a `[tabs]` WIDGET bundle (`#0`), labels intact (incl. a leading
"Introduction"). The REAL blockers were two:
- **Alignment.** Round 102 fired only on `(openers + 1) == labels` (a leading pre-`[page]` intro panel). The
  consumed family opens the first ("Introduction") panel ON the first `[page N]` — `panels == openers == labels`
  (CEDO102: 6 labels / 6 free `[page N]` / 6 human panels). `(6+1)==6` is false, so it never fired.
- **The consuming widget.** The `[tabs]` opener is consumed by bundle `#0` but is NOT a `[Tab N]` (so not
  flagged `_inquiryCrumb`); it would reach the body-loop bundle-render and emit a duplicate `[tabs]` widget
  beside the crumbs.

Per-module structural read (so the discriminator ships only the clean case):

| module | crumb-list | `[page N]` | human panels | fires? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CEDO102 | 6 labelled, consumed by `[tabs]`, bundle ate ONLY the list | 6 free | 6 | **YES** — clean: panels==openers==labels |
| CEDW101 | 5 labelled + **2 stray empty `[Tab N]`** elsewhere → `pure` fails | 5 | 5 | no (deferred) |
| CEDT208 | 4 labelled | **2** | 4 | no — openers≠panels (non-`[page N]` split) |
| CEDW201 | 5 labelled | **1** | 5 | no — openers≠panels (non-`[page N]` split) |

**FIX (data `body_region.inquiry_tabs.page_split.consumed_crumb_list`; env `CEDCONSUMED_OFF`).** General, no
module hard-coding — three edits to `ContentConverter`:
1. **`#detectInquiryCed`** — accept the `openers == labels` alignment (in addition to round-102's
   `openers+1 == labels`) behind the flag, and when the crumb-list is consumed, collect the consuming bundle
   index(es) into `suppressBundles`. The strict `pure` (a clean labelled run == all tabs, 0 empty) + `≥2 in-stream
   [page N]` gates are UNCHANGED, so CEDT208/CEDW201 (openers≠labels), CEDW101 (`pure` fails), and every real
   `[tabs]`-widget module (0 in-stream `[page N]`) stay no-fire.
2. **Body loop** — a bundle in `suppressBundles` is marked emitted + skipped (its opener reaches the render path
   before the `_inquiryCrumb` members), so the `[tabs]` widget does not render; only the `div.crumbs` remains.
3. **`#inquiryPanels` cedMode** — when there is NO leading content before the first `[page N]` (`segs[0]==""`),
   the panels are the sentinel segments 1:1 (6 panels, not 7). Byte-identical for the leading-intro case
   (`allSegs === [intro, ...panelSegs]` reproduces the round-102 `panelSegs.length + 1` build → CEDK101/CEDT404
   unchanged).

## 2026-06-24 (round 106) — TEFUN fundamentals PHASE-TEXT panels (Chris, TEFUN02) (build 260616.85)

Chris asked me to compare the human-built TEFUN02 with Claude's output and, IF the divergence reflects the
normal format for these modules, refine the converter to reproduce it. The human ships a single-page
**Fundamentals** module built from a `div.phases` nav → `div.introduction` → one `div.fundamentalsPanel` per
PHASE; Claude rendered it **FLAT** — no panels, the bare "Phase 1/2/3/4" delimiters leaking as `<p>Phase N</p>`.

- **INVESTIGATION — is this the class norm? YES.** `phases`/`phaseLink`/`fundamentalsPanel` is the standard
  Fundamentals layout: **45+** human modules (ARFUN/ENFUN/HPFUN/MXFUN/SCFUN/SSFUN/TEFUN/XFUN/XGF9004) use it,
  and every TEFUN01-08 ships single-page with 4 panels. The engine ALREADY builds `fundamentalsPanel` for the
  HPFUN (`[New tab]`) and SSFUN (`[LESSON]`) families (rounds 98/99) — but the TEFUN family delimits each phase
  with a **PLAIN-TEXT "Phase N" line** (no tag), which neither path saw.
- **MEASURED THE CLASS BEFORE CODING** (`outputs/_measure_phase_delimiter.py`). EXACTLY **9** modules carry a
  standalone "Phase N" line: TEFUN01-08 (4 lines → 4 human panels each, CLEAN) + MXFUN01 (multi-file; Phase
  1/2/4 scattered across a 19-page split). **0 non-fundamentals, 0 gated** (no TEFUN is in `compare_set`).
  Discriminator: a SINGLE-FILE fundamentals page carrying ≥2 "Phase N" lines.
- **ROOT CAUSE — three consumers ate the bare "Phase N".** A plain-text line is invisible structural text,
  swallowed by (a) `#coalesceBlackRuns` (merged onto the intro body run — TEFUN02 "Phase 1"); (b) the
  `InteractiveScanner` (a quiz/widget over-capturing it as a member); (c) `#gatherFollowing` (a preceding
  `[Body]`/`[image]` element gathering it into its text + marking it `_consumed`, so the loop skipped it).
  Fighting each in turn was whack-a-mole — the fix normalises the delimiter FIRST.
- **FIX — phase-text PRE-PASS + `#fundamentalsPanels` branch + data-driven scanner terminator.** Data
  `Emit_Templates…fundamentals_panels.phase_text` + `Interactive_Boundary…member_rule.terminators_absolute_text`;
  env `FUNDPHASE_OFF`.
  1. **PRE-PASS** (`ContentConverter.ConvertPage`): in single-file fundamentals mode with ≥2 "Phase N" lines,
     split each black item on every "Phase N" line into a NON-black `{type:"phasebreak"}` marker — which
     `#gatherFollowing` (`next.type!=="black"` → break) and the coalesce both stop at, so the delimiter survives.
  2. The loop emits a panel **sentinel** at each `phasebreak` (closing any container the messy quiz markup left
     open — TEFUN's `[end quiz]`→"end mcq" is not a clean terminator).
  3. `#fundamentalsPanels` (phase_text branch) wraps the body: a `div.phases` nav (one tile per phase) + a
     `div.introduction` wrapping the pre-phase content + one plain `div.fundamentalsPanel phase="N"` per phase
     (NO generated heading — the phase keeps its own `[H3]` "Plan it!").
  4. **Scanner**: a data-driven `terminators_absolute_text` `["^phase N$"]` makes a standalone "Phase N" line a
     HARD widget terminator (so a quiz at a phase's end can't over-capture the next phase).
  EXCLUDES MXFUN01 (`page_model "multi-file"`). The title TEXT was already correct ("Planning and presenting");
  the `phaseLink` card IMAGES + the editorial Te Reo title are non-derivable → **deferred per Chris**.
- **RESULT.** **7/8 TEFUN EXACT** (4 nav tiles + 4 panels + introduction, matching the human); **TEFUN05 builds
  3/4** (its Phase-4 delimiter — uniquely after a `[page ends]` + `[dropdown list]` quiz — is consumed via the
  activity-lead path; content is intact, merged into panel 3; a documented follow-up).
- **PROTECTED gates — full fresh regen (273 dirs, `./_stalecheck.sh` = 0 stale) + drift-immune per-toggle A/B:**
  - **A/B (`FUNDPHASE_OFF=1`) on the TEFUN family: PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD +5.22 (6.52→11.75), compare_structure
    exact +31 (288→319)**, EXTRA / missing / body_compare / defect / leak HELD EXACTLY — a clear WIN on its target.
  - **A/B on gated FUNDAMENTALS (HPFUN101/201, SSFUN01/05, MXFUN01): ZERO delta**; on gated WIDGETS (ENGS302,
    OSAI501, OSBY201, ENGC201): **ZERO delta**. The phase_text path + scanner terminator are inert on the gated
    corpus (no gated module has a "Phase N" line).
  - flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0** — HELD; speechBubble **defect 0** (41 built) — HELD; tags **9557/9557
    REAL FAILURES 0** — HELD. My sentinels (`CV2_FUNDPHASETEXT`/`phasebreak`) leak **0**.
  - **Corpus snapshot (0-stale, 1169 paired):** skeleton SCAFFOLD **48.6%** / pages≥50% **585** / ≥75% **78**;
    compare_structure exact **6151** / EXTRA **167** / missing **247**; body_compare ANY **206**; defect-clean
    **1393/1463 = 95.2%** / leak 259 occ/70 pages. The absolute shifts vs the round-105 snapshot are the **+7
    newly-added TEFUN dirs** (TEFUN01,03-08 — previously absent from the Claude corpus) **+** shared-corpus drift;
    pages≥50%/≥75% + tags + flipCard + speechBubble HELD, and the per-toggle A/B is the proof that **no existing
    module regressed** and the TEFUN family **improved**.

New data flags: `Emit_Templates…fundamentals_panels.phase_text`, `Interactive_Boundary…member_rule.terminators_absolute_text`.

## 2026-06-24 (round 105) — SAME-BLOCK button/link absorbed INTO the callout box (Chris, OSAH501-01) (build 260616.84)

Chris flagged the OSAH501-01 alert (annotated three-pane screenshot): the human (GREEN) renders the Netsafe
external button INSIDE the `.alert` box, on the same continuous sentence as the warning text; Claude (RED) closed the
alert after the `<p>` and dumped the button in a SEPARATE row below it. The ask: "an external button that is within
the same continuous and uninterrupted sentence should be part of the element that is rendered along with the rest of
the sentence, and not use it as a boundary … differentiate this from the scenario of the external button tag a few
lines down which would then trigger a boundary detection and separate it from the preceding element." Build it
ROBUSTLY/generally, not a one-off.

- **TRIANGULATION (WT→human→Claude, OSAH501-01).** WT line 167 is ONE paragraph:
  `🔴[alert]🔴 ⚠️Remember … then report to🔴[external link button]🔴https://netsafe.org.nz/.` — the `[external link
  button]` sits MID-paragraph, in the SAME continuous sentence as the alert. Human (`OSAH501-01.html`): `<div
  class="alert"><div class="row"><div class="col-12"><p>Remember … report to:</p><a href="https://netsafe.org.nz/"
  target="_blank"><div class="externalButton">Netsafe</div></a></div></div></div>` — the button is INSIDE the box.
  Claude (pre): the `.alert` closed after the `<p>`, then `<div class="row"><div class="col-md-8 col-12"><a …><div
  class="externalButton">Go to website</div></a></div></div>` — the button broke OUT into its own row below.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `PageSplitter.BuildItemStream` splits the one WT paragraph into two TAG items — `[alert]` and
  `[external link button]` — that share the SAME source `block` object. `#calloutOpen` (STRICT mode) gathers the box's
  content via `#gatherFollowing`, which walks only BLACK items and STOPS at the first tag — so the button (a tag) was
  never pulled in; it then rendered as its own ELEMENT row in the main loop. The shared `block` reference is exactly the
  "same continuous paragraph" vs "a paragraph later" discriminator Chris described.
- **MEASURED THE CLASS BEFORE CODING** (`outputs/_measure_calloutbtn.py` WT-line scan + `_measure_calloutbtn_engine.cjs`
  full-corpus engine enumeration + `_probe_calloutrun.cjs` per-callout same-block run). Across the 197-set: **13 fire
  sites / ~9 modules** where a STRICT alert/important is immediately followed by a SAME-BLOCK button(ELEMENT)/external-
  link(INLINE) carrying a resolvable URL — OSAH501, OSAH301, OSGM101, OSAH401(×3), ANZH404, XGF9006, MXFL401(×4 across
  2 pages), HES1007, MXEO401. The human NESTS the button/link inside the box in EVERY verified case (OSAH501/OSAH301/
  OSGM101/OSAH401/ANZH404/XGF9006/MXEO401 eyeballed; the same-block boundary aligns EXACTLY with the human's box
  boundary — e.g. OSGM101's "Let's look…" prose is a DIFFERENT block so it correctly stays OUTSIDE; OSAH401's "for any
  digital… YouthLaw…" trailing prose is the SAME block so it correctly stays INSIDE). The **36 DIFF-block** cases (the
  CED `[alert.top]` + separate-paragraph `[Button]` families) are UNTOUCHED → the button stays its own row (matching the
  human's separated layout). The URL guard EXCLUDES a misresolved writer instruction carrying the word "button" but no
  link (`[please add a button to link to SSFUN07: Enterprise when available]`, SSFUN01) — its spurious button is left
  exactly where it was, never relocated.
- **FIX — `ContentConverter.#calloutOpen` (STRICT path); data `callouts.inline_continuation`; env `CALLOUTBTN_OFF`.**
  After the box's own content renders (and only for a `wrap_content` callout — alert/important), walk the SAME-BLOCK
  continuation from i+1: while the next item is a TAG in the SAME source `block` that is a button (ELEMENT, tag includes
  "button") or `[external link]` (INLINE) AND carries a resolvable http(s) target, render it via the normal dispatch
  (`#element`/`#inline`), push it INSIDE the row>col-12 wrap, and mark it `_consumed` (the main loop's existing consumed-
  skip drops the standalone copy). The walk STOPS at the first different-block / non-button-or-link / url-less item, so
  it can never over-capture. Same-block followers are always a contiguous run of tags (BuildItemStream attaches a
  paragraph's black text to its preceding tag), so this never collides with `#gatherFollowing` (black-only). The
  `absorbedInline` flag suppresses the spurious "Empty [callout]" red-flag when a box holds only an absorbed button.
- **PROTECTED gates — full fresh regen (266 gated dirs, `./_stalecheck.sh` = 0 stale) + drift-immune per-toggle A/B
  (`_ab.py CALLOUTBTN_OFF=1`, the round-92/102/103 pattern):**
  - **`CALLOUTBTN_OFF=1` A/B, batch 1 (OSAH501/OSAH301/OSGM101/OSAH401/ANZH404): PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD +0.23
    (58.90→59.13)**, every other decomposable gate HELD EXACTLY (compare_structure exact 180 / EXTRA 5 / missing 3;
    body_compare 0; defect-clean 96.00%; leak 8 occ/1 page). Batch 2 (XGF9006/MXFL401/HES1007/MXEO401/SSFUN01):
    **skeleton SCAFFOLD +0.08 (50.37→50.45)**, every other gate HELD EXACTLY (compare_structure exact 224 / EXTRA 14 /
    missing 25; body_compare 5; defect-clean 97.06%; leak 2 occ/1 page). SSFUN01 contributes 0 (its no-URL instruction
    button is not absorbed); the MathJax MXFL401 does not regress. **Net-positive on the PRIMARY skeleton; zero
    regression on any protected gate.**
  - **Corpus-wide snapshot (fresh, 0-stale):** skeleton SCAFFOLD **48.8%** / pages≥50% **585** / ≥75% **78** (1162
    paired) — corpus-level HELD (the scoped +0.2/+0.08 gain doesn't flip a ≥50%/≥75% threshold or move the rounded mean;
    the A/B is the proof); structural-clean **1387/1456 = 95.3%** / literal-`[tag]` leak **258 occ/69 pages** (+1
    sentinel) — HELD EXACTLY; compare_structure exact **5877 (81.4%)** / EXTRA **164** / missing **244** — HELD EXACTLY
    (the absorbed button is text-unmatched — its label differs from the human's — so its chain change is skeleton-only);
    body_compare ANY **205** (over-capture 57 / runaway 5 / empty 146) — HELD EXACTLY; tags **9557/9557 REAL FAILURES
    0**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0**; speechBubble **defect 0** — all HELD.
- **SCOPE / out of scope.** Position only — the button's LABEL ("Go to website" default vs the human's editorial
  "Netsafe"/"Netsafe Gaming Toolkit"/"Whina preview") and CLASS (`button` vs `externalButton` for a plain `[Button]`)
  are pre-existing non-derivable editorial differences, unchanged. A button the human nests that lives in a DIFFERENT WT
  paragraph (ANZH404's 2nd "Ngā Taonga" button; OSAH401-01's separate-paragraph external link) is the harder multi-
  paragraph-box capture — left for a follow-up; this round never regresses it (those buttons stay where they were).

New data flag: `Emit_Templates.callouts.inline_continuation`. New env toggle: `CALLOUTBTN_OFF`. Tools:
`outputs/_measure_calloutbtn.py`, `outputs/_measure_calloutbtn_engine.cjs`, `outputs/_probe_calloutrun.cjs`.

## 2026-06-24 (round 104) — OSAH501: stray-punctuation embedded-lead drop + speechBubble multi-`<p>` wrapper-div; widget-verifier gate repair (Chris) (build 260616.83)

Chris flagged two OSAH501 defects (annotated three-pane screenshots) and asked that BOTH be fixed ROBUSTLY/generally, not as one-offs. While proving the gates I also found and repaired a silent staleness in all 8 widget verifiers.

### Fix 1 — STRAY-PUNCTUATION embedded lead (OSAH501-00 whakataukī ":")

- **TRIANGULATION (WT→human→Claude, OSAH501-00).** WT: `🔴[RED TEXT] [whakatauki]:  [/RED TEXT]🔴Mā te whakarongo, ka mōhio, … | Through listening …` — the writer glued a stray **`:`** to the tag (inside the red span). Human (`OSAH501-00.html`): `<div class="whakatauki"><p>Mā te whakarongo …</p><p>Through listening …</p></div>` — clean. Claude (pre): `<div class="whakatauki"><p><b>:</b></p><p>Mā te whakarongo…</p><p>Through listening…</p></div>` — a spurious leading `<p><b>:</b></p>`.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `TagNormaliser.RenderText` keeps text OUTSIDE a tag's brackets (`[H1] INTRODUCTION` → `INTRODUCTION`). For `[whakatauki]:` it folds the tag and returns the residue `":"`. `ContentConverter.#calloutOpen` then treats that as the box's embedded LEAD and emits `<p><b>:</b></p>`.
- **MEASURED THE CLASS BEFORE CODING** (`outputs/_measure_strayleadpunct.cjs` over the full 197-set; `outputs/_measure_strayleadpunct_wt.py` for the WT upper bound). **42** RenderText results are punctuation-only across **26** modules: `]`×27 (doubled/`[[H2]` brackets), `(`×6 (`[alert.top.] (` — CEDO/R/T/W501, XDLS905), `:`×4 (OSAH501 + **OSAH301** whakataukī, SSFUN01 `[Insert Alert - RHS]:`, SSFUN07 `[Title]:`), `.`×2, `|`×1, `.]`×1, `).`×1. EVERY one is pure writer noise; the human renders **none** (verified OSAH301 clean whakataukī, CEDR501 alert keeps only its real Collins-dictionary link).
- **FIX — `TagNormaliser.RenderText`; data `Input_Doc_Rules.render_text.drop_punctuation_only:true`; env `STRAYLEAD_OFF`.** After extracting the outside-bracket text, if it contains **NO letter or digit in any script** (`/[\p{L}\p{N}]/u` — te reo macrons ā/ē/ī/ō/ū are `\p{L}`, so reo is never dropped) it returns `""`. GENERAL across every tag and every RenderText caller; the `|| blackAfter` fallback chains now fall through to the real content. CONSERVATIVE: a residue with even one letter/digit (a genuine embedded title/label) is untouched, so it can never strip real content — robust to ANY erroneous glued character, exactly as Chris asked.

### Fix 2 — speechBubble MULTI-`<p>` WRAPPER DIV (OSAH501-01; a RECURRING miss Chris re-flagged)

- **TRIANGULATION (WT→human→Claude, OSAH501-01).** WT table cell: `[static speech bubble] *Tēnā koe! … the law.*  / *Online Abuse … referred to as* ***OAH****.*` — a 2-paragraph bubble (` / ` split). Human: `<div class="bubble-basic no-hover bubble-right"><div><p>…</p><p>…</p></div></div>` — an EXTRA `<div>` wraps the `<p>`s inside a `bubble-basic` element. Claude (pre): `<div class="bubble-right no-hover"><p>…</p><p>…</p></div>` — no `bubble-basic`, no wrapper `<div>`.
- **MEASURED THE CLASS BEFORE CODING** (`outputs/_measure_bubble_wrapper.py` + `outputs/_measure_builtbubble_human.py`, mapping every builder-built multi-`<p>` bubble to its human counterpart). Of the builder's multi-`<p>` bubbles whose HUMAN counterpart is **genuinely** multi-`<p>` (n=12), **12/12 (100%) use `bubble-basic` AND a wrapper** (11 `<div>`, 1 hand-styled `<span>`) — OSAH501-01/02/03, OSAI501-01/02, OSGM101/401, OSBY201-02, OSOH501, OSAI401. The apparent "direct-`<p>`" exceptions (MXFU402, OSAI201, OSBY201-01) are a SEPARATE pre-existing divergence: the human used ONE `<p>` with `<br><br>` where the builder splits ` / ` into two `<p>` (out of scope). The bulleted `build_list` bubble (OSBY201-02) ALSO uses `bubble-basic` + wrapper.
- **FIX — `InteractiveBuilder.#speechBubble`; data `Emit_Templates…speechBubble.multi_wrapper`; env `SBWRAP_OFF`.** When the bubble body is **> 1 `<p>`** (the ` / ` multi-paragraph path) OR a bulleted block, emit `<div class="bubble-basic no-hover bubble-{side}"><div>{block}</div></div>` (the multi-paragraph path now composes a complete `<p>…</p><p>…</p>` block). **Single-`<p>` bubbles are UNCHANGED** (Chris's rule is strictly "> 1 `<p>`"; the single-`<p>` shape varies in the corpus and is left alone). ## 2026-06-24 (round 103) — BLL "Module N -" title-bar prefix → MODULE chip + lowercase title (Chris, BLL232) (build 260616.82)

Chris flagged the BLL232 overview header (annotated three-pane screenshot): the human (GREEN) renders the
`#module-code` chip as **MODULE 2** and the title as **oe, ow, ir, ur, …** (lowercase), where Claude (RED) showed
the generic chip **MODULE** and kept the WHOLE **Module 2 - oe, ow, …** as the title. "Look into how the human has
structured the module name and code … how this is interpreted from the writers template … check if this is
consistent amongst the other BLL modules, and if so implement it … whenever dealing with BLL modules in future."

- **TRIANGULATION (WT→human→Claude, BLL232-0.0).** WT `[TITLE BAR]` payload = `*Module 2 - oe, ow, ir, ur, ui, ew,
  au, aw, al, ph, kn, wr*`. Human OVERVIEW: `<div id="module-code"><h1>Module 2</h1></div>` + `<h1><span
  style="text-transform:lowercase;">oe, ow, …</span></h1>`; human LESSONS: chip `1.0`/`2.0` (decimal) + the SAME
  lowercase title. Claude (pre): chip `<h1>Module</h1>` (the generic free-text) + `<h1><span>Module 2 - oe, ow,
  …</span></h1>` (un-split, un-lowercased — the site CSS Title-Cases it to "Oe, Ow, …").

- **MEASURED THE CLASS BEFORE CODING (`outputs/_measure_module_prefix.py`, all 202 modules).** EXACTLY **49** WT
  title bars carry a leading `Module N <sep>` prefix — **ALL BLL, 0 non-BLL** (the discriminator is self-scoping; no
  over-fire risk to any other subject). (1) The human STRIPS the prefix from the title h1 in **49/49** — **0 cases
  keep "Module N" in the title** (over-fire-safe). (2) Lowercase span on the title h1: **44/44** parseable (the rest
  confirmed by hand). (3) The chip NUMBER tracks the **module CODE's last digit (44/46)**, NOT the writer's
  title-bar prefix (42/46): where they differ — BLL142 (WT "Module 3" / code …2 / human "Module 2"), BLL147 ("Module
  5"/…7/"Module 7"), BLL154 ("Module 3"/…4/"Module 4") — the writer typo'd the prefix and the human used the code.
  The 2 code-last-digit misses (BLL166 a human copy-paste "Module 2" for code …166; BLL143 labelled "Module 4" same
  as BLL144 — a human dup) + the 3 full-code chips (BLL176/177/252 ship "BLL17x") are NON-DERIVABLE editorial
  deviations — and ALL of this is in `#header`, so it is INVISIBLE to every gate (see below).

- **FIX — `ContentConverter.#partitionItems` (strip) + `SkeletonBuilder.#buildHeader` (chip + lowercase template) +
  `ConversionRun`/`PageAssembler` (the run.modulePrefix flag); data `header.title_split.module_prefix_split` (+
  `title_h1_lowercase`); env `MODPREFIX_OFF`.** The title-bar parse matches the data regex `^Module \d+ <sep>(.+)$`
  (sep = spaced `- – — :`); on a fire it sets `payload = remainder`, `titleBar.modulePrefix = true`, and keeps
  `titleBar.rawEnglish` (the full pre-strip title). PageAssembler shares `run.modulePrefix` module-wide (so every
  lesson's title h1 also gets the lowercase span); SkeletonBuilder overrides the OVERVIEW chip to `Module {last-digit
  of moduleCode}` and wraps the title in `<span style="text-transform:lowercase;">`. The whole behaviour reverts via
  `MODPREFIX_OFF` (or `enabled:false`): no strip → flag stays false → generic chip + un-split, un-lowercased title.

- **COMPANION DEDUP FIX (required — else the strip CREATES a body leak).** BLL232 has a mid-doc `[Title]` alias whose
  text EXACTLY repeats the title bar ("Module 2 - oe, …"); the overview title-dedup (`#partitionItems`
  SECTION_MARKER) consumed it because it matched `#pageEnglishTitle`. After stripping the title to "oe, …", that
  match failed and the alias LEAKED as `<h3>Module 2 - oe, …</h3>` in `#body` (a false skeleton +0.27 — a leaked
  heading coincidentally aligning with the human's leading `<h3>Introduction</h3>` row). FIX: the dedup now also
  matches `#pageRawTitle` (the full pre-strip title; `titleBar.rawEnglish`), so the alias stays consumed EXACTLY as
  before — BLL232's `#body` is byte-identical to its pre-change state. (Non-BLL: `#pageRawTitle` is "" → the new
  clause is inert.)

- **RESULT.** BLL232 overview now EXACTLY matches the human (chip "Module 2"; title `<h1><span
  style="text-transform:lowercase;">oe, ow, …</span></h1>`); lessons keep the `1.0`/`2.0` chip and gain the lowercase
  title. Across the regenerated 49-module family: title prefix stripped 49/49; lowercase 44/44; chip == human 40/44
  (the 4 misses are the gate-invisible human chip inconsistencies above). Non-BLL canaries OSAI201/CEDW501/ENGC102
  byte-identical (chip = full code; bilingual pipe/dash splits intact; no lowercase span).

**PROTECTED gates — drift-immune A/B (`_ab.py MODPREFIX_OFF=1 <codes>`, the round-92/102 pattern; the shared corpus
may be mid-drift so the proof is the per-toggle A/B):** the change is `#header`-scoped and **gate-INVISIBLE by
construction** — the skeleton text-strips content + `KEEP_ATTR` excludes `style` (so the chip text, title text, and
lowercase `style` attr all collapse to identical nodes), and `compare_structure`/`body_compare`/`structural-defect`
leak-scan are all `#body`-scoped. **A/B over 25 modules (22 BLL prefix + OSAI201/CEDW501/ENGC102 canaries): ZERO
effect on EVERY metric** — skeleton SCAFFOLD mean / pages≥50% / ≥75% HELD, compare_structure exact/EXTRA/missing
HELD, body_compare ANY HELD, structural-clean % HELD, literal-`[tag]` leak HELD. **tags 9557/9557 (REAL FAILURES 0)
— HELD; speechBubble defect 0 — HELD; flipCard — UNTOUCHED** (no tag/widget/body path changed). 0-stale verified on
the 49-module affected family (147 files fresh vs the edited sources). So no protected gate regressed — a pure
visible-fidelity match to the human header. New data `header.title_split.module_prefix_split` (+ `title_h1_lowercase`);
new env toggle `MODPREFIX_OFF`. Tool: `outputs/_measure_module_prefix.py`. DEFERRED (sized, separate convention): the
PRE-EXISTING mid-doc `[Title]`-alias body leak in 6 modules (BLL142/151/154/165/213/214) whose alias text DIFFERS
from the title bar (reordered/extra sounds, different dash) so the exact-fold dedup never matched it (present in OFF
too — A/B-confirmed neutral); the human renders these as `<h3>Introduction</h3>` (4/5) — a corpus-wide `[Title]`-
alias→"Introduction" convention that needs its own measured round (the current code consumes exact repeats to

## 2026-06-24 (round 102 / TEMPLATES round D-followup) — INQUIRY CED [Page N]-split family, the ORPHAN crumb-list cut (Chris) (build 260616.81)

Round 100/101 shipped the INQUIRY tabbed template for the BLL `[Tab N]`-label-list family (panels open on EMPTY `[Tab N]`). The brief's next SECONDARY win is the **CED `[Page N]`-split family**, where the panels are delimited NOT by empty `[Tab N]` but by in-stream `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY markers — a different mechanism the round-100 detector can't see. Chris chose this lane. This round ships the **ORPHAN crumb-list sub-family (CEDK101, CEDT404)** — the easy first cut; the CONSUMED sub-family is the documented follow-up.

- **TRIANGULATION (WT→human→Claude, CEDK101).** WT: overview → `[End page]` → `Side Tabs:` + a `[Tab 1] Introduction … [Tab 6] Heat Technology` crumb-label list → `[MODULE INTRODUCTION]` + intro body/video → `[end page]`/`[page 2]` → `[H2]`+activities → `[Page 3..6]` (mixed case). Human (`CEDK101_0.html`): `<body class="inquiry container-fluid">`, `#body > div.crumbs` (`crumb="0".."5"`, labels from the tab list), 6 stacked `div.inquiryPanel` (first showing), `#footer > ul.footer-nav.inquiry-nav` (home/prev/next). Claude (pre): body class already `inquiry container-fluid` (round-97 resolver) but the tab labels leaked as plain `<p>` in `#module-menu-content`, NO crumbs, NO panels, content flat, empty `#footer`.

- **ROOT CAUSE.** All 6 CED targets are `page_model:single-file` (CEDO102 a recorded exception), so `[page N]`/`[end page]` stay IN-STREAM as section breaks (the SSFUN round-99 precedent) — they do NOT pre-split the module (every CED module is one Claude page). The round-100 detector requires ≥2 EMPTY `[Tab N]` openers; the CED family has a PURE labelled crumb-list (0 empty openers) and opens panels on `[page N]` instead, so it never fired. And the label run can land in EITHER partition: CEDK101's sits in the MENU (before `[Module Introduction]`), CEDT404's in the BODY (after it).

- **MEASURED THE CLASS BEFORE CODING (`outputs/_probe_cedpage.cjs`, run over ALL 27 corpus modules carrying both `[Tab N]` and `[page N]`).** EXACTLY 2 fire the proposed rule — **CEDK101 + CEDT404** — and BOTH predict the human panel count EXACTLY (6/6). The CONSUMED sub-family (CEDO102/CEDT208/CEDW201/CEDW101) has its labels eaten by the scanner (`oL=0`) → does not fire (the follow-up). BLL230 keeps its round-100 path (it has empty openers). **OVER-FIRE CHECK PASS: 0 of the 27 candidates + the watch-list (BLL236/232, MXDB202, OSAI501, ENGJ301/402, XGF9003, MXFL301, PNR101…) fire** — every real `[tabs]`-widget module carries 0 in-stream `[page N]`, the clean discriminator.

- **FIX — `ContentConverter.#detectInquiryCed` (new) + the body-loop PAGE_BOUNDARY hook + `#inquiryPanels` page_split mode + the menu/body suppression flag + `SkeletonBuilder` footer shell; data `body_region.inquiry_tabs.page_split` (+ `footer_nav_links`); env `CEDPAGE_OFF`.** `#detectInquiryCed` scans the FULL page stream and FIRES only when ALL hold: a consecutive labelled `[Tab N]` run ≥3 that EQUALS the module's total `[Tab N]` (a pure crumb-list), 0 empty openers, ≥2 in-stream `[page N]` openers, AND panels(openers+1) == crumbs(labels). On a fire it captures the labels in order and flags each label item `_inquiryCrumb` (the menu builder AND body loop `continue` past them). In the body loop a top-level `[page N]` closes any open activity (round-101 idiom) then pushes the panel sentinel. `#inquiryPanels` page_split mode wraps the body into N UNIFIED crumbs (the first tab IS the intro — NO separate "Introduction" crumb, distinct from BLL) + N `inquiryPanel`s (first showing); `content.cedInquiry` makes `SkeletonBuilder` emit the fixed home/prev/next `ul.footer-nav.inquiry-nav` ONLY when the registry gave no footer links (single-file CED → empty footer), so round-100 BLL footers are byte-unchanged. Crumb/panel index VALUE is editorial + skeleton-invisible (KEEP_ATTR excludes rel/crumb); 1-indexed matches CEDT404 exactly.

- **RESULT.** CEDK101 + CEDT404 each build `<body class="inquiry container-fluid">` + `div.crumbs` (6 correctly-labelled crumbs, first showing) + 6 `div.inquiryPanel` (first showing) + the `footer-nav inquiry-nav` shell; div-balanced, 0 sentinel leaks, no stray label `<p>`.
