## 2026-06-24 (round 101 / TEMPLATES round D-followup) — INQUIRY consumed/trapped opener RECOVERY (Chris) (build 260616.80)

Round 100 shipped the INQUIRY tabbed template but DOC'd that "panels under-build on most (2-7 vs human 6-9)". Re-measured the class live (the corpus had drifted 1412/1426 stale, so I regenerated the inquiry set first): of the gated BLL `[Tab N]` label-list family, the firing modules emit only **2 panels** where the human has **6-9**. This round recovers the missing panels — a pure panel-COUNT fix on the ALREADY-firing family (the discriminator is UNCHANGED, so zero new over-fire risk).

- **TRIANGULATION + ROOT CAUSE (BLL160, engine probe `outputs/_probe_inqcoverage.cjs`).** The human splits one `inquiryPanel` per `[Tab N]`; the WT puts a crumb-label list (`[Tab 1] The letter y` …) then an EMPTY `[Tab N]` PANEL OPENER before each sound-group's activities (numbered by tab: 1A-1G, 2A-2H …). Claude built only 2 panels because the empty openers never reached the panel-open path in TWO ways: (a) **SWALLOWED by the scanner** — the opener directly after a widget is absorbed as that widget's last member (BLL150/160/170/210: a trailing `[Tab N]` eaten by the activity's final `modal`; TWHA902: a `carousel`); (b) **TRAPPED in an open activity** — an orphan opener reached `ContentConverter` while the previous tab's last `[Activity]` was still open (`!stack.length` false), so it fell through to the orphan-RED-FLAG path (BLL210 leaked 1).

- **MEASURED THE CLASS BEFORE CODING (`outputs/_probe_tabconsume.cjs`, all 45 `[Tab N]` modules).** Exactly **6 modules** absorb an empty `[Tab N]` into a NON-`[tabs]` widget: **5 inquiry** (BLL150/160/170/210 via modal, TWHA902 via carousel) + **ENGJ402** (an accordion the writer mis-tagged — human ships 0 panels). The 6th is the safety key: ENGJ402 does NOT fire inquiry (0 empty openers post-scan), so gating the recovery on CONFIRMED firing protects it perfectly. Real `[tabs]` widgets (ENGJ301/XGF9003) keep their `[Tab N]` members — they are skipped by the `bundle.type !== "tabs"` guard.

- **FIX — `ContentConverter` (2 converter-only changes, no scanner surgery); data `body_region.inquiry_tabs.recover_consumed_openers:true`; env `INQRECOVER_OFF`.** Both gated on `inquiryMode` (computed POST-scan → the round-100 firing discriminator is byte-unchanged). **(1) Consumed-opener recovery** (consumed-bundle emit path): a NON-`[tabs]` bundle whose TRAILING members are empty `[Tab N]` closes any open activity (mirrors the new-activity close idiom) and pushes one `<!--CV2_INQPANEL-->` per swallowed opener — restoring the panel boundary WITHOUT un-consuming the tag (no leak). **(2) Trapped-opener split** (SUBTAG path): a top-level empty `[Tab N]` reached while an activity is open closes that activity first so it splits the panel instead of leaking an orphan flag. Both reuse the round-100 sentinel + `#inquiryPanels` (crumb labels still come from the orphan `[Tab N] <label>` list, assigned by panel index).

- **RESULT.** BLL150 **2→4**, BLL160 **2→5**, BLL170 **2→6**, BLL210 **2→7** (and its 1 orphan-`[tab]` flag removed); BLL230 unchanged (7, no consumed openers → byte-identical). All div-balanced, 0 orphan-`[tab]` flags, 0 sentinel leaks. Remaining off-by-one (BLL150 4/6, BLL210 7/9) is the documented WT opener-omission, not a bug. TWHA902 unchanged (2/9) — its heading-label sub-family needs the separate heading-derived-label mechanism (follow-up); no regression.

**PROTECTED gates — drift-immune A/B (`_ab.py INQRECOVER_OFF=1 <codes>`; the shared corpus is mid-drift from a parallel session — 1412/1426 stale at session start, NOT from this change — so absolutes aren't comparable, the proof is the per-toggle A/B per the round 94/95/96 pattern):** **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD — IMPROVED** (BLL150/170/210/BLL236 **34.39→34.55 +0.17**; BLL160/230/TWHA902/ENGJ402 **39.88→39.93 +0.05**); **compare_structure exact chain — IMPROVED** (+4 and +2; EXTRA/missing HELD — the recovered panel wrappers match the human chain); **body_compare ANY — HELD**; **structural-defect clean % — HELD** (100%; BLL210's orphan flag removed is a net improvement, the orphan note was already gate-excluded as cv2-note); **literal-`[tag]` leak — HELD** (0); **tags 9557/9557 (REAL FAILURES 0) — HELD**; **speechBubble defect 0 — HELD**; **flipCard — UNAFFECTED** (CEDO102, the one inquiry-family flipCard module, BYTE-IDENTICAL on/off; the verifier's TRR114-refused run is a pre-existing sandbox quirk). **OVER-FIRE CANARIES ZERO-EFFECT on every metric** — MXDB202, OSAI501, PNR101, XGF9003 (real `[tabs]` widget), ENGJ402 (mis-tagged accordion), BLL236 — all byte-identical (they do not fire inquiry → never reach the recovery). No protected gate regressed; PRIMARY + compare_structure improved. New data flag `body_region.inquiry_tabs.recover_consumed_openers`; new env toggle `INQRECOVER_OFF`. Tools: `outputs/_probe_inqcoverage.cjs`, `outputs/_probe_tabconsume.cjs`. ## 2026-06-24 (round 97 / TEMPLATES round A) — TEMPLATE-MODE RESOLVER + Fundamentals body-class order/attrs + inquiry order normalise (Chris) (build 260616.76)

Chris asked to start executing `reference/Template_Inventory_And_Roadmap.md` → its execution doc `reference/Templates_Build_Kickoff_Brief.md`, which sequences the Inquiry/Fundamentals/Dual-Language template builds and mandates a **TEMPLATE-MODE RESOLVER first** (round A) so rounds B/C/D slot in as data, not bolt-ons. This round lands the resolver + the cheapest, cleanest body-class fixes through it, proving it is BYTE-NEUTRAL where it must be. Re-measured live (`outputs/_measure_template_modes.py`) — the corpus drifted vs the roadmap's authoring snapshot (mathJax now 3 module-level + 13 mixed; inquiry 30/24-gated).

- **TRIANGULATION (WT-mandate, per page).** **Fundamentals HPFUN101** — human `<body class="fundamentals container-fluid" language="eng" translation="reo">`; Claude (pre) `<body class="container-fluid fundamentals">` — WRONG token order + MISSING the language/translation attrs. **Inquiry CEDK101** — human `<body class="inquiry container-fluid">`; Claude (pre) `<body class="container-fluid inquiry">` — wrong order. **Dual-language PNR101** — human `<body class="container-fluid reoTranslate" language="reo" translation="eng">`; Claude (pre) had the class but DROPPED the attrs. **MathJax MXEO401** — human carries `mathJax` on only 1 of 7 pages; Claude 0 — see the deferral below.

- **ROOT CAUSE.** `SkeletonBuilder` emits `rules.body_class` verbatim from the `Style_Anchor_Registry`, which stored the bases in the WRONG order (`container-fluid fundamentals` / `container-fluid inquiry`), never emitted the `language/translation` body attrs, and is per-group/per-module (so it can't track per-page modifiers). The human convention (measured): BASE tokens (`fundamentals`/`inquiry`) PREPEND before `container-fluid`; MODIFIER tokens (`mathJax`/`reoTranslate`) APPEND after it; `fundamentals`+`reoTranslate` carry the language-toggle attrs.

- **FIX — `app/js/TemplateModeResolver.js` (new) + `data/Template_Modes.json` (new); env `TEMPLATEMODE_OFF`.** One small data-driven resolver, consulted by `SkeletonBuilder.BuildPage`, that parses the registry `body_class`, recomposes it in canonical order `[bases] + container-fluid + [unknowns] + [modifiers]`, and emits the per-mode `language/translation` attrs. `Emit_Templates.skeleton.body_open` gains a `{bodyAttrs}` slot (`<body class="{bodyClass}"{bodyAttrs}>`); wired into the node harness (`batch_convert.cjs` data list + class load), `Config.DataFiles`, and `app/index.html`. PROVABLY byte-neutral: a body class with NO `container-fluid` core (sentinels `n/a`/`—`) passes through untouched; Standard `container-fluid` and already-correct `container-fluid mathJax` recompose to themselves with empty attrs (verified by the canary A/B below). Env `TEMPLATEMODE_OFF` (or `Template_Modes.enabled:false`) reverts to the raw registry string with no reorder/attrs — byte-identical to round 96.

- **MathJax DEFERRED (measured non-derivable, recorded — NO code).** `mathJax` is NOT a 3-module mode but a PER-PAGE modifier — **75 human pages across ~16 modules** (49 hide inside modules whose representative page is plain `container-fluid`), and it has **no derivable Writers-Template signal**: a LaTeX/math-marker WT scan over all 197 modules gave **0 true positives / 3 false negatives** (the 3 pure-mathJax modules), and MXEO401's human uses `mathJax` on only 1/7 pages — so a per-group registry fire would OVER-emit. The resolver PRESERVES whatever `mathJax` the registry already emits (the MXFL302/MXFL401/MXDB301/MXFL301 canaries are byte-identical) and adds none. Real lever = a per-page math-content signal (CLAUDE.md §15). This corrects the roadmap's "half-working consistency fix" assumption.

- **MEASURED CLASS (`outputs/_measure_template_modes.py`).** Fundamentals 11–12 modules → all `fundamentals container-fluid` + `language=eng translation=reo`; inquiry CED/TWHA pages → `inquiry container-fluid`; dual-language 5 modules (3 emit output; TRR106/TRR114 are MTK-refused by design, round C) → `container-fluid reoTranslate` + `language=reo translation=eng`. Standard byte-neutrality: 833 human standard pages are exactly `container-fluid`.

**PROTECTED gates — drift-immune A/B isolation (`_ab.py TEMPLATEMODE_OFF=1 <codes>`; the corpus is mid-drift from a parallel session — 1304/1414 pages older than the newest source — so absolutes aren't comparable, the proof is the per-toggle A/B, per the round 94/95/96 pattern):** **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD — IMPROVED** on the affected sets (Fundamentals+Reo HPFUN101/102/201+SSFUN01+XFUN01+PNR101/102 **+0.33**, 15.21→15.54; inquiry-order CEDK101/102+CEDW101+CEDT208+TWHA901/902 **+0.31**, 7.88→8.19), every other gate HELD EXACTLY in both; **CANARIES ZERO-EFFECT on every metric** (ENGR101 standard, MXDB301 + MXFL301 mathJax-bearing standard, MXFL302 + MXFL401 pure mathJax, MXEO401 the flagged module, OSAI501 complex/inquiry-watchlist) — byte-identical, proving no over-fire and Standard-corpus safety. So compare_structure / body_compare / structural-defect / literal-`[tag]` leak — HELD everywhere; tags / flipCard / speechBubble verifiers untouched (no widget/tag path changed). No protected gate regressed; PRIMARY improved on the targeted modules. NOTE: a full 0-stale `ship.sh` regen is the standard backstop for a CLEAN (non-drifting) session; the drift-immune A/B + the affected-set regen (all fundamentals/inquiry-CED-TWHA/reo modules fresh-with-fix) are the authoritative proof here. New file `app/js/TemplateModeResolver.js`; new data `data/Template_Modes.json` (flag `enabled`); new env toggle `TEMPLATEMODE_OFF`. Tool: `outputs/_measure_template_modes.py`. NEXT (per the kickoff brief §5): round B Fundamentals `fundamentalsPanel` build (`FUNDPANEL_OFF`), round C Dual-Language reo/eng element pairing (`REOTRANSLATE_OFF`), round D Inquiry crumbs+panels staged (`INQUIRYTABS_OFF`) — all now slot into this resolver.

## 2026-06-23 (round 93) — PIPELINE AUDIT + HARDENING: make the round-92 process errors impossible to repeat (Chris) (build 260616.72)

**NO converter / output change — every module is byte-identical, every protected gate NUMBER is unchanged from round 92.** Chris asked for a full, careful audit of the entire fix pipeline to PROACTIVELY prevent the two process errors from round 92: (1) "reading a stale `body_compare.json` (not recomputing after each toggle regen) — invalidating the isolation"; (2) "A/B the body_compare delta on a small draft set before committing to a full regen, and confirm what actually causes a regression before 'fixing' it." Full writeup: `reference/Pipeline_Audit_And_Hardening_Round93.md`.

- **AUDIT (read every pipeline script).** The tooling is mature: `_fastloop_diff.py` (inner loop) ALWAYS re-runs the 4 gate scripts on the current corpus — it can never read a stale json — and self-guards freshness; `_regen_safe.sh`/`_stalecheck.sh`/`_batch_plan.py` already guard the regen traps (rc masking, oversized batches, the stale surprise, `--force`); `_fastloop_validate.py` proves the decomposition is exact. **The round-92 errors came from working OUTSIDE these tools** (a hand `batch_convert` + a hand `json.load("body_compare.json")`) and from ONE genuinely missing tool (no full-regen verdict). Five loose ends catalogued (severity-ranked in the report); the three HIGH ones are now fixed with NEW tools — **zero edits to the gate scripts, so no gate number can shift.**

- **(1) `_ab.py` — ATOMIC per-toggle A/B isolation (the keystone fix).** `python3 _ab.py VAR=VAL CODE…` regenerates the modules with the toggle ON (fix reverted) and OFF (default), RE-RUNS all 4 decomposable gates SCOPED both times, prints exactly which metric the toggle moves, then restores the live full cs/bc jsons and leaves the modules in the default state. It re-runs the gates each pass → **can never read a stale json**; a ZERO-effect result tells you the toggle is NOT the cause → **confirm before you "fix"**. VERIFIED on the exact round-92 case: `_ab.py INSTRDOM_OFF=1 ENGC201 ENGR101 MXDB301` → **ZERO effect on every metric** (proving INSTRDOM was NOT the over-capture's cause — the answer I got wrong by hand, which had cost the wasted boundary-tighten + 2nd full regen). This ONE command prevents BOTH round-92 errors.

- **(2) `_gatecheck.py` — one-command FULL-REGEN verdict.** `_fastloop_diff.py` correctly REFUSES after a full regen (every module is newer than its baseline), so a full-regen ship had no automated verdict and round-92 hand-diffed the json (where the stale-read risk lives). `_gatecheck.py` asserts 0-stale, re-runs the 4 decomposable gates FULL, and diffs vs the committed drift-proof `gate_baseline.json`, printing the same HELD/IMPROVED/REGRESSED table. Splittable for the 45s wall (`_gatecheck.py skeleton defect` then `cs bc`). VERIFIED: reproduced the round-92 numbers exactly (skeleton 539/70, cs 5902/142/252, body 184, leak 253) and flagged a live **−0.03 defect drift from a parallel session** (not any code change here). Wired into `ship.sh` (replaces the bare gate-suite print with the verdict + the 3 verifier gates).

- **(3) `_gate_fresh.py` — STALE/FRAGMENT backstop.** Filesystem-only (no gate-script edit): a persisted gate json is STALE if any Claude html is newer than it (a regen happened after the gate ran), FRAGMENT if it holds far fewer rows than the corpus (a scoped `codes` run). VERIFIED: flags a 5/1358-row fragment and an old-mtime full file; passes the live full jsons. Call it before EVER hand-reading; the recompute tools make hand-reading unnecessary.

- **WORKFLOW + DOCS.** `ship.sh` now runs `_gatecheck.py` for the verdict. CLAUDE.md §5 (the disciplined loop) now mandates: when a gate regresses, PROVE the cause with `_ab.py` before any "fix"; §9 adds the **"NEVER hand-read a gate json — use `_ab.py`/`_fastloop_diff.py`/`_gatecheck.py` (they recompute); if you must, run `_gate_fresh.py` first"** rule + the session-start re-baseline note; §13 lists the three new tools.

**PROTECTED gates — UNCHANGED BY CONSTRUCTION (no `app/js`/`data` output logic touched; the 3 tools are additive, the 7 existing pipeline scripts were not edited — mtimes pre-session).** `_gatecheck.py` on the live corpus reproduced the round-92 baseline exactly except a parallel session's −0.03 defect-clean drift (95.10→95.07, NOT from this round; the committed `gate_baseline.json` round-92 numbers stand, to be re-baselined at the next gate-affecting ship per the §9 rule). ## 2026-06-23 (round 90) — PIPELINE / TOOLING: fast-loop default + freshness guard + timeout-safe regen + widget-gate fix (Chris) (build 260616.69)

**NO converter / output change — every module is byte-identical, every protected gate NUMBER is unchanged.** This round answers Chris's two asks: (a) the per-round "speechBubble"/"flipCard" ceremony felt like bloat — assess whether it's worth keeping; (b) recurring `batch_convert` timeouts keep being forgotten conversation-to-conversation — build safeguards. Full written assessment: `reference/Pipeline_Bloat_And_Timeout_Assessment.md`.

- **MEASURED the "bloat" (numbers, not vibes).** The widget verifiers are cheap: flipCard **3.4s**, speechBubble **3.4s**, vs the PRIMARY skeleton gate **24s** and the full 198-module regen **~12 min / 16+ calls**. So the conspicuous changelog line is ~0.4% of a round — culling it saves almost nothing. The REAL sink is the reflexive **full-corpus regen every round** when a fix touches a handful of modules; the fast-loop that avoids it already existed (rounds 85-88) but was never made the default, partly because its baseline had no freshness check so a careful session rightly distrusted it.

- **speechBubble verifier was VACUOUS as run; flipCard verdict was misleading — FIXED, not culled (Chris chose "fix, don't cull").** The per-round `speechBubble defect 0 — HELD` was run (when at all) on the flipCard module set `CEDO102 MXDB302 TRR114 XMES201`, which builds **ZERO** bubbles — a pass that verified nothing, and it was never even in `run_all_gates.sh`. Pointed at a real set (`OSAI501 OSAI401 OSAH501 ENGR101 OSGM501`) it builds ~39 bubbles, defect 0 — so it is now WIRED INTO `run_all_gates.sh` on that set. The flipCard verifier printed `RESULT: real defects present ✗` every single run (its `defect 14` is a tracked baseline, not a target of 0) — the verdict now keys on the actual protected criterion **divergence 0** (counts 37/13/10/14 unchanged).

- **FAST-LOOP is now the DEFAULT (§5 step 4 / §5b / §10).** Step 4 was rewritten: default to `./iterate.sh <affected CODES>` (scoped regen + exact decomposition diff, ~1 min); a per-round full-corpus regen is NOT required — it's the ship-checkpoint backstop (`./ship.sh`), once per BATCH. Reserve full regen for changes whose affected set can't be bounded.

- **FRESHNESS GUARD — the safeguard that makes the fast-loop trustworthy (`_fastloop_diff.py`).** It now refuses (exit 2) to print deltas when (a) an affected module wasn't regenerated since your last source edit, or (b) the baseline is stale (an UNAFFECTED module was regenerated after the snapshot) — the exact silent-wrong-delta trap behind round 89 running on a round-85 baseline. Override `--allow-stale-baseline`. (Confirmed firing: 240 unaffected modules newer than the on-disk baseline → correctly refused.)

- **TIMEOUT-SAFE REGEN (the recurring rc-124 / stale-surprise pain, now guarded in tooling not memory).** `_batch_plan.py` hole fixed — AGH/ANZH/ENGI/HES/PHE moved to the HEAVY tier and LIGHT capped 26→22 (the round-88 26-mix timeouts), plus an optional `reference/tests/_module_weights.json` override (kept OUT of `data/` — a `data/*.json` is scanned by the staleness checks and would falsely stale the whole corpus) so a newly-slow module is appended without code edits; it now emits self-checking `./_regen_safe.sh` lines. New `_regen_safe.sh` runs ONE batch with `timeout 40`, captures node's TRUE rc (no pipe masking), and after a clean run NAMES any module that didn't produce fresh HTML (partial-timeout catch). New `_stalecheck.sh` NAMES the stale module dirs (not just a count → no more "282 stale surprise") + prints the exact regen command; `ship.sh` now calls it. CLAUDE.md §10 corrected the dangerous "2 parallel batch_convert safe" line (it silently drops the 2nd here).

- **PROTECTED gates — VERIFIED on a fresh 0-stale FULL regen (round 90 also LANDED the baseline).** No `app/js` converter logic or `data/*.json` shape changed (Config.js AppVersion is UI-only, never stamped in output, excluded from staleness), so output is unchanged by construction — and now CONFIRMED empirically: regenerated all **217 stale dirs → `_stalecheck.sh` = 0 stale** (the new `_regen_safe.sh` guard caught + auto-split **3 over-heavy batches** — HIS/MX, XDLS, BLL/CED — that silently time-out + leave stale pages under the old hand-batched recipe), then ran the FULL gate suite: every protected gate matches the round-89 committed baseline **EXACTLY** — skeleton **47.8% / ≥50% 523 / ≥75% 65**; compare_structure **5892 / 142 / 259**; body_compare **181**; defect **1290 / 95.0% / leak 254 / 68**; tags **9557/9557**; flipCard **divergence 0** (37/13/10/14); speechBubble **defect 0** (39 builds — now a REAL check wired into `run_all_gates.sh`, not the old vacuous 0). Fast-loop **baseline refreshed** (`outputs/_fastloop_baseline/`) and `_fastloop_diff.py`'s freshness guard now **PASSES** (it was correctly REFUSING the round-85 baseline before this) — verified with a live `OSAI501` diff: all gates HELD, delta 0. `gate_baseline.json` round-89 numbers stand. ## 2026-06-23 (round 87) — ENGI302-00: media-TIMESTAMP CS note ("(to 1:00)") + acks UNKNOWN-TYPE ❗ flag consistency (Chris) (build 260616.66)

Chris flagged two things on the ENGI302 overview (two three-pane screenshots): (1) the red `(to 1:00)` annotation after the intro-video URL "needs to be captured as an instruction to CS" — it was being silently dropped; (2) the Acknowledgements block flags `[VIDEO TITLE REQUIRED]`/`[CHANNEL REQUIRED]` video lines with a ❗ but leaves `Jpg:` / `Text:` lines (which "don't seem formatted correctly… due to not enough information") UN-flagged — "there needs to be the same exclamation mark present as there is on the other copyright lines." Both triangulated WT→human→Claude, measured corpus-wide BEFORE coding, fixed behind a data flag + env toggle each, and proven gate-safe on a full 0-stale regen + an A/B isolation on the affected modules.

- **(1) MEDIA-TIMESTAMP CS NOTE (data `elements.media_timestamp_note`; env `TIMESTAMPNOTE_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — WT line 116 `https://…uOmAmZiV8TI🔴[RED TEXT]  (to 1:00) [/RED TEXT]🔴`; the human strips the note (editorial); Claude rendered the URL `<p><a>` and DROPPED `(to 1:00)`. ROOT CAUSE — `(to 1:00)` is a wholly-red span with no tag, no instruction cue, only 2 free words and no bracket, so `TagNormaliser.ResolveSpan` falls to the final `else → "noise"` and `ContentConverter` (line 458, `!primary` + `class!=="instruction"`) emits NOTHING. MEASURED (`outputs/_measure_round87.py`) — a blanket "short red parenthetical → note" is UNSAFE (the 136-strong bucket is heterogeneous: flipCard `(front)`/`(Back)`, `(trigger engagement)` widget markers, `(Gold)`/`(middle image)` labels). The clean, coherent class is a parenthetical that is WHOLLY a clock timestamp/range: **41 occ / 11 modules** (`(to 1:00)` ENGI302, `(0:10-1:48)` ENGI303, `(1:45-2:27)` ENGR101, `(2:26-4:16)` ENGS401, …), ZERO false positives; the longer `… only`/`clip …` forms (48) are already retained as ≥3-word instructions. FIX — `TagNormaliser.#isMediaTimestampNote(free)` (lazy data regex) adds one OR-term to the instruction branch, so a wholly-timestamp parenthetical is classed `instruction` and retained via the round-43/57 path as `<p class="cv2-note">CS: (to 1:00)</p>` right after the media element. ## 2026-06-22 (round 85) — NOTE-RESIDUE empty bullet drop — the ALL-EMPTY / consecutive follow-up to round 84 (Chris, MXDI202-00 / BLL126-01) (build 260616.64)

Chris re-flagged a stray bullet in MXDI202-00 — the same family as AGH1004's round-84 empty bullet, but the variant round 84 deliberately can't reach. Also surfaces a MIRROR sub-class (preceded-by-note) and DEFERS it with the measurement, because one module ships deliberate blanks there.

- **ROOT CAUSE (why round 84's `drop_empty_items` missed it).** Round 84 drops a stray empty `<li>` only from a MIXED list (≥1 real item) and KEEPS an ALL-empty list (the human ships deliberate blank-worksheet scaffolds). MXDI202's note bullet is a STANDALONE `• [RED] Insert brief introductory text. [/RED]` — its OWN single-item list, which goes all-empty once the instruction is lifted to the `CS:` note, so the "keep all-empty" guard preserved it as `<ul><li></li></ul>`. The "• " arrives as its own black item just before the instruction item, so the residue and the lifted note end up adjacent emissions.

- **MEASURED (BEFORE coding; `outputs/_measure_loneempty.py`).** Splitting ALL-empty lists LONE (1 `<li>`) vs MULTI (≥2): Claude **139 lone all-empty / 63 immediately FOLLOWED by a `cv2-note`** (the note-residue signature, MXDI202 among them) across **25 modules**; the human ships **0** of those — but ships **109 lone blanks** (ARFUN/ENFUN/FUN worksheets) + **1937 multi-item scaffolds**, so "drop ANY lone empty" is UNSAFE — the discriminator is **note-adjacency**, not loneness. (PES1004 sits in BOTH Claude's residue set and the human's deliberate-blank set — the fix must be surgical.)

- **THE FIX — note-residue strip (data `body_region.list_nesting.drop_note_residue_bullet`; env `NOTEBULLET_OFF`).** `ContentConverter.#dropNoteResidueBullets`, a post-pass on the assembled body (parity with round 80 `#stripMediaResidue`), removes a RUN of one-or-more consecutive single-item empty `<ul><li></li></ul>` immediately FOLLOWED by a `cv2-note` paragraph — the residue of bulleted instructions whose text was lifted to that note. It runs OUTERMOST (after the relevel/promote/activity/alert passes), because an intervening element between the bullet and its note can be removed by those passes, so the adjacency only fully forms AFTER them (ENGR301-03 — diagnosed with a temporary `DBG_NOTEBULLET` trace). A populated list, a multi-blank worksheet scaffold (≥2 `<li>`), and a deliberate lone blank NOT followed by a note never match; when nothing matches the body is byte-identical.

Note-FOLLOWED residue corpus-wide **63 → 0**. Scope spot-check: 6 non-affected modules (AGH1004/OSBY201/ENGC102/CEDO102/MXDB302/TRR114) regen byte-IDENTICAL (the post-pass is a no-op off the signature).

**PROTECTED gates (FAST-LOOP: scoped regen of the 25 affected modules + the exact `_fastloop_diff.py` decomposition diff vs the round-84 baseline, then a FULL gate-suite run that reproduced the differ's numbers to the digit; baseline refreshed to the shipped state):** **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD — IMPROVED** (mean **47.52 → 47.56%**; pages ≥50% **496 → 497, +1**; pages ≥75% **59 → 61, +2**); compare_structure **exact 5719 / EXTRA 135 / missing 246 — HELD EXACTLY**; **body_compare ANY 172 — HELD** (the dropped empties were Claude-only residue — no body lost); structural-clean **1245/1305 = 95.4% — HELD**, literal-`[tag]` leak **207 occ / 60 pages — HELD**; JS regression **0 / 9557 (100%) — HELD**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0 — HELD** (the 4 verifier modules byte-identical). No protected gate regressed; the PRIMARY improved. A/B reversal: `NOTEBULLET_OFF` restores the residue bullets.

## 2026-06-22 (round 84) — SPLIT/ORPHANED HOVER-DEFINITION bracket weave + empty-bullet drop (Chris, AGH1004-00/-01/-02) (build 260616.63)

Chris flagged (AGH1004 three-pane screenshots) three things Claude should have processed: (1) a `[hover definition]` whose def **broke the paragraph** ("…specific areas or **regions** [" then stopped) and the bracket leaked; (2) a `[hover definition:` that broke the paragraph AND rendered its def as a stray **"CS:" note** ("topographies" / "CS: the shape and features…"); (3) an **empty bullet** left in the module-intro list after a "note to CS" bullet's instruction was lifted out. He asked — per the in-screenshot note — that the fix be GENERAL so ANY tag hitting the same error renders correctly. All three root-caused at the real item-tokenisation level, measured corpus-wide BEFORE coding, fixed behind data flags + env toggles; every protected gate held-or-improved on a full 0-stale regen, A/B-isolated on the 38 affected modules over the identical corpus.

- **ROOT CAUSE (why round 82's `#weaveHoverDefinition` missed them).** Round 82 weaves a hover/rollover/mouseover DEFINITION marker onto the preceding word as `<span class="infoTrigger" info="DEF">anchor</span>`, but only when the marker's own text both starts with `[` AND carries the def. The `_dump_infotrigger` probe (real DocxExtractor→PageSplitter→TagNormaliser) showed AGH1004's two shapes resolve to `primary=info trigger` yet defeat that: **(A1)** the marker's opening `[` was left in the preceding BLACK run, so the item text begins `hover definition] DEF` (NO leading `[`) → `head_pattern` (`^\[`) fails; **(A2)** the marker is an UNCLOSED `[hover definition:` (no `]`, empty `blackAfter`) — or a closed-but-empty `[hover definition]` — and the def is the FOLLOWING item (`tag/instruction`: `DEF…]` + the paragraph continuation in ITS `blackAfter`); round 82's `mk` regex needs a `]`+inline-def so it bailed, the paragraph broke and the red def item became a `CS:` note.

- **MEASURED (the discriminators, BEFORE coding).** `outputs/_measure_hoverweavegap.cjs` over the finalized corpus: **A1 orphan-lead-bracket 8 occ / 6 mods**; **A2 unclosed/empty with def in the NEXT RED span 101 occ / 28 mods** (FIXABLE); **A2b def-in-BLACK 41 occ / 10 mods** (no red def item — LEFT UNTOUCHED, AGH1007 "plant materia]"). Key engine fact: DocxExtractor MERGES the writer's fragmented red runs into ONE item, so every A2 def is a single clean item (AGH1009's char-split "D/isease…" → one `how acidic or alkaline a substance is]`). `outputs/_measure_emptybullet.py`: Claude **19 stray empty `<li>` across 16 MIXED lists / 6 mods**; the human ships **0** in those paired pages but DOES ship **2046 ALL-empty worksheet lists** (MXFUN03/PES1004/MXDB301 blank scaffolds) — so the discriminator is "drop a stray empty `<li>` ONLY when the list also has a real item; keep an all-empty list".

- **THE FIX — hover (data `elements.hover_definition_inline.split_bracket {lead_orphan, unclosed_next_item}`; env `HOVERSPLIT_OFF`, independent of `HOVERDEF_OFF`).** `InteractiveScanner.#weaveHoverDefinition`: **(A1)** when the resolved marker lacks a leading `[` but starts with a head keyword and contains `]`, restore the `[` before the head test, and strip a trailing orphan `[` off the host (so "regions [" never leaks). **(A2)** when the marker yields no self-def and its `blackAfter` is empty, pull the def from the FOLLOWING non-interactive instruction/noise/black item (trim a stray late `]`), re-join its `blackAfter` continuation, and consume it (removing the spurious `CS:` note). Reuses round 75's `U+E000` sentinel + `ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup`, so bold/plain anchors both build the span. Round 82's own cases are untouched (the def-in-own-text path runs first); the def-in-BLACK form and a real widget tag in the next slot are never consumed.

- **THE FIX — empty bullet (data `body_region.list_nesting.drop_empty_items`; env `EMPTYBULLET_OFF`).** `ContentConverter.#renderBlackText`/`renderList`: when a list has ≥1 non-empty item, drop the empty ones (the "• "-only artifact); a list whose items are ALL empty is left intact (the deliberate blank-worksheet scaffold). The ol-override is recomputed on the kept set; when nothing is dropped the result is byte-identical to before.

- **RESULT (AGH1004).** -01 `…specific areas or <span class="infoTrigger" info="a distinct and defined geographic area…">regions</span> New Zealand's regional areas…` (one `<p>`, no orphan `[`); -02 `…beautiful <span class="infoTrigger" info="the shape and features…">topographies</span> on planet Earth…` (one `<p>`, the `CS:` note gone — matches human -06); -00 the intro `<ul>` ends at "…use of it today." with NO empty `<li>`, the CS video note still retained after the list. infoTrigger spans corpus-wide **230 → 452**.

**PROTECTED gates (full fresh corpus regen, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1305 pages / 1042 paired; A/B-ISOLATED on the 38 affected modules over the IDENTICAL corpus — regen `HOVERSPLIT_OFF=1 EMPTYBULLET_OFF=1` → gate → ON → gate, the other ~1145 pages constant. NOTE the on-disk corpus has grown to 1305/1042 (extra finalized dirs incl. the affected non-compare_set AGH/PHE/SSFUN/ARFUN modules), so absolutes are NOT comparable to the round-83 snapshot (1168/942) — the proof is A/B on the current corpus):** **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD — IMPROVED** (pages ≥50% **495 → 496, +1**; pages ≥75% **58 → 59, +1**; mean 47.5% / median 49.1% held); compare_structure **exact 5717 → 5719 (+2 — IMPROVED)** / EXTRA **135 — HELD** / missing **246 — HELD**; **body_compare ANY 172 — HELD EXACTLY** (over-capture 38 / runaway 5 / empty 132 — no body lost, the consumed CS-note def + dropped empty `<li>` were Claude-only); structural-clean **1245/1305 = 95.4% — HELD**, literal-`[tag]` leak **207 — HELD** (the audit's regex never counted `[hover]`; the woven spans only REMOVE free-body bracket leaks, the residual `[hover` literals are pre-existing TABLE-CELL/widget-placeholder paths, untouched); JS regression **0 / 9557 (100%) — HELD**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0 — HELD**; speechBubble **defect 0 — HELD**. No protected gate regressed; the PRIMARY and compare_structure improved. A/B-VERIFIED: both toggles OFF restores AGH1004-01's broken "regions [" + -02's split paragraph & `CS: the shape…` note + -00's empty `<li>` byte-for-byte. New data flags `elements.hover_definition_inline.split_bracket`, `body_region.list_nesting.drop_empty_items`; new env toggles `HOVERSPLIT_OFF`, `EMPTYBULLET_OFF`. ## 2026-06-22 (round 83) — ACTIVITY NUMBERING: number-from-tail (SPLIT_INLINE) + bare re-emphasis MERGE (Chris, ENGC101-02) (build 260616.62)

Chris flagged (ENGC101-02 three-pane screenshot) that a single interactive activity was SPLIT into two boxes: the writer opened `[Activity 2A]`, then typed a SECOND bare `[Activity]` inside it to re-mark where the interactive sits, and the converter mistook that for a new activity. He asked for a corpus-wide deep dive: does this scenario recur, and does the human interpret it consistently? It does, and it does — and the deep dive surfaced a larger cousin (the activity number typed OUTSIDE the bracket). Both fixed behind data flags + env toggles; every protected gate held-or-improved on a full 0-stale regen, A/B vs both toggles OFF.

- **THE DISCRIMINATOR (measured, the headline).** The human emits a NUMBERLESS `<div class="activity">` only **0.65%** of the time (43 / 6567) vs Claude **24%** (631 / 2628) — the human numbers EVERY activity box. `outputs/_measure_nested_bare_activity.py` / `_measure_nested_bare_activity2.py` classify the 472 bare `[Activity]` tags corpus-wide: **SPLIT_INLINE 180** (number outside the bracket — "[Activity] 3A"), STANDALONE 216, SPLIT_NEXT 53, **NESTED_PROSE 12 / 9 modules** (the ENGC101 re-emphasis class — in every one the human has ZERO numberless boxes), SECTION_SEP 6, NESTED_EMPTY 5.

- **(a) NUMBER-FROM-TAIL (data `activity_wrapper.number_from_tail`; env `ACTNUMTAIL_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — ANZH101 WT `🔴[Activity] 1A 🔴`, `[Activity] 1B`, `[Activity] 1C` (the id is in the RED span AFTER the bracket, so `parse.numbers` was empty → NUMBERLESS box); human `number="1A"`/`"1B"`/`"1C"`. MEASURED 180 such openers (digit+letter 174, bare-digit-then-title 6, ZERO digit+lowercase-prose). FIX — `TagNormaliser.Parse` lifts a LEADING digit+letter id token ("1a"/"10b") from the span's free text into `parse.numbers` when an `[Activity]` CONTAINER_OPEN tag carries no bracket number, so every consumer (`#activityOpen` id, `InteractiveScanner` activityId, the adjacent-merge carry) sees it. Digit+LETTER only — the 6 bare-digit cases are skipped so prose like "5 minutes" can NEVER be read as a number. RESULT — ANZH101 numberless 7→1 (the 6 SPLIT_INLINE boxes now `number="1A".."3B"` matching the human). **Skeleton-NEUTRAL** (A/B +0.0000pp on all 8 affected modules): the numbered activity line still differs from the human on the orthogonal `.interactive`/`.alertPadding` CLASS modifier (`div.activity[number=1A]` vs human `div.activity.interactive[number=1A]`), so the corrected number doesn't yet complete a skeleton match — but the OUTPUT now matches the human's numbering convention. `ACTNUMTAIL_OFF` reverts to the numberless box.

- **(b) BARE RE-EMPHASIS MERGE (data `activity_wrapper.bare_reemphasis_merge`; env `REEMPH_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — ENGC101-02 WT: `[Activity 2A]` → `[H3] Identifying adjectives` → CS image-instruction + Adult/Child speech → `[Image]` → `[Activity] Which words does the child use…? Tick the describing words:` → the tick-list + `[Button] Check/Reset`. Human: ONE `<div class="activity interactive alertPadding" number="2A">` with the bare `[Activity]`'s text as a `<p>` lead-in, then the speechBubble + multiChoiceQuiz. Claude round-82: `number="2A"` (image) + a SECOND **numberless** `<div class="activity">` (the tick-list) — 2A SPLIT in two. DISCRIMINATOR (merge vs renumber, measured): the human MERGES only when the open numbered activity's OPENER had an EMPTY tail (ENGC101 `[Activity 2A]`, title from a separate `[H3]`); when the opener carried its own title (`[Activity 5C] Extra for Experts` / `[Activity 5E] Pick a task` / `[Activity 1D] Body rhythm`) the bare activity is a NEW sibling the human RENUMBERS (Dropbox/Reflection/Pick-a-task) — LEFT UNTOUCHED. FIX — a guard in `ContentConverter.ConvertPage` (before `autoClose`, which would otherwise close the open activity on the new `[activity]` tag): a TRULY-bare `[Activity]` (`parse.free` empty — the red span is exactly "[Activity]", lead carried as BLACK text) arriving while the TOP activity is open, NUMBERED (`top.id`), content-bearing, and had an EMPTY opener tail (`!titledOpener`), and whose lead is not an excluded standalone type (dropbox/reflection/journal/upload), flows its lead text into the open box and suppresses the new box. The numbered-open + empty-opener + free-empty gates keep the RENUMBER chains (CEDO102 Dropbox, ENGI405 Pick-a-task, ENGI203 bare-`[Activity]` chains the human numbers 4A/4B/…, PHE1005 `[activity] short answer box` descriptive-label openers) UNCHANGED. ## 2026-06-22 (round 82) — HOVER/ROLLOVER DEFINITION weave + supervisor-note heading de-pollution (Chris, ENGC101-01/-02) (build 260616.61)

Chris flagged (ENGC101 three-pane screenshot) two things Claude should have processed correctly: (1) a HOVER TEXT that split the paragraph it was part of and dropped its definition, and (2) the FIRST heading "Conversations" rendering one level too deep. Both root-caused, measured corpus-wide BEFORE coding, fixed behind data flags + env toggles; every protected gate held-or-improved on a full 0-stale regen, A/B vs both toggles OFF.

- **(1) HOVER/ROLLOVER DEFINITION weave (data `elements.hover_definition_inline`; env `HOVERDEF_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — ENGC101-02 WT L209 `Using **adjectives** 🔴[hover text] Describing words.🔴can make a conversation exciting…`; human L49 `Using <span class="infoTrigger" info="Describing words.">adjectives</span> can make…` (ONE `<p>`); Claude split it into `…Using <b>adjectives</b>` + `<p>can make…</p>` and DROPPED the def. ENGC101-01 L126 `gestures 🔴[hover: Moving part of the body…]🔴 and expressions` is the same class (human weaves `<span infoTrigger>gestures</span>`, Claude broke at "gestures"). ROOT CAUSE — `[hover text]` / `[hover: DEF]` resolve to plain `[body]` (NOT infoTrigger), so they never reached round 75's standalone weave; they were emitted as a fresh `[body]` paragraph marker. These are TWO shapes round 75 (keyed on the word "trigger") cannot reach: the COLON form `[hover: DEF]` / `[hover on X: DEF]` / `[hover definition: DEF]` (def inside the bracket after the first colon) and the MARKER-THEN-DEF form `[hover text] DEF` (def follows the `]` inside the same red span). MEASURED corpus-wide (`outputs/_measure_hovertext.cjs`, runs the real TagNormaliser over the finalized `*_parsed.txt`): of 2,270 hover/rollover/mouseover/trigger markers — colon-self-closed **644 / 74 mods**, marker-then-def **187 / 66 mods** — dominated by `[Hover: DEF]` (**417**); the instruction/other-widget forms (`trigger engagement` 236, `shape hover` 24, `hover audio player` 28, quiz/dev notes) correctly stay excluded. FIX — a new `InteractiveScanner.#weaveHoverDefinition` runs BEFORE the INTERACTIVE-skip (the body-resolving shape never reaches the standalone path), detects a def-carrying hover/rollover/mouseover marker (data `head_pattern`), and weaves it onto the nearest preceding word as `<span class="infoTrigger" info="DEF">anchor</span>` using round 75's `U+E000` sentinel + `ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup` (bold `**adjectives**` and plain `gestures` both build the span). A colon-def INSIDE the bracket is recovered BEFORE any text after the `]`, so a trailing `]. ` (a sentence period the writer left in the red span) is sentence TAIL, not a 1-char def (fixed free-body `info="."` 20→7; the residual 7 are the pre-existing SPLIT-bracket class — §15, deferred). SCOPE/SAFETY: a `trigger` form is left to round 75 (`skip_if_tag_keyword`); a marker resolving to a non-infoTrigger widget (shapeHover, hover audio player) is skipped; a consumed/widget-internal marker is untouched; a marker with no recoverable def is left as-is (never a leaked literal). RESULT — infoTrigger spans **57 → 230 across 120 modules** (closing the human-803 gap); ENGC101 page 1 "gestures" + page 2 "adjectives" now byte-match the human; CEDO202's free-body defs (Autumn/characterise/traits/Aotearoa/composer…) match the human exactly. `HOVERDEF_OFF` reverts to the round-81 split/drop behaviour.
- **(2) SUPERVISOR-NOTE HEADING DE-POLLUTION (data `body_region.heading_relevel.supervisor_skip_classes`; env `SUPHEAD_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — ENGC101-02 WT L289/L305 `[Supervisor note] Listen attentively…`; human renders a `<div class="row supervisor">…<div class="…super-content-button">…<p>…</p>` callout with NO heading label; Claude emits the `supervisor note` template's fixed `<h3>Supervisor note</h3>` inside that box. ROOT CAUSE — `super-content-button` was NOT in the heading re-leveller's skip set, so those two `<h3>Supervisor note</h3>` labels sat in the page's free-body level POOL and PINNED the rank base at h3 — so the page's real writer `[H3]` section headings (digit + body_shift = h4) could not normalise back DOWN to h3 ("Conversations"/"Speaking clearly"/"Listening"/"Practise…" stuck at h4 vs the human's h3). The re-leveller is a rank map (distinct free-body levels → base, base+1…); the supervisor label is a fixed-level callout, not a section heading, so it must not pollute the pool. FIX — `super-content-button` is added to the re-level skip (like a widget subtree) so its heading leaves BOTH the pool and the rewrite; its own fixed `<h3>` is unchanged. RESULT — ENGC101-02 "Conversations" (the flagged first heading) + "Speaking clearly"/"Listening"/"Practise being a good listener" now render `<h3>` matching the human. `SUPHEAD_OFF` reverts to including the supervisor label in the pool. NOTE the in-activity headings ("Identifying adjectives"/"Talking about pictures"/"Howard learns to listen") remain `<h4>` vs the human's `<h3>` — those are an activity-LEAD-heading-level sub-issue (a heading emitted at digit+shift inside a skipped activity subtree), a distinct measured follow-up.

**PROTECTED gates (full fresh corpus regen, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1150 pages; A/B vs `HOVERDEF_OFF=1 SUPHEAD_OFF=1` = the round-81 baseline, which reproduced the round-81 changelog numbers EXACTLY — skeleton 47.8% / compare_structure 4900/116/216 / body 152 / clean 1102 / leak 150 / tags 9557 / flipCard 37·0 / speechBubble 0):** **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD 47.8 → 47.9% — IMPROVED** (pages ≥50% **448 → 452, +4**; median 49.3 → 49.5%; the woven spans + the un-split paragraphs + the corrected h3 section headings are scaffold-visible wins); compare_structure **exact 4900 → 4916 (+16 — IMPROVED)** / EXTRA **116 — HELD** / missing 216 → 217 (+1 — a second-order text-match shift on a MEASUREMENT-MANDATE-demoted sub-bucket from joining the hover paragraphs; net strongly positive per the round-50 NET-POSITIVE rule); **body_compare ANY 152 — HELD EXACTLY** (over-capture 32 / runaway 5 / empty 118 — no body lost); structural-clean **1102/1150 = 95.8% — HELD**, literal-`[tag]` leak **150 — HELD** (the audit's `LITERAL_TAG` regex does not count `[hover]`, but a per-module A/B confirmed the weave only REDUCES `[hover…]` leaks — CEDO202 8 → 1 — and never adds one; XGF9001's bare-`[hover]` no-def leaks are pre-existing and untouched); JS regression **0 / 9557 (100%) — HELD**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0 — HELD**; speechBubble **defect 0 — HELD**. No protected gate regressed; the PRIMARY improved. A/B-VERIFIED: both toggles OFF restores ENGC101's split paragraph + dropped def + `<h4>Conversations` byte-for-byte. New data flags `elements.hover_definition_inline`, `body_region.heading_relevel.supervisor_skip_classes`; new env toggles `HOVERDEF_OFF`, `SUPHEAD_OFF`. Overview menu archetypes: **tabs 152 / two_col 114 / simplified 10 / none 7**. two_col splits into TWO families that correlate banner + col-class + curriculum level: the **BLL banner family** (`banner_h4_span:true` — banner + `col-md-6 col-12 paddingR` + curriculum h5+span FIXED; renders correctly today) and the **ENG offset family** (`banner_h4_span:false` — NO banner + `col-md-6 offset-md-0 col-12` + curriculum RE-LEVELLED by subject×phase + span). Discriminators measured: bilingual `reo|english` headings reduce to English in the two_col (the 58/276 pipe-keepers are tabs maths strands); italics are stripped (12/276 keep); the banner is BLL-only (39/55 BLL vs ~0 elsewhere); curriculum headings carry `<span>` (697 vs 257), LI/SC are plain (313 vs 91). **GATE-VISIBILITY finding (the key to a safe fix): `#module-menu-content` lives in `#header`, so compare_structure + body_compare (both `#body`-scoped) are INERT to it; only the PRIMARY skeleton sees the menu — and it strips TEXT, so bilingual/colon/wording changes are gate-invisible and only node shape (cols, banner, levels, `<span>`/`<i>`) moves it.** Tools: `outputs/_measure_modulemenu.py`, `_measure_curriculum_level.py`, `_measure_menu_shell.py`, `_probe_menu.cjs`, `_gen_menu_spec.py`.

Three consecutive such headings → `#dropEmptyHeadings` nukes ALL THREE → the left column empties. BLL escapes because its writers put the prose in a SEPARATE paragraph.

- **THE FIX (data `Emit_Templates.menu.two_col_li.eng_family` + `shells.two_col_offset`; env `MENUCURRIC_OFF`).** For the OFFSET family — `convention.banner_h4_span === false` AND subject ∈ `[ENGC, ENGI, ENGJ, ENGS, MXDB, SSOG, MXFUN]` (the families MEASURED to use the bare offset shell with the simple Understand/Know/Do curriculum) — `#buildMenu` now: (1) **splits** a curriculum `**Label:** prose` into `<h{level}><span>Label</span></h{level}>` (colon dropped) + the prose as a following `<p>` (separate-prose writers already render — both unify); (2) routes curriculum-LEFT / everything-else-RIGHT (the corpus majority + BLL convention — LI sits right with WILF in 100/118; ENGC102's LI-left is editorial balance, not derivable); (3) re-levels the curriculum heading by subject×phase (`curriculum_level_by_group`, measured; e.g. ENGC|1-3→h3, ENGC|4-6→h4, ENGS→h3, senior→h4); (4) reduces a piped `reo|english` LI/SC heading to the English half; (5) emits the `two_col_offset` shell (no banner, `col-md-6 offset-md-0 col-12`) via SkeletonBuilder; (6) strips `<i>/<em>` from the panes; (7) skips the round-46 named-heading promotion so WALT/I-can stay `<p>` lead-ins. The BLL banner family is byte-identical. EXCLUDED for now (sized follow-ups, different shell): MXFL/MXEX/ARFUN/XWHA (`div.item` carousel wrapper + plain col), ENGR/XFUN (offset+padding), CEDO/CEDT/EXPFUN/ENGFUN/XGF (paddingR), ANZH (mixed). ## 2026-06-22 (round 80) — ENGC102 OVERVIEW: lone-title Māori guard · overview dup-heading de-dup · video-title/paren leak (Chris, ENGC102-00) (build 260616.59)

Chris flagged three errors on ENGC102's overview (screenshots): (1) the title bar shipped `<h1>Communication</h1>` (the front-matter Course) with the real English title "Keeping it real" pushed into the Te Reo slot; (2) a DUPLICATE `<h3>Keeping it real</h3>` leaked into the body; (3) a junk box "Nonfiction Text Features )" after the video. Asked to investigate the WT → human → Claude thoroughly and study the sibling modules. Root-caused all three, measured each class corpus-wide BEFORE coding, fixed behind data flags + env toggles; every protected gate held-or-improved (PRIMARY skeleton +4 pages), A/B-proven on a full 0-stale regen.

- **(1) LONE-TITLE MĀORI GUARD (data `header.title_split.lone_title_maori_guard`; env `LONETITLE_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — ENGC102 WT L9 `[TITLE BAR] *KEEPING IT REAL*`; docx front-matter `Course: Communication`; "Kia mau ki te pono" (the human's Te Reo `<h1>`) appears NOWHERE in the WT (`grep` confirmed — the human translator added it, non-derivable). Human `<h1>Keeping it real</h1>` + `<h1>Kia mau ki te pono</h1>`; Claude round-79 `<h1>Communication</h1>` (Course) + `<h1>Keeping it real</h1>` (English shoved to Te Reo). ROOT CAUSE — PageAssembler's Course-backup (motivated by OSAI301 "Kirirarautanga matihiko AI") ASSUMES any single `[TITLE BAR]` title differing from the Course is the Te Reo name, so it promotes the lone title → Te Reo and uses the Course as English. That misfires when the lone title is the ENGLISH module title (ENGS302 even put the *Māori* Course "Te Ara Hou" in the English slot). FIX — promote ONLY when the lone title is actually Te Reo: Te Reo Māori uses only a e h i k m n o p r t u w (+ macrons; ng/wh digraphs) and NEVER b c d f j l q s v x y z, so a lone title carrying any of those is English → it STAYS the English title with NO invented Te Reo (round-76 "only ship what's real"). MEASURED + VALIDATED against the human gold (`outputs/_probe_lonetitle.cjs` runs the real engine): of 40 single-title comparison-set modules ALL have English lone titles the human keeps as English (slot-1 match 5→7 in the 10-module sample; ENGC102 "Communication|Keeping it real"→"Keeping it real", ENGS302 "Te Ara Hou|Short Film Studies"→"Short Film Studies"); OSAI301 (Māori lone title) STILL promotes byte-identical (English from Course). 0 regressions. `LONETITLE_OFF` restores the always-promote behaviour.
- **(2) OVERVIEW DUP-HEADING DE-DUP (data `body_region.lesson_title_dedup.overview`; env `OVDEDUP_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — WT L57 `[H1] Keeping it real` in `[MODULE INTRODUCTION]` (on the overview page); human overview drops it (the title is in the header `<h1>`); Claude leaked `<h3>Keeping it real</h3>`. ROOT CAUSE — the lesson-title de-dup (ContentConverter) was DISABLED on the overview page (`#pageLessonTitle = page.isOverview ? "" : …`), so the first body heading was never compared to the title. (Bug 1 compounded it: the header title was the wrong "Communication", so even an enabled de-dup wouldn't have matched.) FIX — on the overview, de-dup the first body heading against the module English title (`#pageEnglishTitle`), exactly as a lesson page de-dups against its lesson title; EXACT folded match only. MEASURED (`outputs/_measure_videocaption_introdup.py`): the human KEEPS the dup in 0 cases — it is always dropped. `OVDEDUP_OFF` reverts to the disabled-on-overview behaviour.
- **(3) VIDEO-TITLE + PAREN LEAK (data `elements.video_embed_title_drop` + `elements.media_url_paren_strip`; env `VIDTITLE_OFF` / `MEDIAPAREN_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — WT L61-63 `[video] Nonfiction Text Features` then `https://…32ckikjugdM  )`; human ships ONLY the iframe (the title → acks "Video: …, Non Fiction Text features"); Claude leaked `<p>Nonfiction Text Features</p>` + `<p>)</p>` (and on page 1 `Red Pandas | …` `()`, `PANDA PANTS … ()`). ROOT CAUSE — `#media` rendered the whole `#gatherFollowing` "rest" (the `[video]` element's OWN title line + the URL-line residue) as body. MEASURED (`outputs/_measure_videoleak_overviewdedup.py`): stray-paren `<p>` — Claude **334 occ / 97 pages** vs Human **0 / 2042 pages**. The video TITLE vs genuine PROSE distinction is NOT separable by punctuation (YouTube titles look like sentences), so the DERIVABLE discriminator is: a `[video]` with a BUILT embed drops its OWN title line (`it.blackAfter` — the acks acknowledgement); FOLLOWING separate prose is KEPT (ENGJ402 "Here is an alternative video…") and AUDIO text is always kept (MXFL301 `[audio clip]` dialogue "Hi, I'm John Atkins…" — no external embed). ## 2026-06-22 (round 79) — WHITESPACE-ONLY RED SPAN no longer FRAGMENTS a paragraph (Chris, OSBY201-03 "Banter is") (build 260616.58)

Chris flagged (OSBY201-03 screenshot) that the paragraph `**Banter is** like playful teasing…` was SPLIT into two `<p>` — `<p><b>Banter i</b>s</p>` + `<p>like playful teasing…</p>` — and asked to analyse + fix it for all modules and all similar situations. Root-caused to a writer mis-colouring, measured the whole class, fixed in the docx serialiser behind a data flag + env toggle; every protected gate held-or-improved.

- **WT → human → Claude (OSBY201-03).** The docx paragraph (unzipped `word/document.xml`) is ONE `<w:p>` with 4 runs: `"Banter i"` (bold black) · `"s"` (black, **bold OFF** — the writer's own typo) · `" "` (a single space, coloured **RED `ff0000`**) · `"like playful teasing…"` (black). DocxExtractor serialises it to the block `**Banter i**s🔴[RED TEXT]   [/RED TEXT]🔴like playful teasing…` — the red SPACE becomes a `[RED TEXT]` marker. Human `OSBY201-03.html` L242: `<p>Banter is like playful teasing…</p>` (one paragraph). Claude round-78: `<p><b>Banter i</b>s</p>` + `<p>like playful teasing…</p>` — PageSplitter saw the mid-paragraph red marker as a standalone item and split the block into two black items → two `<p>`.
- **Root cause (`DocxExtractor.#parseParagraph`).** Every merged red-run group is wrapped in the `[RED TEXT]` markers unconditionally — including a group whose entire content is WHITESPACE (a writer who selects a stray space/tab and applies the red tag colour). That empty marker is a spurious mid-paragraph span that fragments the block.
- **Measured the class (`outputs/_measure_redspace.cjs`, runs the real DocxExtractor over the 197-set + OSSC301).** Whitespace-only red spans that sit MID-paragraph (black text on both sides — the fragmenting bug): **349 spans across ~80 modules**; plus **1234** EDGE spans (a whitespace red span at a block's start/end — cosmetic, no split). A red span with ANY non-whitespace content (a real `[tag]`/instruction) is a different case and is untouched.
- **The fix (data `red_runs.collapse_whitespace_only`; env `REDWS_OFF`).** In the red-run merge, when the merged `redText.trim() === ""` the serialiser emits a single plain space instead of the `[RED TEXT]` marker, so the block text stays continuous (`**Banter i**s like playful teasing…`) and renders as ONE `<p>`. SCOPED to pure whitespace — `trim()` non-empty (a tag, an instruction, any visible red text) always keeps the marker, so the strip can NEVER drop a tag. `REDWS_OFF` reverts to the round-78 split.

## 2026-06-22 (round 78) — ACTIVITY CLOSE-ON-[H3]: a writer [H3] section heading closes the activity CONTAINER, not just the interactive (Chris, OSBY201-03) (build 260616.57)

Follow-up to round 77. Chris flagged (OSBY201-03 screenshot) that even after the shapeHover interactive correctly terminates, the `[H3] The 'banter' trap` + body + Good-banter table were still rendered INSIDE the `<div class="activity" number="3B">` container — the writer DID tag `[Activity 3B] S.A.F.E`, but the `[H3]` is a NEW top-level section that should end the activity container too. Chris asked specifically for a ROBUST rule that recognises the hierarchy change marking where an activity finishes and top-level content resumes. Measured the class corpus-wide first; the fix is a one-value data change behind an env toggle; every protected gate held-or-improved (compare_structure +81).

- **WT → human → Claude (OSBY201-03, Lesson 3).** WT (`OSBY201 Writers Template_parsed.txt`): `[H2] Lesson 3` → `[H3] Kind words are taonga` → `[activity 3A]` → `[Activity 3B] S.A.F.E` → (S.A.F.E body/video/shapeHover) → `[H3] The 'banter' trap` → `[body]` + Good-banter TABLE → `[Activity 3B] Good banter` → `[H3] Be a kindness influencer!` → `[Activity 3C]` → `[H3] Extra resources`. So within the lesson, the sections are all `[H3]` interspersed with `[Activity N]` — the banter `[H3]` is a PEER section heading, a sibling of the activity. Human `OSBY201-03.html`: renders every section as a top-level `<h3>` (it dropped the S.A.F.E activity entirely via unrecorded feedback). Claude round-77: the activity 3B container (correct from the WT) stayed OPEN across the banter `[H3]` + body + table until the next `[Activity 3B]` tag closed it — so the banter rendered INSIDE activity 3B, and one level too deep (`<h4>`).
- **Root cause (`ContentConverter.ConvertPage#autoClose`).** The activity auto-close fires before a heading whose RENDERED level ≤ `activity_close_before.rendered_heading_max` (3) AND after the activity has content. `renderedHeading = writer-H-digit + body_shift(1)`, so a writer `[H3]` renders 4 > 3 and slipped past — only `[H1]`/`[H2]` (render ≤3) closed an activity, and `[H2]` is a lesson boundary handled separately, so in practice a `[H3]` SECTION heading never closed an activity. The activity therefore swallowed everything up to the next `[Activity]`/section-marker/page-boundary.
- **Measured the class (`outputs/_probe_activity_heading.cjs`, runs the real pipeline over the 197-set + OSSC301).** The FIRST top-level heading appearing after an `[Activity]`'s content (skipping widget-bundle-consumed items — those a widget owns), by LOGICAL level: **[H3] ×469** (77% with a NEW `[Activity]` following — a section break), **[H4] ×84**, **[H5] ×21**, [H2] ×0 (a lesson boundary, never reached). So `[H3]` is the section-break level; `[H4]`/`[H5]` are activity SUB-headings the human keeps inside ("Answers", "Questions", "Your Turn", "Checklist" — verified). Human-side cross-check (`outputs/_measure_activity_toplevel_heading.py`): of 12,341 human activities, only 12% hold a top-level post-content heading and those are predominantly the `[H4]`/`[H5]` sub-heading form.
- **The fix (data `container_auto_close.activity_close_before.rendered_heading_max` 3 → 4 + `…_legacy:3`; env `ACTHEAD_OFF`).** Raising the ceiling to 4 means the auto-close now fires on `renderedHeading ≤ 4` = LOGICAL `[H1]`/`[H2]`/`[H3]` (section level), and KEEPS `[H4]`/`[H5]` (render 5 > 4 — sub-headings) inside. The round-43 title protection (`heading_closes_only_after_content`) is unchanged, so a `[H3]` activity TITLE right after the opener still stays inside; only a `[H3]` AFTER the activity has content closes it. Robust to the content that follows (body/table/video/widget/new-activity all then render top-level). `ACTHEAD_OFF` reverts to the legacy ceiling (3). BONUS: once the banter is a top-level section heading (no longer nested in the activity), the heading re-leveller ranks it correctly as `<h3>` (matching the human) — resolving the round-77 `<h4>`-vs-`<h3>` note as a side effect.

**PROTECTED gates (full 197-set + OSSC301 regen, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1024 pages / 198 dirs; A/B vs `ACTHEAD_OFF` = the round-77 baseline):** compare_structure **exact 4308 → 4389 (+81 — IMPROVED)** / EXTRA 111 — HELD / missing 192 — HELD (section content moved OUT of activities now matches the human's top-level wrapper chain); **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD 47.5 → 47.6%** (pages ≥50% **399 — HELD**; the round-77 marginal `<h4>` page recovers to `<h3>`); **body_compare ANY 142 → 141 — IMPROVED** (OVER-CAPTURE 29 → 28); structural-clean **984/1024 = 96.1% — HELD**, literal-`[tag]` leak **127 — HELD**; JS regression **0 / 9557 (100%) — HELD**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0 — HELD**; speechBubble **defect 0 — HELD**. No protected gate regressed. New env toggle `ACTHEAD_OFF` + data `rendered_heading_max_legacy`. A/B-verified: `ACTHEAD_OFF` puts the OSBY201-03 banter back inside activity 3B byte-for-byte. Tools: `outputs/_probe_activity_heading.cjs`, `outputs/_measure_activity_toplevel_heading.py`.

## 2026-06-21 (round 77) — LONE SECTION-BREAK HEADING: a heading_is_terminator:false widget no longer swallows a NEW SECTION heading (Chris, OSBY201-03 shapeHover) (build 260616.56)

Chris flagged (OSBY201-03 screenshot) that the `[shape hover with arrows]` interactive over-captured: it correctly grabbed the four S.A.F.E shape labels but then kept swallowing the `[H3] The 'banter' trap` heading, its body, and the Good-banter table — content the human renders as a SEPARATE section outside the widget. Chris's hypothesis: a single heading followed by a body is a new section, whereas multiple headings in close proximity belong to the interactive — and warned to protect the "marker → title → body → widget-content" case. Measured the whole class corpus-wide first (the mandate); the measurement validated BOTH hypotheses and surfaced a third exclusion (flipCard fronts) the data demanded. Chris greenlit the general rule and the one skeleton trade.

- **WT → human → Claude (OSBY201-03).** Raw WT `OSBY201 Writers Template_parsed.txt` L410-416: `A [shape hover with arrows] when each letter is clicked the text appears in the centre` → (the S/F/A/E shapes + labels *Step away/Feel your feelings/Ask a trusted adult/Ease back in* are floating Word text-boxes, so they reach the engine as black members) → `[H3] The 'banter' trap` → `[body] It is fun to joke around…` → a `Good banter ║ Not Banter` TABLE → `[Activity 3B]`. Human `OSBY201-03.html`: `<div class="shapeHover" layout="clockwise">` CLOSES after the four `<p>` labels; `<h3>The 'banter' trap</h3>` + body + table are a separate section (L239+). Claude round-76: the shapeHover placeholder swallowed the four labels (correct) AND the `[H3]`/body/table (wrong).
- **Root cause (`InteractiveScanner.#swallowMembers`).** shapeHover's bank entry is `heading_is_terminator:false` + `uses_data_table:true`. The round-72 table-section-break rule (`heading_terminates_after_table`) only fires once `bundle.tables.length > 0`; here the `[H3]` arrives BEFORE the Good-banter table (the shapeHover's content is floating black labels, not a table yet), so that rule is inert and the `heading_is_terminator:false` flag lets the heading be swallowed.
- **Measured the class (`outputs/_probe_heading_swallow.cjs` runs the real scanner over the 197-set + OSSC301; `outputs/_measure_widget_internal_heading.py` over the 4,345-file human library).** (1) The 8 `heading_is_terminator:false` widgets DO legitimately hold internal headings in the human builds — accordion 99.8%, memoryGame 95.2%, **shapeHover 69.1%**, tabs 57.7%, flipCard 53.4% — so a blanket flag-flip is unsafe (it would cut an accordion at its first panel). But those internal labels are NEVER standalone `[H#]` tags (they are table cells or promoted plain text / `[data marker]`/`[story heading]`/`[shape n]`). (2) Splitting the swallowed standalone heading TAGS three ways: **LEAD 248** (heading BEFORE any content = widget title — Chris's danger case), **AFTER_CLUSTER 257** (≥2 headings in the bundle = internal panels, e.g. accordion 'Drafting/Revising/Editing/Publishing'), **AFTER_LONE 73** (single heading after content = section-break candidate). The lone bucket by what FOLLOWS: body 38 / image 16 / END 11 / video 3 / table 1 / list 1. VERIFIED vs human: section-break (rendered OUTSIDE) across shapeHover (OSBY201/OSGM401), accordion (CEDW501/XGF9001/MXFL301), flipCard (ENGJ301/EXPFUN06/MXDB302); INTERNAL (kept inside) = the `follow=image` flipCard FRONTS (OSAI501) + the clusters.
- **The fix (data `_meta.member_rule.lone_heading_section_break` + `lone_heading_follow_section_tags`; env `LONEHEAD_OFF`).** A new terminator in `#swallowMembers`, scoped to `headingTerminates===false` widgets: a standalone `[H2]-[H5]` terminates the bundle when (1) the widget already captured ≥1 GENUINE content member (black/table/image/video/face — NOT the LEAD title), (2) it is LONE — no sibling `[H2]-[H5]` between it and the bundle's next ABSOLUTE terminator (not a panel cluster), AND (3) it is FOLLOWED BY ordinary section content (`[body]`/`[video]`/`[audio]`/table/list — NOT an `[image]` front, NOT widget sub-content). The three exclusions (LEAD title / heading CLUSTER / `follow=image` front) keep every legitimate internal heading. DISTINCT from `heading_terminates_after_table` (that needs a captured TABLE; this fires when the captured content is floating black members/images with no table yet). A/B verified: `LONEHEAD_OFF` reverts OSBY201-03 to the swallowed banter section byte-for-byte.

**PROTECTED gates — A/B-isolated on the current corpus (regen the 28 rule-firing modules `LONEHEAD_OFF` → gate → ON → gate; the other 196 are flag-inert; full corpus mtime-verified 0 stale / 1024 pages / 198 dirs) — Chris GREENLIT the one skeleton trade:** compare_structure **exact 4278 → 4308 (+30 — IMPROVED)** / EXTRA 111 — HELD / missing 192 — HELD (content moved out of placeholders now text-matches the human's free body with the right wrapper chain); **body_compare ANY 145 → 142 — IMPROVED** (OVER-CAPTURE 33 → 29, RUNAWAY 5 → 4 — the gate that directly measures this bug; EMPTY 110 → 112 is the round-72-style placeholder-emptier text-metric artifact); structural-clean **984/1024 = 96.1% — HELD**, literal-`[tag]` leak **127 — HELD**; JS regression **0 / 9557 (100%) — HELD**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0 — HELD**; speechBubble **defect 0 — HELD** (OSBY201 builds 4 bubbles); **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD 47.6 → 47.5%** (pages ≥50% **400 → 399, −1** — one marginal page tips under 50% because correctly-exposed content is now scaffold-visible and the banter heading re-levels to `<h4>` vs the human's `<h3>`; **greenlit**, same shape as the round-73/74 trades; OSBY201-03 itself improved). New data flag `member_rule.lone_heading_section_break` + env `LONEHEAD_OFF` A/B. Tools: `outputs/_probe_heading_swallow.cjs`, `outputs/_measure_widget_internal_heading.py`, `outputs/_measure_heading_swallow_RESULTS.md`.

## 2026-06-21 (round 75) — OSBY201-03 fixes (Chris): duplicate lesson title + single-bracket inline trigger; issue-3 sketcher-activity declined as non-derivable (build 260616.54)

Chris reviewed OSBY201-3.0 against the human gold and flagged three issues. Chris's governing instruction this round (and going forward): **only add behaviour when the raw Writers Template actually carries the tag/info to derive it from** — the converter must reproduce the human from the WT + Media List alone, never from the human HTML.

- **(1) LESSON-TITLE DE-DUP, prefix-tolerant compare (issue 1; data `body_region.lesson_title_dedup.strip_lesson_prefix`; env `LESSONPFX_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — WT L363 `🔴[H2]🔴*Lesson 3: Be kind online*`; human `OSBY201-03.html` shows the title ONCE in the header `<h1>Be kind online</h1>` and NO body lesson heading; Claude round-74 emitted BOTH the header AND a body `<h3><i>Lesson 3: Be kind online</i></h3>`. ROOT CAUSE — the round-22 lesson-title de-dup already strips a leading "Lesson N:" and compares to the header title, BUT the writer wrapped this heading WHOLE in `*italic*`, so `raw` = `"*Lesson 3: …"` starts with `*` not `lesson`; the `^lesson` strip missed, the prefix survived into the compare text, and `"Lesson 3: Be kind online" ≠ "Be kind online"` → never de-duped. MEASURED (`outputs/`): **310** Claude pages carry a body `Lesson N:` heading; the human keeps only **7**. FIX — strip a leading `Lesson N:` from BOTH sides of the de-dup COMPARE only (rendering of any genuinely-kept heading is unchanged; the page title is already prefix-free in the header). RESULT — body `Lesson N:` headings **310→35** (275 de-duped to match the human; the 35 kept are legit non-title-matches, conservatively preserved).
- **(2) SINGLE-BRACKET INLINE TRIGGER → infoTrigger weave (issue 2; data `elements.info_trigger_inline`; env `INFOTRIG_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — WT L371 `Being an online kaitiaki 🔴[audio trigger kai-ti-a-ki]🔴means making sure … treasure or taonga🔴[audio trigger ta-o-nga]🔴that boosts …`; human L55 `Being an online <span class="infoTrigger" info="kai-ti-a-ki">kaitiaki</span> means … treasure or <span class="infoTrigger" info="ta-o-nga">taonga</span> that boosts …` (ONE `<p>`, two pronunciation tooltips); Claude round-74 BROKE it into three `<p>` and DROPPED the def. ROOT CAUSE — the marker carries its DEFINITION INSIDE its own SELF-CLOSED red span (the `[…]` opens AND closes in the one marker), so there is NO separate `]` closer item; the existing `hasCloser` split-bracket stitch (InteractiveScanner) never fired and fell to the bare-marker guard, re-exposing `blackAfter` as a fresh `<p>`. Also found: the sentinel the round-40 design relies on (`U+E000 DEF U+E001`, consumed by `#inlineMarkup`) was **never inserted anywhere** in the engine — the stitch only re-joined plain text, which is why the broader split-bracket class leaks the literal `[… trigger: def]` bracket (human **803** infoTrigger spans in the comparison set vs Claude **42** — a 761-span gap across 108 modules; `outputs/_measure_infotrigger.py`). FIX (scoped to the clean self-closed form) — detect the self-closed marker, recover the def in ORIGINAL case from the marker text after `trigger` (`parse.remainders` is folded-lowercase/mangled, e.g. `"info : plant eating"`, so unusable for `info=`), insert the sentinel directly after the preceding anchor word (walk back past already-consumed empties so back-to-back triggers each anchor on their own word), and re-join the continuation → `#inlineMarkup` builds the `<span class="infoTrigger">`. CONSERVATIVE — fires only on a self-closed marker WITH a non-empty def AND a preceding anchor; the SPLIT-bracket form (`[hover trigger DEF` + a separate `]`, the 761-span ENGJ302/MXDI301 leak class) is a messier tokenisation **left for a focused follow-up round**. RESULT — infoTrigger spans **42→57**; OSBY201-03's paragraph now BYTE-matches the human; the existing split-bracket acronym span (`info="Each letter…"`) and ENGJ302 (2→4) are unaffected/improved.
- **(3) SKETCHER → ACTIVITY WRAPPER — DECLINED, non-derivable (issue 3).** TRIANGULATION — WT L375-381: `[body] Circle or tick…` → bare `[sketcher] [image] <drive url>` (NO activity label) → `[body] In the activity below…` → `[activity 3A] Kind words are gems`. Human wraps the bare sketcher in `<div class="activity interactive" number="3A"><h3>Wellbeing kind words</h3>…` and RENUMBERS everything after it (the WT's `[activity 3A]` gems → human 3B, …3E). Two parts are NOT in the WT: (a) the activity TITLE **"Wellbeing kind words"** appears NOWHERE in the WT (`grep` confirmed — it is the human's editorial coinage, loosely echoing the body phrase "areas of *wellbeing kind words*"); (b) the human's sequential A-E numbering CONFLICTS with the WT's own explicit `[activity 3A/3B/3B/3C]` labels. Per Chris's derivability mandate, fabricating a title or overriding the writer's labels would be guessing from the human HTML, not deriving from the WT — so this is left as Decision-Framework class **C** (editorial), recorded not shipped. ## 2026-06-21 (round 74) — Hyperlink-phrase weave (OSBY201-02 issue 3) + media-match by iStock id (Chris) (build 260616.53)

Chris greenlit implementing the deferred OSBY201-02 issue 3 (external link) "as the best solution you deem necessary, by researching how the human interpreted links across the corpus", and fix 2 (media-match by item id). Two general, data-flagged, env-reversible changes; Chris greenlit the one marginal skeleton trade.

- **(1) HYPERLINK-PHRASE WEAVE (data `elements.hyperlink_weave`; env `LINKWEAVE_OFF`).** TRIANGULATION — OSBY201-02 WT line 286 `• __Complete an online contact form__ [LINK: https://report.netsafe.org.nz/hc/en-au/requests/new]  [external link]`. The phrase is a REAL docx `w:hyperlink` (verified in `word/document.xml`: `<w:hyperlink r:id="rId31">Complete an online contact form</w:hyperlink>`, not bold); DocxExtractor already captured it as `block.links {text,target}`. HUMAN: `<li><a href="…/requests/new" target="_blank">Complete an online contact form</a></li>` — the phrase IS the link, the `[external link]` tag is just an "opens externally" modifier. CLAUDE was: `<li>Complete an online contact form</li>` (plain) + a SEPARATE `<p><a href="…">…/requests/new</a></p>` (the `[external link]` tag emitting the bare URL via `#inline`). MEASURED corpus-wide (`outputs/_measure_phraselink.py`): human body has **1011** descriptive phrase-links vs Claude **131** — an **880-link gap across 90 modules**. FIX: `#inlineMarkup` weaves each `block.links` entry onto the FIRST occurrence of its descriptive text as `<a href=target>phrase</a>` (conservative: exact text, skip if the link text IS a URL or already inside an `<a>`); threaded `block.links` through `#renderBlackText` at the body-text call sites; `#inline` now SUPPRESSES its bare-URL `<p>` when the block carries a descriptive-phrase hyperlink (the phrase is rendered as the link by the black item). ROOT CAUSE of the lost link: `#coalesceBlackRuns` merged consecutive bullets' TEXT but dropped the 2nd block's LINKS — now the merged item carries every line's links (shallow-copy the surviving block, extend its `links`). RESULT: descriptive phrase-links **131→711** (+580 now match the human; gap 880→300); OSBY201-02 renders identically to the human, bare-URL duplicate gone.
- **(2) MEDIA-MATCH BY ID (data `Comment_Authors.media_match.id_match`; env `MEDIAMATCH_OFF`).** Round 73's media-match keyed only on the EXACT row URL, so a comment reached a body element ONLY where the writer pasted the same live `<a href>` — but most images are Mode-P PLACEHOLDERS with no live link (the URL survives only as the iStock id). New `#mediaKeys(url)` broadens the match key to the exact URL PLUS the extracted iStock reference number (gm-form `gm1382010801` OR CDN `/id/NNN` form) AND the YouTube video id; both the comment's `rowUrl` and the body image block's `links[].target` are reduced to these keys and matched. id-correspondence verified 100% body↔media-list (MXDI202 18/18, MXFL301 76/76, BLL210 1/1). Conservative — only a shared reference NUMBER matches (no fuzzy/title match). Now surfaces actionable placeholder-image comments the URL match missed (e.g. MXDI202 "Nadia Stanton: Replace images with iStock"). `id_match:false` reverts to exact-URL-only.

The six whitelisted parties resolve cleanly with NO missed variants among the other 56 — exact stored forms: `Kate.Scanlon`, `Nadia Stanton`, `caroline schwer`, `simon vita`, `amanda griffiths`, `Creative Services` (matching is case-insensitive, dot/space-equivalent, `[N]`-stripping, order-tolerant). **8188** of 9391 are whitelisted; ALL are range-anchored. `outputs/_inspect_comment_anchor.py` + per-author sampling surfaced the key finding: **85% (Nadia, 6962) are copyright/licensing notes on the MEDIA LIST table**, not the lesson body — 272 of 376 templates are combined "Writers Template + Media List" files where that table isn't body content. So body-anchoring captures the DESIGNER INSTRUCTIONS (Creative Services / Caroline / Simon / Amanda), not the copyright layer. Chris confirmed all six + a content filter.
- **(1) Capture + anchor (`DocxExtractor`).** New `#parseComments(word/comments.xml)` → `id → {author,text}`; `#parseDocument` scans each top-level chunk for `w:commentRangeStart` and attaches the comment to that block (a comment whose anchor sits in an EMPTY/image paragraph that gets dropped is CARRIED to the next kept block — the nearest real element). Blocks flow `→ PageSplitter.BuildItemStream` (every item already carries `.block`) `→ ContentConverter`.
- **(2) Whitelist + render + omit (`ContentConverter`, data `Comment_Authors.json`).** `#commentNotes` matches the author to the whitelist (`#commentAuthorDisplay`), drops non-whitelisted, and emits `<p class="cv2-comment" style="color: red">{author}: {text}</p>` JUST BEFORE the anchored element as a direct child of the body region (`breakRow()` + `parts.push`). `content_filter` (`#commentIsOmittable`) OMITS a comment that matches the non-actionable boilerplate regex (copyright / permission / "used in online learning within the exception for education" / attribution / © / "link only") AND carries no action_keep signal (so a mixed "Replace with iStock. Used with permission." stays). Master `Comment_Authors.enabled` + env `COMMENTS_OFF`. Measured (`outputs/_measure_comment_content.py`): 8188 whitelisted → ~6800 omitted as commentary → **107 surfaced** (Creative Services / Caroline / Amanda / Simon — the actionable designer instructions), across 44 modules.
- **(3) Part B — reposition embedded instructions (Chris greenlit the gate trade).** A writer instruction rendered INSIDE an un-built interactive placeholder (the OSAI201-01 1B sketcher "CS:" notes) now moves to JUST BEFORE the dashed box (`interactive_placeholder.instructions_before` + env `NOTEBEFORE_OFF`). An interactive whose ONLY rendered content is the instruction renders as just the note (no empty box — the empty-box guard, parity with the round-43 empty-bundle guard). Notes already AFTER an element stay put.
- **(4) Note gate-exclusion cleanup.** ALL converter notes now carry a class — `cv2-note` (CS / RED FLAG retained instructions) and `cv2-comment` (Word comments). The skeleton (`_structural_skeleton.py`) and structural-defect audit (`_structural_defect_audit.py`) now SKIP these classes, and the text gates (`compare_structure` / `full_compare` / `body_compare`) exclude the comment-author prefixes — full parity with the existing `cs `/`red flag` text exclusion. This is the correct measurement (the human strips EVERY note) and it REVEALS that the structural-defect baseline was inflated by note-bracket false-positives: the CS/RED FLAG notes carry the writer's raw `[tag]` references, which were never real content leaks.

Both are CONSERVATIVE — never half-build → keep the orange placeholder on any unexpected shape (the project's prime directive).

A widget BUILD is **SCAFFOLD-neutral** by design (the skeleton collapses every widget — placeholder or built — to one position marker), so the value lands in RAW fidelity (real, functional widgets) not the primary metric.
